Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ for an unknown velocity field $u(x,t) = (u_1, u_2, u_3) : \mathbb{R}^3 	imes [0,\infty) 	o \mathbb{R}^3$ and pressure $p(x,t) : \mathbb{R}^3 	imes [0,\infty) 	o \mathbb{R}$:

$$\partial_t u_i + \sum_{j=1}^{3} u_j \, \partial_{x_j} u_i = 
u \, \Delta u_i - \partial_{x_i} p, \qquad i = 1,2,3,$$
$$
abla \cdot u = \sum_{j=1}^{3} \partial_{x_j} u_j = 0,$$

where $
u > 0$ is the kinematic viscosity and external forces are taken to be zero. Let the initial data $u_0 : \mathbb{R}^3 	o \mathbb{R}^3$ be a divergence-free, $C^\infty$ vector field on $\mathbb{R}^3$ satisfying, for every multi-index $\alpha$ and every integer $K \geq 0$, the decay estimate

$$|\partial^\alpha u_0(x)| \leq C_{\alpha, K} \, (1 + |x|)^{-K}, \qquad x \in \mathbb{R}^3,$$

for suitable constants $C_{\alpha,K}$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every such initial datum $u_0$, there exist smooth functions $u \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3 	imes [0,\infty); \mathbb{R}^3)$ and $p \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3 	imes [0,\infty); \mathbb{R})$ satisfying the equations above with $u(\cdot, 0) = u_0$ and with bounded total kinetic energy,

$$\sup_{t \geq 0} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |u(x,t)|^2 \, dx < \infty.$$

More generally, determine the conditions on the initial data under which globally defined smooth solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations exist.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The global existence and smoothness of solutions to the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations is one of the seven Clay Millennium Prize Problems and remains unresolved as of 2026. No accepted proof or disproof exists; only partial results (e.g., local-in-time smooth solutions, global weak Leray–Hopf solutions, conditional regularity criteria, and recent non-uniqueness results for weak solutions) are known.

Let Ω ⊂ R^3 be a bounded Lipschitz domain representing the reference configuration of an elastic crystal, and let ψ : M^{3×3} × R → R ∪ {+∞} be a free-energy density depending on the deformation gradient A ∈ M^{3×3} and the temperature θ > 0, with ψ(·,θ) typically possessing multiple energy wells reflecting crystallographic symmetry (so that ψ(·,θ) is not quasiconvex in general). For a (relatively open) portion ∂Ω_1 ⊂ ∂Ω of the boundary and a map g : ∂Ω_1 → R^3, define the admissible set
   A = { y ∈ W^{1,1}(Ω; R^3) : y|_{∂Ω_1} = g }
and the energy functional
   I_θ(y) = ∫_Ω ψ(Dy(x), θ) dx.

(a) Characterize those pairs (∂Ω_1, g) for which the infimum of I_θ over A is attained by some y ∈ A.

(b) Characterize those pairs (∂Ω_1, g) for which the infimum is not attained (so that minimizing sequences develop finer and finer microstructure).

(c) In a suitable precise sense (e.g. with respect to natural topologies or measures on the data (∂Ω_1, g)), determine whether non-attainment associated with the formation of microstructure is generic or exceptional.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

This is a well-known open problem in the variational theory of nonlinear elasticity concerning attainment of energy minima for non-quasiconvex multi-well energies. While partial results exist for specific boundary data lying inside or on the boundary of the quasiconvex hull of the energy wells (e.g., rigidity results of Ball–James, Dolzmann–Müller, Kirchheim, and others giving sufficient conditions for attainment or non-attainment), no general characterization of the data (∂Ω_1, g) is known, and the generic vs. exceptional question for non-attainment remains unresolved.

[{"title": "Some open problems in elasticity", "url": "https://zbmath.org/1820121", "snippet": "Problem 17 asks to characterize boundary data for which the minimum of the crystal energy is attained, and asks whether non-attainment is generic or exceptional.", "claim": "The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem."}]

Let $\Omega_h = \omega \times (-h/2, h/2) \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ for a bounded Lipschitz domain $\omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (or, for rods, let $\Omega_h$ be a thin tube of cross-sectional diameter $h$ around a smooth curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$). Consider three-dimensional hyperelastic bodies governed by a stored-energy functional
$$E_h(y) = \int_{\Omega_h} W(\nabla y(x))\, dx - \int_{\Omega_h} f_h \cdot y\, dx - \int_{\partial_N \Omega_h} g_h \cdot y\, dS,$$
where $W : \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3} \to [0,\infty]$ is a frame-indifferent stored-energy density satisfying $W(R) = 0$ for $R \in SO(3)$, $W(F) \ge c\,\mathrm{dist}^2(F, SO(3))$, and is suitably regular near $SO(3)$; deformations $y : \Omega_h \to \mathbb{R}^3$ are subject to mixed Dirichlet/Neumann boundary conditions on the lateral and end (or top/bottom) faces of $\Omega_h$, and $f_h, g_h$ are applied body and surface loads.

(a) Rigorously derive one-dimensional rod models and two-dimensional plate and shell models as the limits of $E_h$ when the thickness parameter $h \to 0$, for all natural scalings of the elastic energy (e.g., $h^\beta$-scalings yielding stretching, von Kármán, linearized von Kármán, bending, and constrained membrane regimes).

(b) Prove that, for each such regime, the sets of (approximate) minimizers and, more generally, solution sets of the corresponding three-dimensional boundary value problems converge — in a suitable topology after rescaling to a fixed reference domain — to the solution sets of the limit lower-dimensional models, with quantitative error estimates in $h$.

(c) Extend these convergence and error results to handle:
  (i) general dead and live loads and mixed boundary conditions;
  (ii) buckling phenomena, including bifurcation diagrams of the 3D problem versus those of the reduced model;
  (iii) boundary layers near lateral boundaries and points of boundary-condition change.

Give a unified rigorous theory establishing such derivations together with explicit convergence and error estimates that cover (a), (b), and (c).

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Substantial progress has been made on this program. Via Γ-convergence, a complete hierarchy of plate models (membrane, von Kármán, linearized von Kármán, bending/Kirchhoff) has been rigorously derived from 3D nonlinear elasticity (Friesecke–James–Müller and successors), as well as analogous theories for rods (including bending–torsion, curved, and incompressible rods) and shells (nonlinear bending shells, von Kármán shells, homogenized shells). However, a unified theory delivering quantitative error estimates, convergence of full solution sets (not just minimizers) under general loads and mixed boundary conditions, rigorous treatment of buckling/bifurcation, and complete boundary-layer analysis remains incomplete; many of these aspects are still active research problems.

For each integer d ≥ 1 and integer r ≥ 1, let F_{d,r} denote the class of real-valued functions f on the unit cube [0,1]^d that are r times continuously differentiable and satisfy

  ‖∂^{|α|} f / ∂x^α‖_∞ ≤ 1  for every multi-index α = (α_1,…,α_d) ∈ ℤ_{≥0}^d with |α| = α_1+…+α_d ≤ r.

For ε ∈ (0,1), let n(ε,d,r) denote the minimal number N such that there exists an algorithm using N function values of f which, for every f ∈ F_{d,r}, approximates the integral ∫_{[0,1]^d} f(x) dx with worst-case error at most ε · ‖f‖ (relative error, with a suitable normalization of the class).

Let r : ℕ → ℕ be a function such that the ratio d / r(d) remains bounded as d → ∞. Prove or disprove the following statement: the quantity n(ε,d,r(d)) cannot be bounded above by any polynomial in d and ε^{-1}; that is, multivariate integration over the family of classes F_{d,r(d)} is intractable.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Hinrichs, Novak, Ullrich and Woźniakowski (2014, "The curse of dimensionality for numerical integration of smooth functions", Math. Comp.; and Part II) proved the curse of dimensionality for multivariate integration on the classes F_{d,r}: the minimal number of function values needed to reach error ε is at least c_r(1+γ_r)^d. In particular this rules out any polynomial bound in d and ε^{-1} when d/r(d) stays bounded, settling the question in the affirmative (the problem is indeed intractable).

Consider numerical integration over the unit cube $[0,1]^d$ in the weighted Sobolev reproducing-kernel Hilbert space $H(K_{d,\gamma})$ with kernel
$$K_{d,\gamma}(x,t) = \prod_{j=1}^{d}\bigl(1+\gamma_j\,\min(x_j,t_j)\bigr), \qquad x,t\in[0,1]^d,$$
where $\gamma = (\gamma_j)_{j\ge 1}$ is a fixed sequence of positive nonincreasing weights with $\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\gamma_j<\infty$. For a quadrature rule $Q_{n,d}(f)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i f(x^{(i)})$ using $n$ function evaluations, let
$$e(n,d) = \inf_{Q_{n,d}}\sup_{\|f\|_{H(K_{d,\gamma})}\le 1}\bigl|I_d(f)-Q_{n,d}(f)\bigr|,\qquad I_d(f)=\int_{[0,1]^d}f(x)\,dx,$$
and $e(0,d)=\sup_{\|f\|\le 1}|I_d(f)|$ be the initial error. The problem is called strongly tractable if there exist constants $C,p>0$ such that for every $d\ge 1$ and every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,
$$\min\{n : e(n,d)\le \varepsilon\, e(0,d)\}\le C\,\varepsilon^{-p}.$$
The exponent of strong tractability $p^{*}=p^{*}(\gamma)$ is the infimum of all $p$ for which such a bound holds. Define
$$s_\gamma = \inf\Bigl\{s>0 : \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\gamma_j^{\,s}<\infty\Bigr\}.$$
Is it true that
$$p^{*}(\gamma) = \max\bigl(1,\,2\,s_\gamma\bigr)\,?$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

A literature search reveals related work by Sloan–Woźniakowski and by Hickernell–Woźniakowski establishing that the strong-tractability exponent lies between 1 and 2 under summability of the weights, and constructive QMC results achieving the upper bound. However, no source clearly confirms the exact identity $p^{*}=\max(1,2s_\gamma)$ for the Sobolev kernel $\prod(1+\gamma_j\min(x_j,t_j))$; the precise value of $p^*$ in this generality appears not to be settled.

Let $d\ge 1$ and let $\gamma=(\gamma_j)_{j\ge 1}$ be a sequence of positive nonincreasing weights. For each $d$ define the weighted Sobolev reproducing kernel Hilbert space $H_{d,\gamma}$ on $[0,1]^d$ as the tensor product Hilbert space with reproducing kernel
$$K_{d,\gamma}(x,t)=\prod_{j=1}^d\bigl(1+\gamma_j\min(x_j,t_j)\bigr),\qquad x,t\in[0,1]^d.$$
For $f\in H_{d,\gamma}$ consider the integration problem $I_d(f)=\int_{[0,1]^d} f(x)\,dx$. A randomized algorithm using $n$ function values is a measurable mapping $\omega\mapsto A_{n,\omega}$ where each $A_{n,\omega}(f)$ depends on $n$ values of $f$ at randomly chosen points and the random choice is independent of $f$. The randomized error is
$$e^{\mathrm{ran}}(n,d):=\inf_{A_n}\sup_{\|f\|_{H_{d,\gamma}}\le 1}\Bigl(\mathbb{E}\bigl|I_d(f)-A_n(f)\bigr|^2\Bigr)^{1/2},$$
and the randomized information complexity is $n^{\mathrm{ran}}(\varepsilon,d):=\min\{n: e^{\mathrm{ran}}(n,d)\le\varepsilon\}$. The integration problem is called tractable in the randomized setting if there exist constants $C,p,q\ge 0$ such that
$$n^{\mathrm{ran}}(\varepsilon,d)\le C\,\varepsilon^{-p}\,d^{q}\qquad\text{for all }\varepsilon\in(0,1),\ d\ge 1.$$

Question: Is the condition
$$\limsup_{d\to\infty}\frac{\sum_{j=1}^d \gamma_j^{\,2}}{\ln d}<\infty$$
necessary for tractability of randomized multivariate integration in the spaces $H_{d,\gamma}$?

Consider a polycrystalline metallic film or coating (for example, of tin, zinc, cadmium, or lead) deposited on a conducting substrate and held under ambient or operating conditions of an electrical device. It is empirically observed that such surfaces can spontaneously extrude single‑crystalline filaments ("whiskers") of the same metal, typically a few micrometres in diameter and up to several millimetres in length, which grow from the base over time and can short‑circuit nearby conductors. Compressive in‑plane mechanical stress in the film is known to promote this extrusion, but no single quantitative model accounts for the observed nucleation sites, incubation times, growth rates, crystallographic orientations, and the dependence on temperature, humidity, substrate, grain structure, and applied electric field.

Problem: Formulate and validate a predictive physical mechanism for spontaneous metal whisker growth from a stressed polycrystalline metal surface. Specifically, derive from first principles (e.g., stress‑driven mass transport, grain‑boundary diffusion, recrystallization, oxide‑layer rupture, or electromigration) a model that
(i) predicts the nucleation conditions and density of whiskers as a function of residual stress state, grain microstructure, and surface oxide;
(ii) yields the steady‑state axial growth velocity and final length distribution; and
(iii) reproduces, with no free parameters fit per experiment, the observed dependence of whisker formation on temperature, humidity, substrate composition, plating chemistry, and external electric field.

Let $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a dispersive (Sinai) billiard table: a compact domain whose boundary consists of finitely many smooth strictly convex arcs whose curvature, viewed from inside $Y$, is negative (i.e., the boundary is convex into the table). Consider the associated billiard map $T_Y$ defined on the unit tangent bundle restricted to the boundary, where a point particle moves in straight lines inside $Y$ and reflects elastically off the boundary. For each integer $n \geq 1$, let $f_Y(n)$ denote the number of periodic orbits of $T_Y$ whose period (number of collisions in one cycle) is at most $n$.

Determine whether the limit
$$h \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\log f_Y(n)}{n}$$
exists for every dispersive billiard table $Y$.

Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a rational polygon, i.e. a polygon all of whose interior angles are rational multiples of $\pi$. Consider the billiard flow on $P$ (a point particle moving at unit speed in a straight line in the interior, reflecting elastically off the sides). A periodic billiard trajectory in $P$ belongs to a maximal parallel family of periodic trajectories of the same length, called a "periodic band" (or cylinder); its length is the common length of the trajectories in the family. For $\ell>0$, let $f_P(\ell)$ denote the number of periodic bands of $P$ of length at most $\ell$.

It is known that there exist constants $0<c_*(P)\le c^*(P)<\infty$ such that
$$c_*(P)\,\ell^2 \;\le\; f_P(\ell)\;\le\; c^*(P)\,\ell^2$$
for all sufficiently large $\ell$.

Problem: Give effective estimates (explicit upper and lower bounds, expressible in terms of the combinatorial and metric data of $P$) for the constants $c_*(P)$ and $c^*(P)$.

The existence of the quadratic bounds is due to Masur (upper/lower) and Boshernitzan, but the original proofs are non-effective. Background. In high-energy astrophysics, charged particles in collisionless plasmas (e.g., at supernova-remnant shocks, in relativistic jets, in pulsar wind nebulae, and in magnetic-reconnection regions) are observed to follow nonthermal power-law energy spectra extending to very high energies. The widely accepted mechanism producing these spectra is Fermi acceleration—in particular, diffusive shock acceleration (DSA)—in which a particle gains energy stochastically by repeated scatterings off magnetic inhomogeneities on opposite sides of a shock or by encounters with moving magnetized scatterers.

A fundamental obstacle is that Fermi/DSA acts efficiently only on particles whose energy already exceeds a threshold (the "injection energy") significantly larger than the typical thermal energy of the background plasma: the particle's gyroradius must exceed the shock thickness, and its speed must be sufficient to repeatedly cross the shock. Thermal particles drawn directly from a Maxwellian distribution generally do not satisfy this condition.

Problem (the injection problem). Identify and quantitatively characterize the physical mechanism(s) by which a fraction of thermal particles (electrons and ions) in astrophysical collisionless plasmas are pre-accelerated from thermal energies up to the injection threshold required for Fermi acceleration / diffusive shock acceleration to operate. Specifically:

(a) Determine, from first-principles plasma physics, the process that brings electrons and ions from a thermal Maxwellian distribution to suprathermal energies sufficient for DSA at collisionless shocks of arbitrary obliquity, Mach number, and plasma beta.

(b) Predict the resulting injection efficiency (the fraction of upstream thermal particles that get injected) and the species-dependent injection energy as functions of the upstream plasma and shock parameters.

(c) Show that the predicted injection mechanism is consistent with the observed nonthermal spectra and abundances of cosmic rays and with in-situ spacecraft measurements at heliospheric and planetary shocks.

Let f(x) = x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + ... + a_0 be a monic polynomial of degree n ≥ 2 with complex coefficients, and let ξ_1, ..., ξ_n denote its (not necessarily distinct) zeros. The Weierstrass (Durand–Kerner) iteration is the map W : (ℂ \ Δ)^n → ℂ^n defined componentwise by

  W_i(x_1, ..., x_n) = x_i − f(x_i) / ∏_{j ≠ i} (x_i − x_j),  i = 1, ..., n,

where Δ denotes the diagonal {x : x_i = x_j for some i ≠ j}. Given a starting vector x^{(0)} = (x_1^{(0)}, ..., x_n^{(0)}) ∈ ℂ^n with pairwise distinct entries, the iteration is x^{(k+1)} = W(x^{(k)}) for k ≥ 0.

Problem: Provide sufficient conditions on the starting vector x^{(0)} (formulated in terms of f and the entries x_i^{(0)}) under which the Weierstrass iteration diverges, in the sense that the sequence {x^{(k)}} does not converge to any permutation of (ξ_1, ..., ξ_n) (allowing, e.g., that some component escapes to infinity, or that the sequence is attracted to a periodic orbit disjoint from the root set, or that a collision x_i^{(k)} = x_j^{(k)} occurs). Furthermore, describe (topologically and/or measure-theoretically) the set of all such starting vectors in ℂ^n that satisfy the proposed divergence conditions.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Partial results exist. It is known that the Weierstrass–Durand–Kerner method is not generally convergent: for every degree d ≥ 3 there are open sets of polynomials whose Weierstrass dynamics admit attracting periodic orbits (Reinke–Schleicher–Stoll and others). Some specific divergence sets have been described (e.g., cycles for cubics, two-sided SOR variants), but a complete characterization of sufficient divergence conditions and the resulting set of starting approximations remains open.

Let f(z) = a_n z^n + a_{n-1} z^{n-1} + ... + a_0 be a complex polynomial of degree n >= 2 with pairwise distinct (unknown) zeros. For an n-tuple of pairwise distinct approximations z = (z_1, ..., z_n) in C^n, define the Weierstrass correction at the i-th component by

   W_i(z) = f(z_i) / ( a_n * prod_{j != i} (z_i - z_j) ),    i = 1, ..., n.

The classical Weierstrass (Durand–Kerner) iteration is z_i^{(k+1)} = z_i^{(k)} - W_i(z^{(k)}). Its SOR-like (successive over-relaxation) modification with a real (or complex) acceleration parameter omega is the iteration

   (*)   z_i^{(k+1)} = z_i^{(k)} - omega * W_i(z^{(k)}),    i = 1, ..., n,    k = 0, 1, 2, ...,

provided all components remain pairwise distinct so that W_i is well defined at every step.

Problem. Determine sufficient conditions on the polynomial f, the acceleration parameter omega, and the initial approximation z^{(0)} = (z_1^{(0)}, ..., z_n^{(0)}) under which the iteration (*) diverges, in the sense that the sequence (z^{(k)})_{k >= 0} fails to converge to the n-tuple of zeros of f. Let $f(z) = \prod_{i=1}^n (z - \zeta_i)$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n \ge 2$ with pairwise distinct complex roots $\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_n$. For an initial vector $(x_1^0,\dots,x_n^0) \in \mathbb{C}^n$ of pairwise distinct approximations, consider the generalized Weierstrass (SOR-type) simultaneous iteration
$$x_i^{k+1} \;=\; x_i^k \;-\; h_k \,\frac{f(x_i^k)}{\prod_{j \ne i}(x_i^k - x_j^k)}, \qquad i = 1,\dots,n, \quad k = 0,1,2,\dots,$$
where $h_k \in (0,1]$ is an acceleration (relaxation) parameter that may depend on $k$ and on the current iterate. Setting $h_k \equiv 1$ recovers the classical Weierstrass (Durand–Kerner) method.

Determine a rule for choosing the sequence $\{h_k\} \subset (0,1]$ that (a) guarantees convergence of $(x_1^k,\dots,x_n^k)$ to a permutation of $(\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_n)$ under explicit, computationally verifiable conditions on the initial approximations, and (b) is optimal among all such guaranteed-convergent choices (for instance, maximizes the convergence rate or the size of the admissible region of initial approximations).

Let $f(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n(z-\zeta_i)\in\mathbb{C}[z]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n\ge 2$ with pairwise distinct (unknown) zeros $\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_n\in\mathbb{C}$. For a vector $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n$ with pairwise distinct components, define the Weierstrass correction
$$W_i(x)=\frac{f(x_i)}{\prod_{j\ne i}(x_i-x_j)},\qquad i=1,\dots,n.$$
Fix an integer $R\ge 0$. Consider the higher-order Weierstrass-type iteration of convergence order $R+2$ defined componentwise by
$$x_i^{(k+1)} = x_i^{(k)} - W_i(x^{(k)})\sum_{r=0}^{R}\Bigg(\prod_{s=1}^{r}\sum_{\substack{j=1\\ j\ne i}}^{n}\frac{W_j(x^{(k)})}{x_i^{(k)}-x_j^{(k)}}\Bigg),\qquad i=1,\dots,n,$$
where the empty product (case $r=0$) is interpreted as $1$. (For $R=0$ this reduces to the classical Weierstrass–Dochev method; increasing $R$ yields methods of increasing order $R+2$.)

Question: Is there a subset $E\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ of Lebesgue measure zero such that for every initial vector $x^{(0)}\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus E$ (with pairwise distinct components) the iteration is well-defined for all $k\ge 0$ and converges to a permutation of $(\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_n)$? If yes, characterize the exceptional set $E$ explicitly; if not, identify the locus of initial conditions where the conjectured global convergence fails.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture that the higher-order Weierstrass-type method is globally convergent outside a measure-zero set in $\mathbb{C}^n$ is attributed to Kyurkchiev and Atanassova and has been studied in subsequent works on critical points and divergent starting configurations of these iterations. Available literature (papers on critical points of Kyurkchiev's method, divergent starting points, and recent local/semilocal convergence analyses) addresses partial aspects but does not establish global convergence almost everywhere. No proof of the full conjecture appears in the literature; the problem appears to remain open.

Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ for an unknown velocity field $u:\mathbb{R}^3	imes[0,\infty)	o\mathbb{R}^3$ and pressure $p:\mathbb{R}^3	imes[0,\infty)	o\mathbb{R}$:

$$\partial_t u_i + \sum_{j=1}^{3} u_j\,\partial_{x_j} u_i \;=\; \nu\,\Delta u_i - \partial_{x_i} p, \qquad i=1,2,3,$$

$$\nabla\cdot u \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_{x_j} u_j \;=\; 0,$$

where $\nu>0$ is a fixed viscosity constant. Impose the initial condition $u(x,0)=u_0(x)$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, where $u_0:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$ is a prescribed divergence-free vector field that is $C^\infty$ and satisfies, for every multi-index $\alpha$ and every $K\ge 0$, a decay estimate of the form
$$|\partial^{\alpha} u_0(x)| \;\le\; C_{\alpha,K}\,(1+|x|)^{-K}.$$

Prove one of the following two statements:

(A) (Existence and smoothness) For every such initial datum $u_0$, there exist functions $u\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,\infty);\mathbb{R}^3)$ and $p\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,\infty);\mathbb{R})$ solving the equations above on $\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,\infty)$ with $u(\cdot,0)=u_0$ and satisfying the bounded-energy condition
$$\sup_{t\ge 0}\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |u(x,t)|^2\,dx \;<\;\infty.$$

(B) (Breakdown) There exists an initial datum $u_0$ as above for which no pair $(u,p)$ with the smoothness and bounded-energy properties in (A) solves the equations on $\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,\infty)$.

Let $P_n$ be a finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane. For a pair of points $p, q \in P_n$, define $f(p,q)$ to be the minimum, over all circles $C$ in the plane passing through or containing both $p$ and $q$ (i.e., with $p$ and $q$ in the closed disk bounded by $C$), of the number of points of $P_n$ contained in (the closed disk bounded by) $C$.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $c$ such that for every finite set $P_n$ of $n$ points in the plane, one can find a pair of points $p, q \in P_n$ with
$$f(p,q) \;\ge\; \frac{n}{4} - c\,?$$
Equivalently, prove or disprove that every $n$-point planar set contains two points such that every circle containing both of them encloses at least $n/4 \pm c$ points of the set.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture (attributed to Neumann-Lara and Urrutia) that the optimal constant is $n/4$ remains open. Known lower bounds include $\lceil n/3 \rceil$-type results from Hayward, Rappaport, Wenger and subsequent work; a recent 2019 result by Claverol, Huemer et al. improved this to roughly $n(1/2 - 1/\sqrt{12}) + O(1) \approx n/4.7$, still short of the conjectured $n/4$.

For integers $s, t \geq 2$, the Ramsey number $r(s,t)$ is the smallest positive integer $N$ such that every 2-coloring of the edges of the complete graph $K_N$ with colors red and blue contains either a red clique on $s$ vertices or a blue clique on $t$ vertices. Write $r(n,n)$ for the diagonal Ramsey number. It is known that $\sqrt{2} \leq \liminf_{n\to\infty} r(n,n)^{1/n} \leq \limsup_{n\to\infty} r(n,n)^{1/n} \leq 4$ (with recent improvements to the upper bound). Prove or disprove: the limit
$$c \;=\; \lim_{n \to \infty} r(n,n)^{1/n}$$
exists. If it does, determine its value.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The existence of $\lim_{n\to\infty} r(n,n)^{1/n}$ remains a famous open problem. Even with the recent exponential improvement on the upper bound for $r(n,n)$ by Campos, Griffiths, Morris, and Sahasrabudhe (2023), the existence of the limit has not been established, and no nontrivial lower bound on $\liminf$ beyond $\sqrt 2$ is known.

The conjecture that every $n$-point set in general position admits a convex decomposition with at most $n+1$ convex polygons was disproved by Aichholzer and Krasser in 2001, who exhibited point configurations requiring more than $n+1$ pieces. Subsequent work has tightened both lower and upper bounds; the best known upper bound (Neumann-Lara, Rivera-Campo, Urrutia and later improvements) is linear in $n$ with a larger constant.

Let F = {l_1, ..., l_n} be a family of n pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the Euclidean plane. A simple alternating path of F is a non-self-intersecting polygonal chain whose edges alternate between (i) "input edges," each of which is a segment of F, and (ii) "connecting edges," each of which has its two endpoints on segments of F and does not intersect any segment of F other than at those two endpoints. The length of such a path is the number of input edges (elements of F) it uses.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every n and every family F of n pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane, F admits a simple alternating path that uses at least c · log n elements of F.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Hoffmann and Tóth proved that the segment endpoint visibility graph of any set of n pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane admits a non-crossing alternating path of length Ω(log n), confirming the conjecture; matching upper-bound constructions show the log n order is tight. Subsequent work ("Long Alternating Paths Exist," SoCG 2020) further extends results in this area.

For positive integers $s,t$, the diagonal Ramsey number $r(s,t)$ is the smallest integer $N$ such that every red/blue edge-coloring of the complete graph $K_N$ contains either a red $K_s$ or a blue $K_t$. Equivalently, $r(n,n)$ is the smallest $N$ such that every simple graph on $N$ vertices contains either a clique of size $n$ or an independent set of size $n$.

A constructive lower bound for $r(n,n)$ means: an explicit deterministic algorithm that, given $n$, outputs a simple graph $G_n$ on $N$ vertices (in time polynomial in $N$) such that $G_n$ contains neither a clique of size $n$ nor an independent set of size $n$; this witnesses $r(n,n) > N$.

Problem: Exhibit such an explicit construction achieving an exponential lower bound. Concretely, find a constant $c > 0$ and an explicit (polynomial-time constructible) family of graphs $\{G_n\}$ on $N = N(n)$ vertices with no clique and no independent set of size $n$, such that
$$r(n,n) > (1+c)^n.$$

The best known explicit construction, due to Chattopadhyay and Zuckerman (2015) and subsequent improvements via two-source extractors, yields Ramsey graphs avoiding cliques/independent sets of size roughly $2^{(\log\log n)^c}$, i.e. lower bounds on $r(n,n)$ that are quasi-polynomial in $n$ but still far from exponential $(1+c)^n$. Recent (2025) exponential improvements by Ma–Shen–Xie are non-constructive. The explicit-construction problem of obtaining $r(n,n)>(1+c)^n$ remains open.

Let n be a positive integer and let F = {C_1, ..., C_n} be a family of n pairwise disjoint closed convex sets in the Euclidean plane R^2. Say that a straight line l separates two convex sets A, B ⊂ R^2 if A and B lie in the two distinct open half-planes determined by l (so neither set meets l).

Prove or disprove the following: there exists an absolute constant c ≥ 0 such that for every such family F there exist an element C ∈ F and a straight line l with the property that l separates C from at least ⌊n/3⌋ − c of the remaining elements of F.

Let n be a positive integer and let F = {C_1, ..., C_n} be a family of n pairwise disjoint closed convex sets in the Euclidean plane R^2. Say that a straight line l separates two convex sets A, B ⊂ R^2 if A and B lie in the two distinct open half-planes determined by l (so neither set meets l).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture (that for n pairwise disjoint planar convex sets some element can be separated by a single line from ≈ n/3 of the others) appears to remain open in full generality. Partial results are known: for disks, a separation of about (n−7)/4 elements is achievable; for line segments that can be extended to pairwise disjoint half-lines, a bound of ⌈n/3⌉+1 has been established. No proof or counterexample for arbitrary convex sets achieving the n/3 bound has been found in the search.

Determine an asymptotic formula for $r(3,n)$ as $n 	o \infty$; that is, find a function $f(n)$ such that
$$\lim_{n 	o \infty}  rac{r(3,n)}{f(n)} = 1,$$
or show that the limit $\lim_{n	o\infty} r(3,n) \log n / n^2$ exists and determine its value.

The order of magnitude r(3,n) = Θ(n²/log n) was established by Ajtai–Komlós–Szemerédi (upper bound) and Kim (lower bound, 1995), with Shearer's constant 1+o(1) on top in the upper bound and Kim's c≈1/162 (later improved) in the lower bound. The exact asymptotic constant remains unknown; recent work (e.g., 2023–2025) has narrowed the gap to roughly a factor of 3 but no asymptotic formula has been determined. The problem is still open.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Even the asymptotic growth rate of diagonal Ramsey numbers $r(n,n)$ is not known precisely (recent work of Campos–Griffiths–Morris–Sahasrabudhe improved the upper bound), and no nontrivial separation of the form $r(n+1,n) \ge (1+c)\, r(n,n)$ is known. This is a long-standing conjecture (attributed to Shermer) on vertex guards for polygons with holes. It is known to hold for h = 1 (proved independently by Shermer and by Aggarwal). Let P be a simple polygon in the plane with n vertices, regarded as a closed region bounded by its edges. For an edge e of P, say that a point x ∈ P is visible from e if there exists a point y ∈ e such that the closed segment xy lies entirely in P. A set E of edges of P is said to illuminate (or cover) P if every point of P is visible from at least one edge in E; the elements of E are called edge guards.

Determine whether there exists a positive integer n₀ with the following property: for every simple polygon P having n ≥ n₀ vertices, one can choose a set E of at most ⌊n/4⌋ edges of P such that every point of P is visible from some edge in E.

A set E of edges of P is said to illuminate (or cover) P if every point of P is visible from at least one edge in E; the elements of E are called edge guards.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Toussaint's edge-guard conjecture (that ⌊n/4⌋ edge guards suffice to cover any simple polygon with sufficiently many vertices) remains a long-standing open problem in computational geometry. Subsequent work has established weaker upper bounds and studied variants (open edge guards, mobile guards, curvilinear galleries), but the original ⌊n/4⌋ conjecture has not been proved or disproved.

Consider the Hilbert space $L^2(\mathbb{R}, dx)$ and a nonnegative measurable function $\phi:\mathbb{R}\to[0,\infty)$ (an "equilibrium distribution") that is normalized so that $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi(x)\,dx=1$. Define the integral-difference operator $\mathcal{K}_\phi$ by
$$(\mathcal{K}_\phi u)(x)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{u(x)\phi(s)-u(s)\phi(x)}{|x-s|}\,ds,\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}.$$
Assume that $\phi$ has compact support $\Sigma:=\operatorname{supp}\phi\subset\mathbb{R}$ and that there exists a constant $c>0$ with $\phi(x)\ge c$ for almost every $x\in\Sigma$. Let $P_\Sigma$ denote the orthogonal projection of $L^2(\mathbb{R},dx)$ onto $L^2(\Sigma,dx)$, and put
$$K_\phi:=P_\Sigma\,\mathcal{K}_\phi\,P_\Sigma.$$
For the reference choice $\phi_0=\tfrac{1}{2}\chi_{[-1,1]}$, the corresponding restricted operator $K_{\phi_0}$ commutes with the second-order differential operator
$$L=(x^2-1)\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+2x\frac{d}{dx},$$
whose eigenfunctions are the Legendre polynomials.

Question: Does there exist any equilibrium distribution $\phi$ satisfying the above hypotheses (compact support and uniform separation from zero on the support), other than (affine images of) $\phi_0$, for which the restricted operator $K_\phi$ commutes with some nonzero differential operator or pseudodifferential operator on $\Sigma$?

For each a > 0, let H_a = L^2([-a, a]) and consider the integral-difference operator K_φ^a acting on suitable functions u on [-a, a] by
  (K_φ^a u)(x) = ∫_{-a}^{a} (u(x) φ(s) − u(s) φ(x)) / |x − s| ds,
where φ(x) = C e^{−x^2} and C > 0 is a fixed normalization constant (e.g. so that ∫_{-∞}^{∞} φ = 1). By the rescaling x = a y, this operator is unitarily equivalent to an operator K_a on L^2([-1, 1]) defined by
  (K_a u)(x) = ∫_{-1}^{1} (u(x) φ_a(s) − u(s) φ_a(x)) / |x − s| ds,
with φ_a(x) = C_a e^{−a^2 x^2} (C_a chosen analogously). Each K_a is self-adjoint and nonnegative; let E_a(·) denote its spectral projection. It is known that for every M > 0,
  dim E_a([−M, M]) H_a → ∞ as a → ∞,
so that 0 is a point of spectral concentration in the large-a limit.

Question: As a → ∞, does the discrete spectrum of the family {K_a} condense into continuous spectrum of a limiting operator? More generally, determine the spectral properties (nature of the spectrum: pure point, absolutely continuous, singular continuous; multiplicity; spectral measure) of the limit operator obtained from K_a as a → ∞.

Let $\varphi:\mathbb{R}\to[0,\infty)$ be a nonnegative integrable function (an "equilibrium distribution") with $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\varphi(x)\,dx<\infty$ and with infinite support, i.e.\ the set $\{x\in\mathbb{R}:\varphi(x)>0\}$ is unbounded. Consider the integral-difference operator $K_\varphi$ acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R},dx)$ by
$$(K_\varphi f)(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}} k(x-y)\,\sqrt{\varphi(x)\varphi(y)}\,f(y)\,dy,$$
where $k$ is a fixed even, real-valued kernel (the "difference" kernel) such that $K_\varphi$ defines a bounded self-adjoint operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R},dx)$.

For the case when $\varphi$ has compact support, spectral information about $K_\varphi$ can be obtained by comparing its resolvent with that of the "constant-equilibrium" reference operator
$$(K_0 f)(x)=c\int_{I} k(x-y)\,f(y)\,dy,\qquad x\in I,$$
acting on $L^2(I,dx)$ for a finite interval $I\subset\mathbb{R}$ with $c>0$ constant on $I$. When $\varphi$ has infinite support, two obstructions arise:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\varphi$ cannot simultaneously be integrable and uniformly bounded away from zero on $\mathbb{R}$, so the compact-support resolvent-comparison method does not apply;
\item the constant-equilibrium reference operator $K_0$ cannot be defined on all of $\mathbb{R}$ because the corresponding integrals diverge.
\end{enumerate}

Problem: Construct an alternative reference operator $K_{\mathrm{ref}}$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R},dx)$, adapted to equilibrium distributions $\varphi$ with infinite support, that is (i) explicitly definable on all of $\mathbb{R}$ without divergence, (ii) amenable to resolvent or related comparison with $K_\varphi$, and (iii) yields effective spectral information (essential spectrum, discrete spectrum, asymptotics of eigenvalues) for $K_\varphi$. Develop the corresponding spectral analysis of $K_\varphi$ via this reference operator.

For integers $n \ge 1$ and $0 \le t \le n$, let $H = H(n,t)$ denote the graph obtained from the complete graph $K_n$ by adding one new vertex and joining it to exactly $t$ of the vertices of $K_n$; thus $H$ has $\binom{n}{2} + t$ edges.

Prove or disprove: for every graph $G$ with exactly $\binom{n}{2} + t$ edges (and no isolated vertices), one has
$$r(G,G) \le r(H,H).$$

Equivalently, among all graphs with $\binom{n}{2}+t$ edges, the diagonal Ramsey number is maximized by $H(n,t)$.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, let $n>1$ be an integer, and let $k^{[n]}=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the polynomial algebra in $n$ variables over $k$. Define
$$\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k^{[n]} := \{\sigma\in \mathrm{Aut}_k k^{[n]}\mid \det(D_i(\sigma(x_j)))_{1\le i,j\le n}=1\},$$
where $D_i=\partial/\partial x_i$. Let $T$ be the diagonal torus
$$T:=\{\sigma=\mathrm{diag}(t_1,\dots,t_n)\in \mathrm{Aut}^*_k k^{[n]}\mid \sigma(x_i)=t_i x_i,\; t_i\in k^*,\; t_1\cdots t_n=1\}.$$
A nonzero locally nilpotent derivation $D$ of $k^{[n]}$ is called a root vector of $\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k^{[n]}$ with respect to $T$ if there exists a nontrivial character $\chi:T\to \mathbb{G}_m$ such that $\sigma\circ D\circ \sigma^{-1}=\chi(\sigma)D$ for every $\sigma\in T$; the character $\chi$ is then called the corresponding root.

Determine all roots and all root vectors of $\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k^{[n]}$ with respect to $T$.

The problem (a question of Popov on roots of the affine Cremona group with respect to the diagonal torus) was solved by A. Liendo (arXiv:1010.4034, 2010; published in Transformation Groups, 2011). Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$ and let $n>1$. Let $\mathrm{Aut}_k k[n]$ denote the group of polynomial $k$-automorphisms of the polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, identified with the group of regular automorphisms of affine $n$-space $\mathbb{A}^n_k$. Let
$$\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k[n] := \{\varphi \in \mathrm{Aut}_k k[n] : \det(\mathrm{Jac}(\varphi)) = 1\}$$
be the subgroup of volume-preserving (Jacobian determinant $1$) automorphisms. An algebraic torus action on $\mathbb{A}^n_k$ is a morphism of algebraic groups $T \to \mathrm{Aut}_k k[n]$, where $T \cong (k^*)^r$ for some $r\ge 1$; the action is called linearizable if there exist coordinates on $\mathbb{A}^n_k$ in which $T$ acts by diagonal linear transformations. Call the action volume-preserving if its image lies in $\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k[n]$.

Question: Is every volume-preserving algebraic torus action on $\mathbb{A}^n_k$ linearizable? Equivalently, is it true that $\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k[n]$ contains no maximal (with respect to inclusion) algebraic tori of dimension less than $n-1$? In particular, resolve the first nontrivial case $n=3$.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, let $n>1$ be an integer, and let $k^{[n]}=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables. Denote by $\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k^{[n]}$ the group of $k$-algebra automorphisms of $k^{[n]}$ whose Jacobian determinant equals $1$ (the volume-preserving polynomial automorphisms).

A $k$-derivation $D$ of $k^{[n]}$ is called locally nilpotent if for every $f\in k^{[n]}$ there exists an integer $m\ge 1$ with $D^m(f)=0$; for such $D$ the formal exponential $\exp D=\sum_{m\ge 0} D^m/m!$ is a well-defined element of $\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k^{[n]}$, and for every $f\in\ker D$ the product $fD$ is again locally nilpotent, so $\exp(fD)\in\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k^{[n]}$.

Call a subgroup $G\le\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k^{[n]}$ $\partial$-generated if there exists a (possibly infinite) set $\mathcal G$ of locally nilpotent $k$-derivations of $k^{[n]}$ such that $G$ is generated by $\{\exp D : D\in\mathcal G\}$. Call $G$ finitely $\partial$-generated if there exists a finite set $\mathcal G$ of locally nilpotent $k$-derivations such that $G$ is generated by $\{\exp(fD) : D\in\mathcal G,\ f\in\ker D\}$.

Question: Is $\mathrm{Aut}^*_k k^{[n]}$ $\partial$-generated? If yes, is it finitely $\partial$-generated?

In the Table-$k$-SUM problem, the input consists of a $k \times m$ table $A$ of integers (i.e., $k$ rows, each containing $m$ integers) together with a target integer $S$. The standard meet-in-the-middle algorithm solves Table-$k$-SUM in time $O(m^{\lceil k/2 \rceil})$ (up to polylogarithmic factors).

Fix an integer k ≥ 2. In the k-SUM problem, the input consists of m integers a_1, ..., a_m together with a target integer S, and one must decide whether there exist indices 1 ≤ i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_k ≤ m such that a_{i_1} + a_{i_2} + ... + a_{i_k} = S.

Recall the following two models of computation on inputs viewed as points in R^m:

(a) Algebraic decision tree model. A computation is a rooted ternary tree whose internal nodes are labeled by polynomials p(x_1, ..., x_m) of bounded degree; the branch taken at a node depends on the sign (negative, zero, positive) of p evaluated on the input. Leaves are labeled "yes" or "no". The complexity is the depth (worst-case number of polynomial tests).

(b) Algebraic computation tree model. A computation tree in which each internal node either performs an arithmetic operation (+, −, ×, ÷, √) on previously computed values or the input variables, or branches on the sign of a previously computed value. The complexity is again the depth.

Problem: Establish any non-trivial (i.e., super-linear, or more generally super-(m log m)) lower bound on the depth required to solve the k-SUM problem in either the algebraic decision tree model or the algebraic computation tree model, for some fixed k ≥ 3.

Part (a) is a special case of the Burr–Erdős conjecture, which asserts that p-degenerate graphs have linearly bounded Ramsey numbers; this was proved by Choongbum Lee (2017), so the linear bound for graphs whose p-vertex subgraphs have at most 2p−3 edges (a 2-degenerate-type condition) follows from Lee's theorem. For an integer $k\geq 1$, let $r_k = r(\underbrace{3,3,\dots,3}_{k})$ denote the $k$-color Ramsey number for triangles: the smallest integer $N$ such that every edge-coloring of the complete graph $K_N$ with $k$ colors contains a monochromatic triangle. It is known that the sequence $(r_k)$ is supermultiplicative, i.e. $r_{k+\ell}\geq r_k\, r_\ell$ for all $k,\ell\geq 1$, so by Fekete's lemma the limit
$$L = \lim_{k\to\infty} r_k^{1/k}$$
exists in $(1,\infty]$. Schur's classical bound gives $r_k < e\cdot k!$ (in particular $L$ could a priori be infinite, although the upper bound $r_k \le \lfloor e\cdot k!\rfloor$ does not immediately yield finiteness via $k$-th roots). Determine the value of $L$.

Define the following two computational problems.

SUBSET-SUM: Given n positive integers a_1,...,a_n and a positive integer goal B, decide whether there exists a subset I ⊆ {1,...,n} with sum_{i∈I} a_i = B.

Table-k-SUM (k fixed): Given a k×m table T of positive integers and a positive integer goal S, decide whether there exist indices j_1,...,j_k ∈ {1,...,m} (one entry chosen from each of the k rows) such that T[1,j_1] + T[2,j_2] + ... + T[k,j_k] = S.

It is known (by standard padding/encoding arguments) that an efficient polynomial-time algorithm for Table-k-SUM for every fixed k would imply faster exact exponential-time algorithms for SUBSET-SUM. Establish (or refute) a reverse implication: prove that the existence of a fast exact exponential-time algorithm for SUBSET-SUM (e.g. running in time c^n for some constant c < 2) implies the existence of a polynomial-time algorithm for Table-k-SUM for every fixed k. More generally, identify any nontrivial reduction direction showing that improved exponential-time algorithms for SUBSET-SUM yield improved (polynomial-time) algorithms for Table-k-SUM.

EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM is the following decision problem: given n positive integers b_1, ..., b_n, decide whether there exist two disjoint non-empty subsets A, B ⊆ {1, ..., n} such that Σ_{i∈A} b_i = Σ_{i∈B} b_i. A baseline exact algorithm runs in O*(2^n) time (where O* hides factors polynomial in n) via reduction to a 4-SUM-style tabulation. SUBSET-SUM is the related problem of, given positive integers b_1, ..., b_n and a target t, deciding whether some subset sums to t; it admits an O*(2^{n/2}) meet-in-the-middle algorithm.

(a) Design an exact algorithm for EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM whose worst-case running time is strictly better than O*(2^n) (and ideally better than the meet-in-the-middle bound O*(3^{n/2}) ≈ O*(1.7321^n)).

(b) Clarify the relationship between the time complexities of exact algorithms for SUBSET-SUM and for EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM: in particular, determine whether a faster-than-2^{n/2} algorithm for SUBSET-SUM yields a correspondingly faster algorithm for EQUAL-SUBSET-SUM, and conversely.

The conjecture (that bounded-degree graphs have linear size-Ramsey number) was disproved by Rödl and Szemerédi, who constructed graphs on n vertices of maximum degree 3 with size-Ramsey number at least c·n·(log n)^{1/60}. The lower bound has since been strengthened (e.g., to c·n·exp(c√log n)) by Tikhomirov and others. Thus, the disjunction "prove or disprove" is resolved in the disprove direction.

Fix an integer k ≥ 3. The k-CLIQUE problem is defined as follows: given an undirected simple loopless graph G on p vertices, decide whether G contains a clique on k vertices (i.e., a subset of k pairwise adjacent vertices).

The currently fastest known algorithms for k-CLIQUE (with fixed k) reduce the problem to fast matrix multiplication, yielding a running time of O(p^{ωk/3}) (where ω < 2.373 is the matrix-multiplication exponent), due to Nešetřil and Poljak. The space complexity of such algorithms is polynomial in p.

Problem: Design an algorithm for k-CLIQUE that achieves either
(a) asymptotically better worst-case time complexity than O(p^{ωk/3}), or
(b) asymptotically better worst-case space complexity than the existing matrix-multiplication-based methods while keeping competitive time, or
(c) simultaneous improvement in both time and space complexity,
where the bounds are measured as functions of p with k held fixed.

For a graph $G$, let $K_{1,n}$ denote the star with $n$ edges. For positive integers $s, t$ and sequences of positive integers $n_1, \dots, n_s$ and $m_1, \dots, m_t$, let
$$F_1 = \bigcup_{i=1}^{s} K_{1,n_i}, \qquad F_2 = \bigcup_{j=1}^{t} K_{1,m_j}$$
denote the vertex-disjoint unions of the indicated stars.

The size Ramsey number $\hat{r}(F_1, F_2)$ is defined as the smallest integer $N$ such that there exists a graph $H$ with $N$ edges with the property that in every 2-coloring of the edges of $H$ with colors red and blue, either $H$ contains a red copy of $F_1$ or a blue copy of $F_2$.

For each integer $k$ with $2 \le k \le s+t$, define
$$\ell_k = \max\{\, n_i + m_j - 1 \;:\; i+j = k,\ 1 \le i \le s,\ 1 \le j \le t \,\}.$$
(When the set is empty, take $\ell_k = 0$.)

Prove that
$$\hat{r}(F_1, F_2) \;=\; \sum_{k=2}^{s+t} \ell_k.$$

(It is known that in the special case $n_1 = \cdots = n_s = n$ and $m_1 = \cdots = m_t = m$ one has $\hat{r}(sK_{1,n}, tK_{1,m}) = (m+n-1)(s+t-1)$.)

The fastest known k-clique algorithms use the Nešetřil–Poljak reduction to (rectangular) matrix multiplication, giving running time O(n^{ωk/3}) when 3 | k, and improvements due to Eisenbrand–Grandoni when k ≢ 0 (mod 3). for some constant $C_r > 0$ depending only on $r$.

$$t(n, K_{r,r}) > c_r \, n^{2 - 1/r}$$
for all sufficiently large $n$. Equivalently, show that the Kővári–Sós–Turán upper bound is tight in order of magnitude for every $r$.

Let n be a positive integer. Boolean matrix multiplication (BMM) is the problem of computing, given two n×n matrices A, B with entries in {0,1}, the n×n matrix C with entries C[i,j] = OR over k of (A[i,k] AND B[k,j]). The 3-CLIQUE (triangle detection) problem is: given an undirected simple loopless graph on p vertices, decide whether it contains three pairwise adjacent vertices.

Say that two problems are "subcubically equivalent" if, for every ε > 0, a truly subcubic O(N^{3−ε}) time algorithm for one yields a truly subcubic algorithm for the other (with appropriate parameter identification p = Θ(n)).

Determine whether 3-CLIQUE has the same algorithmic difficulty as Boolean matrix multiplication. In particular, does there exist an algorithm solving 3-CLIQUE in time T(p) such that BMM on n×n Boolean matrices can be solved in time Õ(T(n))? Equivalently, can every improvement in the running time for triangle detection be transferred to an improvement for Boolean matrix multiplication?

Let $r \geq 2$ be an integer. Suppose $H$ is a bipartite graph that contains a subgraph $H'$ with minimum degree strictly greater than $r$. Then there exist constants $c > 0$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ (depending only on $H$) such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n,H) \;\geq\; c\, n^{\,2 - 1/r + \varepsilon}$$
for all sufficiently large $n$.

The conjecture was disproved by Oliver Janzer (2021, published in IMRN 2023). For the case $r=2$, the conjecture predicts that any bipartite graph $H$ containing a subgraph of minimum degree at least 3 satisfies $\mathrm{ex}(n,H) \geq c\, n^{3/2+\varepsilon}$. Janzer constructed, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a 3-regular bipartite graph $H$ with $\mathrm{ex}(n,H) = O(n^{4/3+\varepsilon})$, contradicting the conjecture.

Let $\omega$ denote the exponent of square matrix multiplication, i.e., the infimum of real numbers $c$ such that two $n \times n$ matrices over a ring can be multiplied using $O(n^c)$ ring operations. Use $O^*(\cdot)$ to suppress factors polynomial in the input size.

The MAX-CUT problem is defined as follows: given an undirected graph $G = (V, E)$ on $n = |V|$ vertices, find a subset $X \subseteq V$ that maximizes the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in $X$, i.e., the size of the cut $|\{\{u,v\} \in E : |\{u,v\} \cap X| = 1\}|$.

A known exact algorithm solves MAX-CUT in time $O^*(2^{\omega n/3})$ by reducing the problem to finding a maximum-weight triangle in an auxiliary graph of $2^{n/3}$ vertices and then applying fast matrix multiplication.

Problem: Design an exact algorithm for MAX-CUT on general $n$-vertex graphs whose worst-case running time is asymptotically faster than $O^*(2^{\omega n/3})$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The rational exponents conjecture for Turán numbers of bipartite graphs (a converse to the Erdős–Simonovits problem) remains open. Bukh–Conlon (2018) showed every rational in (1,2) is realized as the Turán exponent of a finite family of graphs, and Kang–Kim–Liu (2020) and subsequent work established new families of rationals realized by a single bipartite graph (e.g. 2−2/(2k+1)), but the conjecture is far from settled in full generality.

Let n be a positive integer and let d : {1,…,n} × {1,…,n} → ℝ_{≥0} be a distance function (not assumed symmetric or to satisfy the triangle inequality). Consider the Hamiltonian-path version of the travelling salesman problem: among all permutations σ of {2,…,n−1}, find one minimizing

  d(1, σ(2)) + d(σ(2), σ(3)) + ⋯ + d(σ(n−2), σ(n−1)) + d(σ(n−1), n),

i.e., the shortest path starting at city 1, ending at city n, and visiting each of the cities 2,…,n−1 exactly once.

Design an exact algorithm that solves this problem in time O*(1.99^n), where O*(·) suppresses factors polynomial in n (and in the bit-length of the input distances). Equivalently, exhibit a constant c < 2 and an exact algorithm running in time O*(c^n).

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $t(n,Q_k)$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular, determine the asymptotic order of $t(n,Q_3)$. It is known that there exist positive constants $c_1,c_2$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$,
$$ c_1\, n^{3/2} \;\le\; t(n,Q_3) \;\le\; c_2\, n^{8/5}.$$
Close this gap by determining the correct order of magnitude of $t(n,Q_3)$.

Let $G$ be a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices. A cycle in $G$ is a subgraph isomorphic to $C_k$ for some $k \geq 3$ (i.e., a simple cycle on $k$ distinct vertices). Let $c(G)$ denote the total number of simple cycles in $G$ (of all lengths from $3$ to $n$).

Design an exact algorithm that, given $G$, computes $c(G)$ and runs in time $O^*(1.99^n)$, where the $O^*$ notation suppresses factors polynomial in $n$. Equivalently, exhibit a constant $c < 2$ and an algorithm computing $c(G)$ in time $O^*(c^n)$, or prove that no such algorithm exists.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of counting all simple cycles in a general n-vertex graph in time O*(c^n) for some c<2 appears to remain open. Surveys and texts on exact exponential algorithms (e.g., Fomin–Kratsch) list cycle counting among problems lacking a known sub-2^n algorithm; subexponential results are known only for restricted classes such as planar graphs. No general-graph algorithm achieving O*(1.99^n) was found in the search.

Let $K_{2,2,2}$ denote the octahedron graph, i.e., the complete tripartite graph with three parts of size $2$ (equivalently, the $1$-skeleton of the regular octahedron). For a graph $G$, let $\alpha(G)$ denote the independence number of $G$ (the size of the largest set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices).

Prove or disprove: every sequence $(G_n)_{n \ge 1}$ of graphs, where $G_n$ has $n$ vertices, contains no copy of $K_{2,2,2}$ as a subgraph, and satisfies $\alpha(G_n) = o(n)$ as $n \to \infty$, must also satisfy
$$e(G_n) = o(n^2),$$
where $e(G_n)$ denotes the number of edges of $G_n$.

Equivalently, determine whether the Ramsey–Turán number $\operatorname{RT}(n, K_{2,2,2}, o(n)) = o(n^2)$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Surveys of Ramsey–Turán theory describe the determination of $\operatorname{RT}(n,H,o(n))$ for cliques (Erdős–Sós for odd cliques, Erdős–Hajnal–Sós–Szemerédi for even cliques), but the analogous problem for the octahedron $K_{2,2,2}$ with $\alpha(G)=o(n)$ is repeatedly cited as an open Erdős–Hajnal–Sós–Szemerédi problem. No solution was found in recent literature (Fox–Loh, Balogh–Hu–Simonovits, Conlon–Fox–Sudakov surveys, and 2024 work on generalized Ramsey–Turán numbers), so the problem appears still open.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question concerns the precise leading constant in the extremal number for graphs of girth at least 5. Standard surveys note that while an upper bound of order $\frac{1}{2}n^{3/2}$ is known and constructions from generalized quadrangle / polarity-type graphs give lower bounds, it remains open whether the leading constant equals $\frac{1}{2\sqrt 2}$, and even whether graphs of girth 5 are asymptotically denser than $\{C_3,C_4\}$-free graphs.

For a graph $H$ and a graph $G$, let $\#(H,G)$ denote the number of induced subgraphs of $G$ that are isomorphic to $H$. For integers $k\ge 2$ and $n\ge k$, define
$$f(k,n)=\min_{G}\bigl(\#(K_k,G)+\#(K_k,\overline{G})\bigr),$$
where the minimum is taken over all graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices and $\overline{G}$ denotes the complement of $G$, and $K_k$ is the complete graph on $k$ vertices.

Determine the value of $f(k,n)$, or equivalently determine the asymptotic constant
$$c_k=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{f(k,n)}{\binom{n}{k}},$$
for every integer $k\ge 4$. (For a uniformly random graph on $n$ vertices, $\#(K_k,G)+\#(K_k,\overline{G})$ equals $2^{1-\binom{k}{2}}\binom{n}{k}$ in expectation; it is known that $c_k<2^{1-\binom{k}{2}}$ for $k\ge 4$, so the random graph does not achieve the minimum.)

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The original Erdős conjecture that the random graph minimizes the number of monochromatic $K_k$'s was disproved by Thomason (1989) for $k\ge 4$, and improved constructions were given by Franek–Rödl and others. However, the exact value of $f(k,n)$ (equivalently the Ramsey multiplicity constant $c_k$) remains unknown for every $k\ge 4$; only upper and lower bounds are known, and the problem is regarded as open.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, let $R = k[X_0, X_1, \ldots, X_{n+3}]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring with irrelevant maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m} = (X_0, \ldots, X_{n+3})$, and let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+3}_k$ be a closed arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay subscheme of dimension $n > 0$ and codimension $3$. Set $I = I(X) \subset R$, $A = R/I$, and let
$$K = \mathrm{Ext}^{3}_{R}(A, R)(-n-4)$$
be the (graded) canonical module of $X$. Recall that $X$ (equivalently, $I$) is called licci if it lies in the complete-intersection liaison class of a complete intersection, i.e., it can be linked to a complete intersection in finitely many steps via complete-intersection links. It is known that if $X$ is licci, then the graded local cohomology modules satisfy
$$H^{i}_{\mathfrak{m}}(K \otimes_{R} I) = 0 \quad \text{for all } 0 \le i \le n.$$
Question: Is the converse true? That is, if $X$ is an arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^{n+3}$ of dimension $n>0$ and codimension $3$ such that $H^{i}_{\mathfrak{m}}(K \otimes_{R} I) = 0$ for every $0 \le i \le n$, must $X$ be licci?

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and let $\mathbb{P}^n = \mathbb{P}^n_k$ be projective $n$-space. A closed subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ is called arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay (ACM) if its homogeneous coordinate ring $k[x_0,\dots,x_n]/I_X$ is a Cohen–Macaulay ring. A subscheme is called arithmetically Gorenstein if its homogeneous coordinate ring is Gorenstein.

Given two equidimensional closed subschemes $V_1, V_2 \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ without embedded components and of the same codimension $c$, one says that $V_1$ and $V_2$ are directly Gorenstein linked if there exists an arithmetically Gorenstein subscheme $G \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ containing both, with $I_G : I_{V_1} = I_{V_2}$ and $I_G : I_{V_2} = I_{V_1}$. The Gorenstein liaison equivalence relation is the equivalence relation generated by direct Gorenstein links. A subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ is called glicci if it lies in the same Gorenstein liaison class as some complete intersection in $\mathbb{P}^n$ of the same codimension.

Fix an integer $c \ge 1$. Is it true that every arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay closed subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ of codimension $c$ is glicci, equivalently, that there is exactly one Gorenstein liaison class containing all codimension-$c$ ACM subschemes of $\mathbb{P}^n$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of whether every arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay subscheme of projective space is glicci is widely cited as a central open problem in Gorenstein liaison theory. It is known to hold in codimension 2 (where glicci is equivalent to having an N-type resolution) and for various special classes (e.g., certain monomial ideals, standard determinantal schemes), but the general case—even for zero-dimensional schemes in $\mathbb{P}^3$—remains open as of recent literature.

For a graph H, let f_n(H) denote the number of labelled graphs on the vertex set {1,2,...,n} that do not contain H as a subgraph, and let t(n,H) denote the Turán number of H, i.e. the maximum number of edges in an H-free graph on n vertices. It is known that t(n,C_4) = (1/2 + o(1)) n^{3/2}, where C_4 is the cycle on 4 vertices.

Prove or disprove the following:
  f_n(C_4) ≤ 2^{(1+o(1)) t(n,C_4)} = 2^{(1/2 + o(1)) n^{3/2}}
as n → ∞.

More generally, prove or disprove that for every graph H,
  f_n(H) ≤ 2^{(1+o(1)) t(n,H)}.

It is known that t(n,C_4) = (1/2 + o(1)) n^{3/2}, where C_4 is the cycle on 4 vertices.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture is proved for every non-bipartite H (Erdős–Frankl–Rödl). The bipartite case remains open even for H = C_4: Kleitman and Winston showed f_n(C_4) ≤ 2^{cn^{3/2}} for some constant c, and subsequent work (containers, Kleitman–Wilson, Kreuter) refined the constants for even cycles, but a tight bound of the form 2^{(1/2 + o(1)) n^{3/2}} for C_4 is not known. Recent surveys on the hypergraph container method explicitly note that the sharp constant for C_4-free graphs remains open.

The general question of whether every ACM subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^n$ is glicci is a well-known open problem in liaison theory. For a finite simple graph $G$, call an induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ regular if every vertex of $H$ has the same degree within $H$ (this includes the empty graph and complete graphs as trivial regular subgraphs). For a positive integer $n$, let $f(n)$ denote the largest integer $k$ such that every simple graph on $n$ vertices contains a regular induced subgraph on at least $k$ vertices. By Ramsey's theorem one has $f(n) \geq c \log n$ for some absolute constant $c > 0$, since every $n$-vertex graph contains a clique or independent set of size at least $c \log n$, both of which are regular.

Prove or disprove the following conjecture:
$$\frac{f(n)}{\log n} \longrightarrow \infty \quad \text{as } n \to \infty.$$

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $\mathbb{P}^n = \mathbb{P}^n_k$ denote projective $n$-space. Fix positive integers $p, q, r$ with $r \le \min(p,q)$, and let $M = (f_{ij})$ be a $p \times q$ matrix whose entries $f_{ij}$ are homogeneous polynomials in the coordinate ring $R = k[x_0, \dots, x_n]$, with the degrees of $f_{ij}$ chosen so that the $r \times r$ minors of $M$ are homogeneous. Let $I_r(M) \subset R$ be the ideal generated by the $r \times r$ minors of $M$, and let $X_{p,q,r} \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ be the closed subscheme defined by $I_r(M)$.

Assume that $X_{p,q,r}$ has the expected codimension
$$\mathrm{codim}\,X_{p,q,r} = (p-r+1)(q-r+1),$$
and that $X_{p,q,r}$ is arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay (i.e., $R/I_r(M)$ is a Cohen–Macaulay ring).

A subscheme $Y \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ is said to be glicci if it lies in the Gorenstein liaison class of a complete intersection, that is, if there is a finite sequence of Gorenstein links connecting $Y$ to a complete intersection subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^n$.

Question: Is every such $X_{p,q,r}$ glicci?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The case of maximal (i.e., $r = \min(p,q)$) standard determinantal schemes is known to be glicci by results going back to Gaeta and extended in the work on Gorenstein liaison (e.g., Kleppe–Migliore–Miró-Roig–Nagel–Peterson). Various subclasses—mixed ladder determinantal varieties, symmetric and skew-symmetric cases, and schemes arising from geometric vertex decomposition—have also been shown to be glicci. However, the general question for non-maximal $r \times r$ minors of an arbitrary $p \times q$ homogeneous matrix (with expected codimension and arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay) does not appear to have been settled in full generality, and remains a guiding open question in the area, of which the broader conjecture "every arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^n$ is glicci" is the well-known umbrella problem.

Let $f: X \to S$ be a smooth projective family of complex algebraic varieties over a smooth quasi-projective base $S$, and consider the associated period mapping
$$\Phi: S \to D/\Gamma,$$
where $D$ is the classifying domain (assumed here to be a bounded symmetric / Hermitian symmetric domain in the classical case, or more generally a period domain admitting a bounded realization) parametrizing polarized Hodge structures of the relevant type, and $\Gamma$ is the arithmetic monodromy group acting properly discontinuously on $D$. Borel's extension theorem asserts that if $\bar S$ is a smooth projective compactification of $S$ such that the boundary $\bar S \setminus S$ is a normal crossings divisor, then $\Phi$ extends to a morphism $\bar\Phi: \bar S \to \overline{D/\Gamma}$, where $\overline{D/\Gamma}$ denotes a canonical (e.g., Baily–Borel) compactification of $D/\Gamma$.

Question: Does the extension property continue to hold for an arbitrary smooth projective compactification $\bar S$ of $S$ whose boundary $\bar S \setminus S$ is not assumed to have normal crossings? Equivalently, characterize the precise sense in which $D/\Gamma$ is "minimal at infinity": namely, show that there is a canonical compactification of $D/\Gamma$ to which every period map from a smooth quasi-projective $S$ extends, independently of the choice of smooth compactification of $S$.

Let X be a smooth complex projective variety, and let {X_s : s ∈ S} → S be the Kuranishi (local versal) deformation of X, where S is a germ of the local moduli space at the point 0 corresponding to X. For each s ∈ S the complex cohomology H^k(X_s, C) carries a pure Hodge structure of weight k, given by the Hodge filtration F^p H^k(X_s, C). The local period map sends s ∈ S to the point in the appropriate flag variety (period domain) parametrising this Hodge filtration on the fixed underlying vector space H^k(X, C) (identified via the Gauss–Manin connection).

The local Torelli problem asks whether this local period map is injective (equivalently, whether the Hodge structures on the cohomology of the fibers separate points of S near 0).

(a) Develop general methods, applicable to broad classes of smooth projective varieties, by which the local Torelli theorem can be either established or refuted.

(b) Determine whether the local Torelli theorem holds for every simply connected smooth complex projective surface X with ample canonical bundle K_X (i.e. a simply connected canonical surface of general type): that is, decide whether for every such X the local period map on its Kuranishi space is injective at 0, or exhibit a counterexample.

Equivalently, show that every triangle-free graph on $5n$ vertices admits a cut (a bipartition of the vertex set) such that the number of edges not crossing the cut is at most $n^2$.

The conjecture of Erdős, Faudree, Pach and Spencer remains open in general. It is known to hold for triangle-free graphs with at least $n^2$ edges in the regime above $5n^2/... $ (Erdős–Győri–Simonovits proved it for graphs with at least roughly $5n^2$ edges via a related result), and recent work (e.g., Kwan et al.) has obtained progress on related "dense induced bipartite subgraphs in triangle-free graphs" questions, but the full conjecture in the intermediate edge range is still unresolved.

Let $X$ and $X'$ be two smooth complex projective K3 surfaces; that is, simply connected smooth projective surfaces over $\mathbb{C}$ with trivial canonical bundle $K_X \cong \mathcal{O}_X$ and $K_{X'} \cong \mathcal{O}_{X'}$. Let $L \in \mathrm{Pic}(X)$ and $L' \in \mathrm{Pic}(X')$ be ample line bundles (polarizations) of the same degree. Consider the second integral cohomology lattices $H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})$ and $H^2(X',\mathbb{Z})$, equipped with the cup-product intersection form (each isometric to the K3 lattice $-E_8(-1)^{\oplus 2} \oplus U^{\oplus 3}$), together with their Hodge decompositions
$$H^2(X,\mathbb{C}) = H^{2,0}(X) \oplus H^{1,1}(X) \oplus H^{0,2}(X),$$
and similarly for $X'$. Suppose there exists an isometry of lattices
$$\varphi : H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}) \longrightarrow H^2(X',\mathbb{Z})$$
such that $\varphi(c_1(L)) = c_1(L')$ and whose $\mathbb{C}$-linear extension sends $H^{2,0}(X)$ to $H^{2,0}(X')$ (equivalently, preserves the Hodge filtration).

Prove or disprove: there exists a unique isomorphism of algebraic varieties $f : X' \to X$ with $f^* L \cong L'$ such that $f^* = \varphi$ on $H^2$.

In other words, decide whether the polarized Hodge structure on $H^2$ together with the polarization class is a complete isomorphism invariant of polarized complex algebraic K3 surfaces (the global Torelli theorem for polarized K3 surfaces).

representations.normalized: A graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is called triangle-free if it contains no three mutually adjacent vertices. A triangle-free graph $G$ is called maximal triangle-free if for every pair of non-adjacent vertices $u,v$ in $G$, adding the edge $uv$ creates a triangle. Let $M(n)$ denote the number of (labeled) maximal triangle-free graphs on the vertex set $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. Determine the asymptotic behavior of $M(n)$, or at least obtain matching upper and lower bounds for $\log_2 M(n)$ as $n\to\infty$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Balogh and Petříčková (2014) proved that the number of maximal triangle-free graphs on n vertices is 2^{n^2/8 + o(n^2)}, matching the known lower bound and resolving Erdős's problem. A follow-up by Balogh, Liu, Petříčková, and Sharifzadeh determined the typical structure of such graphs.

Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^4_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a smooth (nonsingular) cubic hypersurface (a smooth cubic threefold). The third integral cohomology $H^3(X,\mathbb{Z})$ carries a Hodge structure of weight 1 with Hodge decomposition $H^3(X,\mathbb{C}) = H^{2,1}(X) \oplus H^{1,2}(X)$ and a unimodular intersection form, giving rise to the intermediate Jacobian $J(X) = H^{1,2}(X)/H^3(X,\mathbb{Z})$, which is a principally polarized abelian variety of dimension 5; equivalently, $X$ determines a polarized Hodge structure on $H^3(X,\mathbb{Z})$.

Question: Does the global Torelli theorem hold for smooth cubic threefolds? That is, if $X_1, X_2 \subset \mathbb{P}^4_{\mathbb{C}}$ are two smooth cubic threefolds such that their principally polarized intermediate Jacobians $(J(X_1),\Theta_1)$ and $(J(X_2),\Theta_2)$ are isomorphic as principally polarized abelian varieties (equivalently, the polarized Hodge structures on $H^3(X_1,\mathbb{Z})$ and $H^3(X_2,\mathbb{Z})$ are isomorphic), must $X_1$ and $X_2$ be isomorphic as projective varieties?

The global Torelli theorem for smooth cubic threefolds was established by Clemens and Griffiths in "The intermediate Jacobian of the cubic threefold," Annals of Mathematics 95 (1972), 281–356, where they proved that a smooth cubic threefold over $\mathbb{C}$ is uniquely determined up to isomorphism by its principally polarized intermediate Jacobian. Subsequent works (e.g., Beauville, Mumford) gave alternative proofs.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The conjecture was settled asymptotically by Grzesik (2012) and independently by Hatami, Hladký, Král', Norin, and Razborov (2013) using flag algebras: every triangle-free graph on N vertices has at most (N/5)^5 pentagons. Lidický and Pfender (2017) extended this to an exact result for all n ≥ 9, characterizing the balanced blow-up of C_5 as the unique extremal graph.

Let $\Delta \subset \mathbb{C}$ be an open disc with origin $0$, and let $\Delta^* = \Delta \setminus \{0\}$. Let $f \colon Y \to \Delta$ be a proper holomorphic map with $Y$ a smooth complex manifold, such that the restriction $f \colon f^{-1}(\Delta^*) \to \Delta^*$ is a smooth proper submersion with connected fibers. Denote the singular fiber by $V_{s_0} = f^{-1}(0)$ and a nearby smooth fiber by $V_s = f^{-1}(s)$ for $s \in \Delta^*$. The Picard–Lefschetz monodromy associated to a loop around $0$ acts on $H^q(V_s, \mathbb{C})$; transporting to the special fiber via the specialization map, one obtains an endomorphism $T \colon H^q(V_{s_0}, \mathbb{C}) \to H^q(V_{s_0}, \mathbb{C})$.

Call a class $\psi \in H^q(V_{s_0}, \mathbb{C})$ a local invariant cohomology class if $T(\psi) = \psi$.

Question: For every integer $q \geq 0$ and every local invariant cohomology class $\psi \in H^q(V_{s_0}, \mathbb{C})$, does there exist a class $\widetilde{\psi} \in H^q(Y, \mathbb{C})$ whose restriction to $V_{s_0}$ equals $\psi$? Equivalently, is the restriction map $H^q(Y, \mathbb{C}) \to H^q(V_{s_0}, \mathbb{C})^T$ surjective?

The local invariant cycle conjecture (originally posed by Griffiths) was proved over the complex numbers. Clemens–Schmid established it via limit mixed Hodge structures; Deligne gave an independent proof using the Weil conjectures (in the algebraic setting), and it also follows from the BBDG decomposition theorem. The theorem is now standard and goes by the name "local invariant cycle theorem".

The conjecture remains open. Partial progress includes Krivelevich's bound (with $n^2/36$ in place of $n^2/50$), Razborov's improvement showing the statement holds with constant $27/1024$ instead of $1/50$, results of Keevash–Sudakov under additional hypotheses, and Norin–Yepremyan for dense graphs. Let $U \subset \mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ be an open neighborhood of the origin and let $f : U \to \mathbb{C}$ be a holomorphic function with $f(0) = 0$ such that $0$ is an isolated critical point of $f$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ and $0 < \eta \ll \varepsilon$, set $B = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^{n+1} : \|z\| \le \varepsilon\}$ and let $D^* = \{s \in \mathbb{C} : 0 < |s| < \eta\}$. For $s \in D^*$ define the Milnor fiber
$$M_s = \{z \in B : f(z) = s\},$$
which is a smooth compact manifold with boundary, homotopy equivalent to a bouquet of $n$-spheres. Fix a base point $s_0 \in D^*$ and let $T : H^n(M_{s_0}, \mathbb{Q}) \to H^n(M_{s_0}, \mathbb{Q})$ be the Picard–Lefschetz monodromy transformation obtained by parallel-transporting cohomology classes once around the origin along the loop $s_0 e^{2\pi i t}$, $t \in [0,1]$.

Question: Is $T$ necessarily of finite order, i.e. does there exist a positive integer $N$ such that $T^N = \mathrm{id}$ on $H^n(M_{s_0}, \mathbb{Q})$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The question is resolved by the monodromy theorem (Brieskorn, "Die Monodromie der isolierten Singularitäten von Hyperflächen", 1970; also Landman, Clemens, Deligne, Grothendieck): for any isolated hypersurface singularity the Picard–Lefschetz monodromy $T$ acting on $H^n(M_{s_0}, \mathbb{Q})$ is quasi-unipotent — its eigenvalues are roots of unity and $(T^N - I)^{n+1} = 0$ for some positive integer $N$. Consequently $T$ is of finite order if and only if it is semisimple (equivalently, if and only if a resolution graph contains no cycles in the surface case); in general nontrivial Jordan blocks occur, so $T$ need not be of finite order. Thus the question is answered: $T$ is always quasi-unipotent but not always of finite order.

Let $f:\mathcal{X}\to \Delta$ be a proper holomorphic map from a complex manifold $\mathcal{X}$ to the unit disk $\Delta\subset\mathbb{C}$, smooth over the punctured disk $\Delta^{*}=\Delta\setminus\{0\}$, with fibers $X_t = f^{-1}(t)$ smooth projective of complex dimension $n$ for $t\in\Delta^{*}$. Fix a base point $t_0\in\Delta^{*}$ and let $T:H^{k}(X_{t_0},\mathbb{Q})\to H^{k}(X_{t_0},\mathbb{Q})$ be the Picard–Lefschetz (local monodromy) transformation obtained by parallel transport along the positive generator of $\pi_1(\Delta^{*},t_0)$.

The local monodromy theorem has two parts:
(i) (Eigenvalue part) Every eigenvalue of $T$ is a root of unity; equivalently, there exist positive integers $m$ such that $T^{m}$ is unipotent.
(ii) (Elementary-divisor / nilpotency-index part) For such $m$, the unipotent operator $T^{m}$ satisfies $(T^{m}-I)^{k+1}=0$, i.e. the size of every Jordan block of $T^{m}$ is at most $k+1$, where $k$ is the cohomological degree.

Problem: Provide a proof — analytic or group-theoretic in nature — of part (i) that simultaneously yields part (ii), i.e. produces the bound $k+1$ on the index of nilpotence of $T^{m}-I$ on $H^{k}(X_{t_0},\mathbb{Q})$.

The local monodromy theorem, including both the quasi-unipotence (eigenvalue) part and the nilpotency-index bound on Jordan block sizes, was established by Landman (1967/1973) via Picard–Lefschetz methods, and by Katz (with input from Deligne) using p-adic/Gauss–Manin connection techniques in "Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem" (Publ. IHÉS 39, 1970), which gives the bound on the exponent of nilpotence. Analytic proofs were later given by Schmid via the nilpotent orbit theorem. The problem is regarded as solved.

Let D be a period matrix domain (a classifying space for polarized Hodge structures of a fixed type, realized as an open orbit G(ℝ)/V in its compact dual, where G is a ℚ-algebraic group of Hodge type and V is the compact isotropy of a reference Hodge structure). Let Γ ⊂ G(ℚ) be an arithmetic subgroup acting properly discontinuously on D, and form the analytic quotient D/Γ. For each rational boundary component F_j of D (in the sense of Hodge-theoretic boundary components stabilized by ℚ-parabolic subgroups), let Γ_j be the arithmetic subgroup of the stabilizer acting on F_j, and equip F_j/Γ_j with its natural topology.

Question: Does there exist a separated, locally compact topological space (D/Γ)* with all of the following properties?
(i) (D/Γ)* contains D/Γ as an open dense subset.
(ii) Set-theoretically, (D/Γ)* = (D/Γ) ⊔ ⨆_j (F_j/Γ_j), the union running over a chosen collection of rational boundary components, each F_j/Γ_j carrying its natural topology as a subspace of (D/Γ)*.
(iii) For every smooth algebraic family X → S of polarized algebraic manifolds whose associated period mapping Φ : S → D/Γ is horizontal and holomorphic, Φ extends continuously to a map Φ* : S* → (D/Γ)*, where S* is a suitable (e.g. smooth projective) completion of S.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The problem, posed by Griffiths in the late 1960s, has been the subject of extensive work. Kato–Usui constructed partial compactifications Γ\D_Σ of period domain quotients using fans of nilpotent cones, achieving the desired extension property in classical (Hermitian symmetric) cases and conditionally in general (subject to existence of a "complete fan"). Watanabe gave a counterexample to the existence of a complete fan in non-classical cases, so a fully general Kato–Usui-type compactification with continuous extension for arbitrary horizontal period maps is not known. More recent work (Bakker–Brunebarbe–Tsimerman, Green–Griffiths–Laza–Robles, et al.) has constructed Hodge-theoretic and toroidal-type completions of period maps in various settings (e.g., every two-parameter horizontal period map admits a log-manifold completion), giving partial answers. The general question remains open.

$$f(n) = \max_{|V(G)|=n} \frac{\chi(G)}{\omega(G)},$$
where the maximum is taken over all simple graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices. It is known that there exist positive constants $c_1, c_2$ such that
$$c_1 \cdot \frac{n}{(\log_2 n)^2} \le f(n) \le c_2 \cdot \frac{n}{(\log_2 n)^2}$$
for all sufficiently large $n$. Determine whether the limit
$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{f(n)}{n / (\log_2 n)^2}$$
exists.
