Let $\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}$ denote the space of real $2\times 2$ matrices, equipped with the Euclidean (Frobenius) norm $\|X\| = \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(X^T X)}$, and let $\det X$ denote the determinant of $X$.

A function $f:\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called rank-one convex if for every $X,Y\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}$ with $\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le 1$ the function $t\mapsto f(X+tY)$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}$.

A locally bounded Borel function $f:\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called quasiconvex (in the sense of Morrey) if for every $X\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}$, every bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with $|\partial\Omega|=0$, and every smooth compactly supported $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$,
$$\int_\Omega f(X+\nabla\varphi(x))\,dx \;\ge\; f(X)\,|\Omega|.$$

Consider the restricted class $\mathcal{F}$ consisting of all functions $f:\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}\to\mathbb{R}$ of the form
$$f(X) = g(\|X\|,\det X)$$
for some function $g:[0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$.

Question: Is it true that every rank-one convex function $f\in\mathcal{F}$ is also quasiconvex?

Let $\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}$ denote the space of real $2\times 2$ matrices, equipped with the Euclidean (Frobenius) norm $\|X\| = \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(X^T X)}$, and let $\det X$ denote the determinant of $X$.

A function $f:\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called rank-one convex if for every $X,Y\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}$ with $\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le 1$ the function $t\mapsto f(X+tY)$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}$.

A locally bounded Borel function $f:\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called quasiconvex (in the sense of Morrey) if for every $X\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}$, every bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with $|\partial\Omega|=0$, and every smooth compactly supported $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$,
$$\int_\Omega f(X+\nabla\varphi(x))\,dx \;\ge\; f(X)\,|\Omega|.$$

Consider the restricted class $\mathcal{F}$ consisting of all functions $f:\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}\to\mathbb{R}$ of the form
$$f(X) = g(\|X\|,\det X)$$
for some function $g:[0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$.

Question: Is it true that every rank-one convex function $f\in\mathcal{F}$ is also quasiconvex?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Morrey's conjecture in the planar case (2×2 matrices) remains a major open problem in the calculus of variations. Recent work on the volumetric–isochoric split and isotropic energies depending on singular values and determinant (e.g., the "magic" function studied by Voss, Martin, Neff and collaborators, 2022) has reduced certain subcases to specific candidate energies but has not resolved the restricted version where the integrand depends only on the Frobenius norm and determinant. No proof or counterexample is currently known for this restricted class.

Let $M = G/K$ be a Riemannian homogeneous space, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively and effectively by isometries on $M$ and $K$ is the isotropy subgroup at a base point $o \in M$. A $G$-invariant Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ is called a $G$-geodesic orbit metric (or $G$-g.o. metric) if every geodesic of $(M,g)$ is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$; that is, for every geodesic $\gamma$ there exists $X$ in the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$ such that $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\cdot o$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$. The space $(M=G/K,g)$ is then called a $G$-g.o. space.

Problem: For an arbitrary Riemannian homogeneous space $M = G/K$ with $G$ a fixed connected transitive isometry group, determine explicitly the set of all $G$-invariant Riemannian metrics $g$ on $M$ such that $(M=G/K, g)$ is a $G$-g.o. space. In particular, produce a classification of all $G$-g.o. metrics that is valid for arbitrary homogeneous spaces $G/K$, rather than only within specific families (such as compact simple Lie groups, generalized flag manifolds, Stiefel manifolds, nilmanifolds, or other previously studied classes).

Let $(M = G/K, g)$ be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$ and $K$ is the isotropy subgroup at a base point $o \in M$. Let $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ be a reductive decomposition of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$, where $\mathfrak{k}$ is the Lie algebra of $K$ and $\mathfrak{m}$ is an $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant complement identified with the tangent space $T_o M$. A nonzero vector $X \in \mathfrak{g}$ is called a geodesic vector if the curve $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\cdot o$ is a geodesic of $(M,g)$. The space $(M,g)$ is called a g.o. (geodesic orbit) space if every geodesic through $o$ is of the form $\exp(tX)\cdot o$ for some $X \in \mathfrak{g}$.

Assume that $(M=G/K, g)$ is not a g.o. space. The problem is the following:

(a) Explicitly describe the homogeneous geodesics that $(M,g)$ does possess, i.e., determine the set
$$ \mathcal{V}(G/K, g) = \{ X \in \mathfrak{g} \setminus \{0\} : t \mapsto \exp(tX)\cdot o \text{ is a geodesic of } (M,g)\}. $$

(b) Provide an effective algorithmic method (in terms of the Lie bracket structure of $\mathfrak{g}$, the decomposition $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$, and the inner product on $\mathfrak{m}$ induced by $g$) for computing $\mathcal{V}(G/K, g)$ in the case when $(M,g)$ is not a g.o. space, i.e., when not every geodesic of $M$ arises in this way.

The literature contains the standard geodesic-vector criterion (Kowalski–Vanhecke) and explicit determinations of homogeneous geodesics in many specific classes (flag manifolds, certain Finsler and Randers spaces, sub-Riemannian settings), but no general effective classification of the set of geodesic vectors for arbitrary non-g.o. homogeneous Riemannian spaces appears to have been established. The problem is posed as an open program of describing such geodesics case by case, and current sources show only partial progress in special families.

Let M = G/K be a connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold with G a connected Lie group acting almost effectively by isometries and K a compact isotropy subgroup. Let g and k denote the Lie algebras of G and K, and fix a reductive decomposition g = k ⊕ m, where m is identified with the tangent space T_o(G/K) at the base point o = eK. The isotropy representation is the action of K (equivalently of Ad(K)) on m. A G-invariant Riemannian metric on G/K is called a geodesic orbit metric (g.o. metric) if every geodesic of (M, g) is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of G; the pair (G/K, g) is then called a g.o. space.

Problem. Assume that the isotropy representation of K on m decomposes as a direct sum of either exactly two or exactly three Ad(K)-irreducible submodules:
  m = m_1 ⊕ m_2   or   m = m_1 ⊕ m_2 ⊕ m_3.
Classify, up to equivalence, all pairs (G/K, g) of this form for which g is a g.o. metric. Equivalently, for each such homogeneous space G/K, determine explicitly all G-invariant Riemannian metrics that are geodesic orbit metrics.

The two-isotropy-summand case for compact simply connected g.o. spaces has been classified by Chen and Nikonorov (Geometriae Dedicata, 2019, and follow-up work). The three-summand case has been treated in several specific settings (e.g., simple isotropy group, rank-two compact Lie groups, Stiefel bundles, strongly isotropy irreducible building blocks), but a complete general classification does not appear to be available; the broader classification of g.o. manifolds remains an active open problem.

Let $(M,g)$ be a connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold. A presentation of $(M,g)$ as a coset space is a pair $(G,K)$, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively on $M$ by isometries of $g$ and $K$ is the isotropy subgroup at a chosen base point, so that $M = G/K$. The pair $(G,K)$ is called reductive if there exists an $\operatorname{Ad}(K)$-invariant complement $\mathfrak{m}$ to the isotropy Lie algebra $\mathfrak{k}$ inside the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$, giving a decomposition $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ with $\operatorname{Ad}(K)\mathfrak{m}\subset \mathfrak{m}$. Such a complement $\mathfrak{m}$ is identified with the tangent space $T_oM$ at the origin.

The Riemannian manifold $(M=G/K, g)$ is called a $G$-geodesic orbit space ($G$-g.o.) if every geodesic of $g$ is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$; equivalently, for every $X \in \mathfrak{m}$ there exists $Z \in \mathfrak{k}$ such that $[X+Z,\, X]_{\mathfrak{m}} = 0$ with respect to some (hence any) $\operatorname{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive complement $\mathfrak{m}$.

Problem. Establish criteria, with proofs, that determine when the $G$-g.o. property of a homogeneous Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ is independent of:

(a) the choice of $\operatorname{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive complement $\mathfrak{m}$ in $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ for a fixed presentation $M = G/K$; and

(b) the choice of transitive group of isometries, i.e., when passing from one presentation $(G,K)$ of $(M,g)$ to another presentation $(G',K')$ by a different transitive Lie group $G'$ of isometries of $(M,g)$.

In particular, clarify precisely under what hypotheses the assertion "$(M=G/K,g)$ is $G$-g.o." is invariant under change of reductive complement, when it transfers between distinct transitive isometry groups, and when (and how) it must be reformulated when the presentation changes.

The literature on geodesic orbit (g.o.) manifolds notes that, for a fixed reductive presentation, the g.o. property is intrinsic to the presentation, but a general criterion describing how the $G$-g.o. property behaves under change of transitive isometry group or change of reductive complement is not stated as a settled theorem. Recent surveys and papers (2017–2025) on g.o. manifolds continue to discuss this issue and emphasize the dependence on the presentation, indicating the problem remains open in its general form.

Let $(M=G/H,g)$ be a pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$, $H$ is the isotropy subgroup at a base point $o\in M$, and $g$ is a $G$-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metric. Let $\mathfrak{g}=\mathrm{Lie}(G)$ and $\mathfrak{h}=\mathrm{Lie}(H)$, and (when available) fix a reductive decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$ with $\mathrm{Ad}(H)\mathfrak{m}\subseteq\mathfrak{m}$, so that $\mathfrak{m}$ is identified with $T_oM$ and the metric $g_o$ corresponds to a (possibly indefinite) non-degenerate $\mathrm{Ad}(H)$-invariant scalar product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ on $\mathfrak{m}$.

A smooth curve $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=o$ is called a homogeneous geodesic if it is an orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$, i.e. $\gamma(t)=\exp(tZ)\cdot o$ for some $Z\in\mathfrak{g}$, and if it is a geodesic of $g$ up to a possibly non-affine reparametrization (this last freedom being needed because a null orbit curve may be a geodesic only after reparametrization).

Solve the following two problems.

(1) (Single-exponential criterion.) Find necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions on $a\in\mathfrak{h}$ and $x\in\mathfrak{m}$ such that the curve
$$\gamma(t)=\exp\bigl(t(a+x)\bigr)\cdot o$$
is, after possibly a non-affine reparametrization, a geodesic of $(M,g)$. The conditions should be expressed purely in terms of the Lie brackets in $\mathfrak{g}$, the projection $\mathfrak{g}\to\mathfrak{m}$, and the scalar product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$, and must reduce, in the Riemannian (positive definite) case, to the classical Kowalski–Vanhecke geodesic lemma:
$$\langle [a+x,y]_\mathfrak{m},x\rangle=0\quad\text{for all } y\in\mathfrak{m}.$$
The pseudo-Riemannian formulation must explicitly allow for a constant $k=k(x)\in\mathbb{R}$ accounting for the case where the orbit parameter $t$ is not an affine parameter of $\gamma$, which can occur when $x$ is null.

(2) (Triple-exponential criterion.) Find necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions on $X,Y,Z\in\mathfrak{g}$ such that the curve
$$\gamma(t)=\exp(tX)\exp(tY)\exp(tZ)\cdot o$$
is, after possibly a non-affine reparametrization, a geodesic of $(M,g)$. The conditions must reduce, in the Riemannian case, to the known algebraic test for three-exponential homogeneous geodesics, and must account for the same non-affine-parameter phenomenon for null orbits.

A pseudo-Riemannian "geodesic lemma" for single one-parameter orbits γ(t)=exp(t(a+x)).o has been established by Dušek and others, in which a constant k=k(x) accommodating the non-affine parameter on null orbits explicitly appears; existence of at least one homogeneous geodesic through each point of a reductive pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous space is also known in the affine setting, although general existence remains subtle. The analogous algebraic criterion for triple-exponential curves exp(tX)exp(tY)exp(tZ).o in full pseudo-Riemannian generality does not appear to be established in the literature in the same complete form as in the Riemannian case, so the program is partially solved.

Let $(M = G/H, g)$ be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$ and $H$ is the isotropy subgroup at a chosen origin $o \in M$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ denote the Lie algebra of $G$. A geodesic $\gamma$ of $M$ through $o$ is called a homogeneous geodesic if it is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$, i.e. $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX) \cdot o$ for some $X \in \mathfrak{g}$. The manifold $(M,g)$ is called a g.o. space if every geodesic through $o$ is homogeneous in this sense.

More generally, a geodesic through $o$ is called a $k$-step homogeneous geodesic if it admits a representation of the form
$$\gamma(t) = \exp(tX_1)\exp(tX_2)\cdots\exp(tX_k) \cdot o$$
for some $X_1, \ldots, X_k \in \mathfrak{g}$. In particular, a two-step homogeneous geodesic is one of the form $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\exp(tY)\cdot o$ with $X,Y \in \mathfrak{g}$, and $(M,g)$ is called a two-step g.o. space if every geodesic through $o$ admits such a two-step representation.

Determine whether the following holds: for every homogeneous Riemannian manifold $(G/H, g)$ and every geodesic through $o$ that admits a $k$-step homogeneous representation with $k \geq 3$, there exist $X, Y \in \mathfrak{g}$ such that the same geodesic admits the two-step representation $\gamma(t) = \exp(tX)\exp(tY)\cdot o$. Equivalently, decide whether the study of $k$-step homogeneous geodesics (for $k \geq 3$) can always be reduced to the study of two-step homogeneous geodesics.

Let $(M=G/H, \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ be a connected pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$ and $H$ is the isotropy subgroup at a base point $o\in M$. Assume the homogeneous space is reductive, so that the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$ admits an $\mathrm{Ad}(H)$-invariant decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$, with $\mathfrak{h}=\mathrm{Lie}(H)$ and $\mathfrak{m}$ canonically identified with $T_oM$ in such a way that $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ corresponds to a (possibly indefinite) nondegenerate $\mathrm{Ad}(H)$-invariant symmetric bilinear form on $\mathfrak{m}$.

A smooth curve $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to M$ is called a two-step homogeneous geodesic through $o$ if it is a geodesic of the Levi-Civita connection and there exist $X,Y\in\mathfrak{g}$ such that
$$\gamma(t)=\exp(tX)\exp(tY)\cdot o\quad\text{for all }t\in\mathbb{R}.$$

Develop a systematic theory of two-step homogeneous geodesics in this pseudo-Riemannian setting. In particular, establish a pseudo-Riemannian geodesic lemma giving necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions on $X,Y\in\mathfrak{g}$ (in terms of the bracket structure of $\mathfrak{g}$, the decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$, and the invariant bilinear form on $\mathfrak{m}$) for the curve $\gamma(t)=\exp(tX)\exp(tY)\cdot o$ to be a geodesic of $M$.

Let $G$ be a connected semisimple linear algebraic group defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $\Gamma \subset G(\mathbb{R})$ be an arithmetic lattice, and let $A \subset G(\mathbb{R})$ be a maximal $\mathbb{R}$-split torus. A trajectory $\{a_t \cdot x : t \in D\}$ in $G(\mathbb{R})/\Gamma$ under the action of a closed cone $D \subset A$ is called divergent if for every compact subset $K \subset G(\mathbb{R})/\Gamma$, the set $\{t \in D : a_t \cdot x \in K\}$ is bounded. A divergent trajectory is called obvious if its divergence is accounted for by a finite explicit collection of algebraic data (for instance, when the trajectory is contained in, or asymptotic to, a closed orbit of a proper $\mathbb{Q}$-parabolic subgroup); otherwise it is called non-obvious.

Construct explicit examples of closed cones $D \subset A$ with $\dim D \geq 3$ such that the action of $D$ on $G(\mathbb{R})/\Gamma$ admits no non-obvious divergent trajectories, or prove that no such examples exist.

Let G/K be a compact homogeneous space with reductive decomposition g = k ⊕ m. Assume that the tangent module m decomposes as an orthogonal (with respect to the negative of the Killing form B of g) direct sum

  m = m_1 ⊕ m_2 ⊕ m_3

of three Ad(K)-invariant irreducible submodules satisfying [m_i, m_i] ⊆ k for i = 1, 2, 3. Such a space is called a generalized Wallach space. For positive parameters λ_1, λ_2, λ_3 > 0, consider the G-invariant Riemannian metric on G/K corresponding to the inner product

  ⟨ , ⟩ = λ_1 (−B)|_{m_1} + λ_2 (−B)|_{m_2} + λ_3 (−B)|_{m_3}.

A nonzero vector X ∈ m is called a geodesic vector if the curve γ(t) = exp(tX) · o is a geodesic of (G/K, ⟨ , ⟩); equivalently, ⟨[X, Y]_m, X⟩ = 0 for all Y ∈ m, where [·,·]_m denotes the m-component.

A generalized Wallach space is said to be of type 2 if exactly two of the structure constants
  a_i = (1/d_i) ∑ B([e^i_α, e^j_β], [e^i_α, e^k_γ])  (for {i,j,k} = {1,2,3})
coincide, and of type 3 if all three are distinct.

Problem: For every generalized Wallach space of type 2 or type 3, and for every choice of positive parameters (λ_1, λ_2, λ_3) with at least two of the λ_i distinct, determine all geodesic vectors X = X_1 + X_2 + X_3 ∈ m (X_i ∈ m_i) by solving, or otherwise explicitly characterizing the solution set of, the corresponding system of dim(m_1) + dim(m_2) + dim(m_3) quadratic equations expressing the geodesic vector condition.

The problem of explicitly determining all homogeneous geodesics on generalized Wallach spaces of types 2 and 3 with arbitrary invariant metric parameters appears to remain open. While the classification of generalized Wallach spaces that are g.o. spaces (i.e., where all geodesics are homogeneous) has been carried out, and homogeneous geodesics have been studied in particular examples such as SU(2) and the Stiefel manifold SO(4)/SO(2), no general solution of the full system of quadratic equations for geodesic vectors in the type 2 / type 3 cases with generic positive (λ_1, λ_2, λ_3) is reported in the literature; the problem is described as not easy in general.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem—commonly called the Jones unknot problem—remains open. It has been verified that every prime knot with up to 24 crossings has non-trivial Jones polynomial, and Khovanov homology is known to detect the unknot (Kronheimer–Mrowka), but whether the Jones polynomial itself detects the unknot is still unresolved as of 2025; even the 4-strand braid case is open.

Let X be a smooth projective complex variety. Let BU denote the classifying space of the infinite unitary group, realized as the direct limit of complex Grassmannians Gr_k(C^n) (over k and n). A holomorphic map X → BU is, in this realization, equivalent to a holomorphic vector bundle on X together with a holomorphic embedding into a trivial bundle. Let Hol(X, BU) denote the space of such holomorphic maps, topologized in the usual way, and let Hol(X, BU)^+ denote its Quillen–Segal group completion (with respect to the H-space structure coming from direct sum of bundles / block-sum on Grassmannians). The natural inclusion of holomorphic maps into continuous maps induces a map

    φ_X : Hol(X, BU)^+ → Map(X, BU),

where Map(X, BU) is the space of continuous maps with the compact-open topology. The homotopy groups of Hol(X, BU)^+ define the "holomorphic K-theory" of X, while those of Map(X, BU) define its topological K-theory.

Problem: Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the smooth projective variety X under which the comparison map φ_X : Hol(X, BU)^+ → Map(X, BU) is a homotopy equivalence.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The comparison map between holomorphic (semi-topological) K-theory and topological K-theory has been studied extensively by Friedlander–Walker, Cohen–Lima-Filho, and others. After inverting the Bott class one obtains a rational isomorphism, and certain special cases (curves, P^n, some flag varieties) are known to yield equivalences. However, a general necessary-and-sufficient characterization of smooth projective varieties X for which Hol(X,BU)^+ → Map(X,BU) is a homotopy equivalence does not appear in the literature; the problem appears to remain open.

Let $S^4$ denote the smooth 4-dimensional sphere. A Riemannian metric $g$ on a smooth manifold $M$ is called Einstein if its Ricci tensor satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = \lambda\, g$ for some constant $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$. Two metrics $g_1, g_2$ on $S^4$ are considered equivalent up to diffeomorphism if there exists a diffeomorphism $\varphi : S^4 \to S^4$ and a positive constant $c > 0$ such that $\varphi^* g_2 = c\, g_1$.

Question: Is the round (standard) metric on $S^4$ the unique Einstein metric on $S^4$, up to diffeomorphism and rescaling? Equivalently, must every Einstein metric on $S^4$ be isometric (after rescaling) to the round metric of constant sectional curvature?

Consider the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations governing a polytropic ideal gas:
  ρ_t + (ρ u)_x = 0,
  (ρ u)_t + (ρ u^2 + p)_x = 0,
  (ρ E)_t + (u(ρ E + p))_x = 0,
where ρ>0 is the density, u the velocity, E = e + u^2/2 the specific total energy, and the pressure obeys the polytropic law p = (γ−1) ρ e with adiabatic exponent γ>1, supplemented with initial data (ρ_0, u_0, e_0). Consider also the corresponding compressible Navier–Stokes system with viscosity coefficient μ>0 and heat conductivity κ>0:
  ρ_t + (ρ u)_x = 0,
  (ρ u)_t + (ρ u^2 + p)_x = μ u_{xx},
  (ρ E)_t + (u(ρ E + p))_x = (μ u u_x + κ θ_x)_x,
with the same initial data, where θ denotes absolute temperature linked to e by the polytropic constitutive relation.

Suppose (ρ, u, e) is a weak solution of the Euler Cauchy problem that arises as a limit, in some appropriate (e.g. distributional or L^p_{loc}) topology, of solutions (ρ^{μ,κ}, u^{μ,κ}, e^{μ,κ}) of the Navier–Stokes system as (μ, κ) → 0 along some sequence (with κ/μ in a physically reasonable range).

(a) Show that (ρ, u, e) is the unique entropy-admissible weak solution of the Euler Cauchy problem in a suitable admissible class.
(b) As a weaker assertion, show that (ρ, u, e) is unique within the class of weak solutions of the Euler Cauchy problem that can be realized as such a zero-dissipation limit of the compressible Navier–Stokes system.

Recent literature establishes existence of weak entropy solutions of the 1D compressible Euler equations for polytropic gases as vanishing-viscosity limits of Navier–Stokes systems (typically with density-dependent viscosity), via compensated compactness. However, no result asserts uniqueness of such limits as entropy-admissible weak solutions for general large initial data, nor uniqueness within the restricted class of zero-dissipation limits. The problem appears to remain open in both formulations.

Consider the one-dimensional full compressible Euler equations for a polytropic fluid:
   ρ_t + (ρu)_x = 0,
   (ρu)_t + (ρu^2 + p)_x = 0,
   (ρE)_t + (u(ρE + p))_x = 0,
where ρ > 0 is density, u is velocity, E = e + u^2/2 is total specific energy, e is specific internal energy, and the equation of state is that of a polytropic gas, p = (γ−1)ρe with adiabatic exponent γ > 1, and the temperature/entropy is determined accordingly. Let V(x,t) = (ρ,u,E)(x,t) be a weak solution of this system in the sense of distributions, with V ∈ BV_loc (functions of locally bounded variation in (x,t)), satisfying the physical (Clausius–Duhem) entropy inequality
   (ρS)_t + (ρuS)_x ≥ 0
in the sense of distributions, where S is the thermodynamic specific entropy.

Question: What additional local structural properties must V(x,t) possess in (x,t)-space beyond those guaranteed by membership in BV alone? In particular:
(a) Around almost every point (x_0, t_0), can V be described locally as a suitable perturbation of a self-similar Riemann solution (i.e., does V locally look like the solution to a Riemann problem with constant left/right states, in the sense established for Glimm-type front-tracking solutions)?
(b) Is every such V necessarily a viscosity solution in the Bianchini–Bressan sense, i.e., obtainable as the limit, as ε → 0+, of solutions V^ε to the parabolic regularization V^ε_t + F(V^ε)_x = ε V^ε_{xx}?

Provide either a proof that every BV entropy solution admits such a local structure / viscosity-solution characterization, or a counterexample.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The fine local structure of BV entropy solutions to the full compressible Euler equations, and whether they coincide with vanishing-viscosity (Bianchini–Bressan) solutions, remains a recognized open problem. Bianchini–Bressan (2005) established the viscosity-solution theory for small-BV solutions of general strictly hyperbolic systems with artificial viscosity, but the corresponding theory for physical viscosity (Navier–Stokes) and the local Riemann-type structure for general BV entropy solutions of the full Euler system are still open.

Consider the compressible Euler equations in $d \ge 2$ space dimensions for an ideal gas:
\[
\partial_t \rho + \nabla\cdot(\rho u) = 0, \qquad \partial_t(\rho u) + \nabla\cdot(\rho u\otimes u) + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \partial_t E + \nabla\cdot((E+p)u) = 0,
\]
where $\rho>0$ is the density, $u\in\mathbb{R}^d$ the velocity, $p$ the pressure, and $E=\tfrac12\rho|u|^2+\rho e$ the total energy, with an equation of state $p=p(\rho,e)$ (e.g.\ polytropic $p=(\gamma-1)\rho e$, $\gamma>1$). A weak solution is a locally integrable triple $(\rho,u,e)$ satisfying these equations in the sense of distributions and an admissibility (entropy) inequality of the form $\partial_t(\rho s)+\nabla\cdot(\rho s u)\ge 0$ for an appropriate entropy $s$.

Develop a well-posedness theory for physically relevant weak solutions of this system. Specifically:
(a) Identify a function space $X$ of initial data and a corresponding solution space in which existence (even short-time) and/or uniqueness of weak admissible solutions can be established.
(b) Describe the geometric structure of generic discontinuities (shocks, contact discontinuities, vortex sheets) in such weak solutions and the manner in which linear and nonlinear waves evolve and interact.
(c) Formulate the correct entropy/admissibility conditions that single out physically relevant solutions and rule out the non-uniqueness phenomena produced by convex integration.
(d) Determine whether planar shock waves and centered rarefaction waves are asymptotically stable under multidimensional, non-planar perturbations.
(e) Determine conditions under which the solution operator (initial data $\mapsto$ solution at time $t$) is compact on $X$.

The multidimensional well-posedness theory for the compressible Euler equations is widely regarded as one of the central open problems in mathematical fluid dynamics. Recent work using convex integration (De Lellis–Székelyhidi, Chiodaroli, Buckmaster and collaborators) has shown non-uniqueness of bounded admissible weak solutions, deepening rather than resolving the problem; stability of planar shocks/rarefactions under multi-D perturbations and the search for adequate function spaces and entropy criteria remain active areas of research as of 2026.

Consider the compressible Navier–Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\ge 2$,
$$\partial_t \rho + \operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0,\qquad \partial_t(\rho u)+\operatorname{div}(\rho u\otimes u)+\nabla p(\rho)=\mu\Delta u+(\mu+\lambda)\nabla\operatorname{div} u,$$
(possibly augmented by an energy equation when temperature is included), where $\rho>0$ is the density, $u\in\mathbb{R}^d$ the velocity, $p$ a smooth pressure law with $p'(\rho)>0$, and $\mu>0$, $2\mu+\lambda>0$ the viscosity coefficients. A planar viscous shock profile is a traveling-wave solution of the form $(\rho,u)(t,x)=(\bar\rho,\bar u)(x_1-st)$ connecting two distinct Rankine–Hugoniot–compatible end states $(\rho_\pm,u_\pm)$. A planar viscous rarefaction wave is the self-similar smooth solution of the corresponding one-dimensional problem associated to a genuinely nonlinear rarefaction Riemann data, lifted to $\mathbb{R}^d$ as a function of $x_1/t$. A planar viscous contact wave is the diffusive profile associated to a linearly degenerate Riemann discontinuity in the one-dimensional system.

(a) Prove or disprove that each of these basic planar wave patterns (viscous shock profile, viscous rarefaction wave, viscous contact wave) is nonlinearly asymptotically stable in $\mathbb{R}^d$ under generic small multidimensional perturbations of the initial data—i.e., perturbations depending on all variables $(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$, not merely on $x_1$, and not subject to zero-mass or other artificial restrictions.

(b) For initial data that are small multidimensional perturbations of such a wave pattern, determine the leading-order (and, if possible, higher-order) large-time asymptotic ansatz describing the solution as $t\to\infty$, including the precise shifts, modulations, and dispersive/diffusive corrections needed to capture the asymptotics.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Significant recent progress exists. Nonlinear stability of planar viscous shock waves for the 3D compressible Navier–Stokes equations under generic multidimensional perturbations (without zero-mass condition) has been established via a-contraction with time-dependent shift methods (Kang–Vasseur–Wang, JEMS, arXiv:2204.09428), and related results cover Navier–Stokes–Poisson and relaxed systems, as well as planar shocks with spatial oscillations. Multidimensional stability of large-amplitude profiles, the full picture for rarefaction and contact waves under generic multi-D perturbations, and precise higher-order asymptotic ansätze remain incompletely resolved, so the problem is partially solved.

Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations
   ∂_t u + (u·∇)u + ∇p = 0,   div u = 0,   x ∈ ℝ², t > 0,
with vortex-sheet initial data, i.e. an initial velocity u₀ ∈ L²_loc(ℝ²) that is divergence free and whose vorticity ω₀ = curl u₀ is a finite Radon measure on ℝ² (possibly without a distinguished sign). A weak solution is a divergence-free u ∈ L^∞_t L²_loc satisfying the Euler equations in the sense of distributions; this is called a classical weak solution if the nonlinear term u⊗u is locally integrable and the equations hold in the standard distributional sense (rather than only as a measure-valued solution in the sense of DiPerna–Majda).

Address the following:

(a) For every vortex-sheet initial datum u₀ as above (in particular without any sign assumption on ω₀), does there exist a global-in-time classical weak solution u of the 2D Euler equations with u|_{t=0} = u₀?

(b) Is such a weak solution unique within a natural class (extending Yudovich's uniqueness theorem for ω₀ ∈ L^∞ to vortex-sheet data)?

(c) Let {u^ε} be a family of approximate solutions obtained either by vanishing-viscosity (Navier–Stokes) approximation or by a vortex method, with initial data u₀^ε → u₀ strongly in L²_loc. Determine whether energy concentration can develop dynamically for t > 0 (i.e. whether |u^ε|² can converge in the sense of measures to a limit possessing a singular part supported on a set of Lebesgue measure zero), and characterize the relation of this phenomenon to concentration–cancellation, namely the property that u^ε ⊗ u^ε converges in the sense of distributions to u ⊗ u despite possible loss of strong compactness.

Consider the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (or on the torus $\mathbb{T}^3$):
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \nu\Delta u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,$$
with viscosity $\nu>0$, where $u:[0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$ is the velocity field and $p$ is the pressure. Address the following questions.

(a) Global regularity. Given an arbitrary divergence-free initial datum $u_0\in C^\infty$ (with suitable decay at infinity, or periodic), does there exist a smooth solution $u\in C^\infty([0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^3)$ to the above system with $u(0,\cdot)=u_0$? Equivalently, can smooth finite-energy data develop a singularity in finite time?

(b) Long-time asymptotics. Describe the asymptotic behavior of Leray–Hopf weak solutions (or smooth solutions when they exist) as $t\to\infty$, both in two and three dimensions.

(c) High Reynolds number asymptotics. Describe the asymptotic behavior of solutions as the Reynolds number $Re = 1/\nu \to \infty$, in particular when the formal limit (Euler) solution develops singularities.

(d) Inertial manifolds. Do the two-dimensional and/or three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations admit a finite-dimensional inertial manifold, i.e. a finite-dimensional smooth invariant manifold in phase space which is exponentially attracting and contains the global attractor?

(e) Prandtl boundary layer theory. In a domain with boundary and no-slip boundary condition, as $\nu\to 0$, is Prandtl's boundary-layer ansatz mathematically justified for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, i.e. can the vanishing viscosity limit be rigorously described by an outer Euler flow matched to an inner Prandtl boundary-layer profile?

The global regularity question for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations is one of the seven Clay Millennium Prize Problems and remains open. The related questions on long-time and high-Reynolds-number asymptotics, existence of inertial manifolds for 2D and 3D Navier-Stokes (3D inertial manifold existence is widely open; even in 2D existence of a classical inertial manifold remains unresolved), and the rigorous validity of Prandtl boundary-layer theory for incompressible flows are all recognized as outstanding open problems in mathematical fluid dynamics as of 2026.

Consider the nonlinear Boltzmann equation
  ∂_t F + v · ∇_x F = (1/ε) Q(F,F),
for the one-particle distribution F(t,x,v) ≥ 0 with x in a domain Ω ⊂ R^d (possibly with boundary ∂Ω on which a kinetic boundary condition such as diffuse reflection or specular reflection is prescribed), v ∈ R^d, and collision operator Q corresponding to a physical interaction (e.g. hard spheres or a hard/soft potential with angular cutoff). Here ε > 0 is the Knudsen number.

In the hydrodynamic (small-Knudsen) limit ε → 0, the macroscopic fields (density, momentum, temperature) of F are formally governed by the compressible Euler equations, whose solutions may develop shock discontinuities and which must be supplemented by boundary conditions at ∂Ω. Near shock hypersurfaces and near ∂Ω one expects thin transition regions — shock layers (of width O(ε)) and Knudsen boundary layers (of width O(ε)) — across which F is not close to a local Maxwellian.

Develop a rigorous mathematical theory of these layers for the full nonlinear Boltzmann equation. Specifically:

(a) Construct matched asymptotic expansions of solutions F^ε in the limit ε → 0, consisting of an interior (Hilbert/Chapman–Enskog) expansion away from shocks and boundaries, together with shock-layer expansions (of travelling-wave type) attached to each Euler shock and boundary-layer expansions (of Knudsen-layer type) attached to ∂Ω, with appropriate matching conditions tying together the inner and outer expansions.

(b) Prove convergence of true solutions F^ε of the nonlinear Boltzmann equation to the composite asymptotic expansion as ε → 0, with quantitative error estimates in suitable norms, thereby justifying the fluid-dynamic approximation by the compressible Euler equations in the presence of both shocks and physical boundaries.

Is such a rigorous theory — formal construction together with convergence proof — achievable for the genuine (non-model) nonlinear Boltzmann equation?

Substantial partial progress has been made. For the Broadwell and other discrete-velocity models, boundary-layer and shock-layer fluid-dynamic limits are established (Caflisch–Nicolaenko, Xin and collaborators). For the full nonlinear Boltzmann equation with hard-sphere or soft-potential collisions, hydrodynamic limits to the compressible Euler equations have been justified for smooth flows, with shock waves (Yu, 2005; Huang–Wang–Wang–Yang), with contact discontinuities, with rarefaction waves, and for stationary boundary-layer (Milne) problems (Esposito–Guo–Kim–Marra). However, a complete unified theory combining matched asymptotic expansions and convergence in the presence of both shocks and physical boundaries for the general nonlinear Boltzmann equation remains incomplete.

Consider the nonlinear Boltzmann equation
  ∂_t f + v · ∇_x f = Q(f, f),    (t,x,v) ∈ (0,∞) × ℝ^d_x × ℝ^d_v,
where Q(f,f) is the standard Boltzmann collision operator
  Q(f,f)(v) = ∫_{ℝ^d} ∫_{S^{d-1}} B(v−v_*, σ) [ f(v')f(v'_*) − f(v)f(v_*) ] dσ dv_*,
with pre/post-collisional velocities v' = (v+v_*)/2 + |v−v_*|σ/2, v'_* = (v+v_*)/2 − |v−v_*|σ/2 and a physical collision kernel B ≥ 0.

A nonnegative function f ∈ C([0,∞); L^1_{loc}(ℝ^d_x × ℝ^d_v)) is a renormalized weak solution in the DiPerna–Lions sense if for every β ∈ C^1([0,∞)) with β'(s)(1+s) bounded one has, in the sense of distributions,
  ∂_t β(f) + v · ∇_x β(f) = β'(f) Q(f,f),
with finite mass, energy and entropy initially, and Q(f,f)/(1+f) ∈ L^1_{loc}.

(a) Establish a quantitative regularity theory for such renormalized weak solutions: identify a functional space (e.g. Sobolev, Besov, or fractional regularity in x and/or v) in which an arbitrary global renormalized solution must lie, given only finite mass, energy and entropy of the initial datum, for a general physically admissible collision kernel B (both cutoff and non-cutoff cases).

(b) Using such regularity, give a rigorous derivation of the hydrodynamic limit: prove that, under the appropriate diffusive (or other) scaling f_ε of renormalized solutions with mean free path ε → 0, the suitably rescaled fluctuations of f_ε converge to a weak solution of the corresponding macroscopic fluid system (incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier, incompressible Euler, or compressible Euler) without smallness or near-equilibrium assumptions.

The hydrodynamic limit toward the incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier system from DiPerna–Lions renormalized solutions has been rigorously established (Golse–Saint-Raymond, and extensions to bounded domains by Masmoudi–Saint-Raymond, etc.). Some velocity-regularization/compactness results exist for non-cutoff kernels (Alexandre–Desvillettes–Villani–Wennberg, and Chen–Desvillettes for long-range interactions). However, the full regularity theory for arbitrary renormalized solutions and rigorous derivation of the incompressible/compressible Euler limits in this generality remain open. Thus the problem is partially solved.

Let X be a smooth projective complex algebraic variety. Consider the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence
  E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, K^q(pt)) ⇒ K^{p+q}(X)
from singular cohomology to topological K-theory, with its successive differentials d_r (r ≥ 2). For each codimension-p algebraic cycle Z on X, the cohomology class cl(Z) ∈ H^{2p}(X, Z) is of Hodge type (p,p) and is annihilated by all differentials d_r of this spectral sequence.

Question: Let c ∈ H^{2p}(X, Z) be an integral cohomology class whose image in H^{2p}(X, C) lies in the (p,p)-component of the Hodge decomposition, and which is killed by every differential d_r of the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence. Must c be expressible as a Z-linear combination
  c = Σ n_i · cl(Z_i)
of classes of codimension-p algebraic subvarieties Z_i of X?
representations.original:
Let X be a smooth projective complex algebraic variety. Consider the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence
  E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, K^q(pt)) ⇒ K^{p+q}(X)
from singular cohomology to topological K-theory, with its successive differentials d_r (r ≥ 2). For each codimension-p algebraic cycle Z on X, the cohomology class cl(Z) ∈ H^{2p}(X, Z) is of Hodge type (p,p) and is annihilated by all differentials d_r of this spectral sequence.

Question: Let c ∈ H^{2p}(X, Z) be an integral cohomology class whose image in H^{2p}(X, C) lies in the (p,p)-component of the Hodge decomposition, and which is killed by every differential d_r of the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence. Must c be expressible as a Z-linear combination
  c = Σ n_i · cl(Z_i)
of classes of codimension-p algebraic subvarieties Z_i of X?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The statement is a well-known refinement of the integral Hodge conjecture due to Atiyah–Hirzebruch and revisited by Totaro. While the integral Hodge conjecture itself has many counterexamples (Atiyah–Hirzebruch torsion classes, Kollár hypersurfaces, Benoist–Ottem Enriques threefolds, etc.), all known counterexamples are obstructed precisely by some Atiyah–Hirzebruch (or cobordism) differential. No counterexample is known to the refined statement that integral (p,p) classes lying in the kernel of every d_r are algebraic, and standard references (nLab, surveys on the Hodge conjecture, Totaro's work) record this as an open problem.

representations.normalized:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex algebraic variety, and let $p$ be an integer with $0 \le p \le \dim X$. The singular cohomology $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ maps to $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{C})$, which carries the Hodge decomposition $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{C}) = \bigoplus_{r+s=2p} H^{r,s}(X)$. An integral $(p,p)$-class is an element of
\[ \mathrm{Hdg}^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z}) := \{\alpha \in H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z}) : \alpha_{\mathbb{C}} \in H^{p,p}(X)\}. \]
A codimension-$p$ algebraic cycle on $X$ is a finite formal $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$-linear combination $Z = \sum_i n_i Z_i$ of closed irreducible subvarieties $Z_i \subset X$ of codimension $p$ (with non-negative integer coefficients $n_i \ge 0$); its cohomology class $\mathrm{cl}(Z) \in H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ lies in $\mathrm{Hdg}^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$. Call a class $\alpha \in \mathrm{Hdg}^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ effective if $\alpha = \mathrm{cl}(Z)$ for some such (non-negative) codimension-$p$ algebraic cycle $Z$, as opposed to a difference $\mathrm{cl}(Z_1) - \mathrm{cl}(Z_2)$ of two such classes.

Problem: Characterize, intrinsically in terms of Hodge-theoretic or cohomological data, the subset of effective classes inside the cone of those integral $(p,p)$-classes on $X$ that arise as integral linear combinations of classes of codimension-$p$ algebraic cycles. In particular, give a necessary and sufficient criterion to decide, for a given $\alpha \in \mathrm{Hdg}^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ that is known to be an integral combination of algebraic cycle classes, whether $\alpha$ is effective in the strong sense $\alpha = \mathrm{cl}(Z)$ for a single (non-negative) codimension-$p$ cycle $Z$.

The question of which integral (p,p)-classes are effective in the strong sense of being represented by a single codimension-p algebraic cycle (rather than a difference of such cycles) is widely regarded as open. representations.normalized:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex algebraic variety, and fix an integer $p$ with $0 \le p \le \dim X$. Consider the singular cohomology group $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ and its image in $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{C})$, which has a Hodge decomposition $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{C}) = \bigoplus_{r+s=2p} H^{r,s}(X)$. Let $\mathrm{Hg}^p(X) \subset H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ denote the group of integral classes whose image in $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{C})$ lies in $H^{p,p}(X)$ (the Hodge classes of codimension $p$). Define the intermediate Jacobian
$$J^p(X)^0 = \frac{H^{2p-1}(X,\mathbb{C})}{F^p H^{2p-1}(X,\mathbb{C}) + H^{2p-1}(X,\mathbb{Z})},$$
where $F^p$ denotes the Hodge filtration. Let $J^p(X)$ be the complex Lie group fitting in the extension
$$0 \longrightarrow J^p(X)^0 \longrightarrow J^p(X) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Hg}^p(X) \longrightarrow 0.$$
A codimension-$p$ algebraic cycle on $X$ that is homologous to zero has an Abel–Jacobi image in $J^p(X)^0$, and an arbitrary codimension-$p$ algebraic cycle has a class in $J^p(X)$ lifting its cohomology class. Let $A^p(X) \subseteq J^p(X)$ be the subgroup generated by the classes of all codimension-$p$ algebraic cycles on $X$.

Problem: Give an intrinsic description (in Hodge-theoretic or geometric terms) of the subgroup $A^p(X)$ inside $J^p(X)$. Equivalently, characterize which elements of $J^p(X)$ are represented by $\mathbb{Z}$-linear combinations of codimension-$p$ algebraic cycles on $X$.

For a positive integer $n$, let $s(n) = \sum_{d \mid n,\, 1 \le d < n} d$ denote the sum of the proper divisors of $n$, and set $s(0) = 0$. For a positive integer $n$, define the aliquot sequence starting at $n$ by $a_0 = n$ and $a_{k+1} = s(a_k)$ for $k \ge 0$.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $n$, the sequence $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ is bounded.
representations.original:
For a positive integer $n$, let $s(n) = \sum_{d \mid n,\, 1 \le d < n} d$ denote the sum of the proper divisors of $n$, and set $s(0) = 0$. For a positive integer $n$, define the aliquot sequence starting at $n$ by $a_0 = n$ and $a_{k+1} = s(a_k)$ for $k \ge 0$.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $n$, the sequence $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ is bounded.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

This is the Catalan–Dickson conjecture (Catalan 1888, refined by Dickson 1913), asserting every aliquot sequence is bounded. The problem remains open. The smallest starting value whose behavior is unresolved is 276, which has been iterated for thousands of steps without termination or detection of a cycle. Guy and Selfridge have conjectured the opposite, that some aliquot sequences are unbounded.

Let $f : X \to S$ be a smooth projective morphism of algebraic varieties defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, the algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{C}$, so that $(X_s)_{s\in S}$ is an algebraic family of smooth projective varieties. Fix a base point $0 \in S(\mathbb{C})$ and an integral cohomology class $\alpha \in H^{2p}(X_0, \mathbb{Z})$. For each $s \in S(\mathbb{C})$, the singular cohomology $H^{2p}(X_s, \mathbb{C})$ carries the Hodge decomposition $\bigoplus_{i+j=2p} H^{i,j}(X_s)$; one says that a class in $H^{2p}(X_s, \mathbb{Z})$ is of type $(p,p)$ at $s$ if its image in $H^{2p}(X_s, \mathbb{C})$ lies in $H^{p,p}(X_s)$. Using parallel transport via the Gauss–Manin connection along paths in $S$, the class $\alpha$ determines a (multi-valued) section of the local system $R^{2p}f_*\mathbb{Z}$, and at each $s \in S$ we may ask whether some parallel transport of $\alpha$ to $X_s$ is of type $(p,p)$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given such data $(f : X \to S, \alpha)$ specified over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, decides whether there exists $s \in S(\mathbb{C})$ at which (some parallel transport of) $\alpha$ becomes a class of type $(p,p)$ on $X_s$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

No algorithm is known to decide whether a given integral cohomology class of a typical fiber in a smooth projective family over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ becomes of Hodge type $(p,p)$ somewhere over the base. The problem is generally regarded as open; while there has been work on computer-assisted exploration of Hodge classes, no decision procedure has been established, and the underlying Hodge conjecture remains an open Millennium Prize Problem.

representations.normalized: Let $\varphi:\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$ denote Euler's totient function, defined by $\varphi(n)=\#\{k\in\mathbb{Z}: 1\le k\le n,\ \gcd(k,n)=1\}$. For a positive integer $m$, let $A(m)=\#\{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}:\varphi(x)=m\}$ denote the number of preimages of $m$ under $\varphi$. Determine whether there exists a positive integer $m$ such that $A(m)=1$; that is, whether the equation $\varphi(x)=m$ has exactly one positive integer solution $x$.
representations.original: Let $\varphi:\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$ denote Euler's totient function, defined by $\varphi(n)=\#\{k\in\mathbb{Z}: 1\le k\le n,\ \gcd(k,n)=1\}$. For a positive integer $m$, let $A(m)=\#\{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}:\varphi(x)=m\}$ denote the number of preimages of $m$ under $\varphi$. Determine whether there exists a positive integer $m$ such that $A(m)=1$; that is, whether the equation $\varphi(x)=m$ has exactly one positive integer solution $x$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

This is Carmichael's totient function conjecture (1907), which asserts that no such $m$ exists, i.e., $A(m)\ne 1$ for every positive integer $m$. It remains a famous open problem. Ford (1998) showed that if a counterexample exists, then $m > 10^{10^{10}}$, and the bound has since been improved, but the conjecture itself is still unresolved.

representations.normalized:
Let $f: \mathcal{X} \to S$ be a smooth projective morphism of smooth complex algebraic varieties defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. For an integer $p \geq 0$, the local system $R^{2p} f_* \mathbb{Z}$ underlies a polarizable variation of Hodge structure of weight $2p$ on $S$. Given a point $s_0 \in S(\mathbb{C})$ and an integral cohomology class $\gamma_0 \in H^{2p}(\mathcal{X}_{s_0}, \mathbb{Z})$ that is of Hodge type $(p,p)$, the associated Hodge locus is the set of points $s \in S(\mathbb{C})$ such that, after parallel transport along some path from $s_0$ to $s$, the class $\gamma_0$ becomes a class of type $(p,p)$ on the fiber $\mathcal{X}_s$. More intrinsically, one defines the Hodge locus $\mathrm{HL}(S, \gamma_0) \subseteq S$ as the union of all components of the locus of Hodge classes (in the relative de Rham bundle) that pass through $(s_0, \gamma_0)$, projected to $S$.

It is known that $\mathrm{HL}(S, \gamma_0)$ is a countable union of closed algebraic subvarieties of $S$ (theorem of Cattani–Deligne–Kaplan). The question is: must every irreducible component of $\mathrm{HL}(S, \gamma_0)$ be defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ as a subvariety of $S$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of whether the Hodge locus, known to be a countable union of algebraic subvarieties by Cattani–Deligne–Kaplan, is necessarily defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ when the family is, remains open in general. Partial results exist (e.g., the locus of Hodge classes in the de Rham bundle has good algebraicity/field-of-definition properties in certain settings, and recent work by Baldi–Klingler–Ullmo and others addresses the structure of the Hodge locus), but the general conjecture that components are defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ has not been established.

representations.normalized: A positive integer n ≥ 2 is called a perfect power if there exist integers a ≥ 1 and k ≥ 2 such that n = a^k. Let 1 < p_1 < p_2 < p_3 < ... be the sequence of all positive perfect powers (with 1 sometimes adjoined) listed in strictly increasing order. Prove or disprove: the consecutive gaps p_{n+1} - p_n tend to infinity as n → ∞. Equivalently, show that for every positive integer N there are only finitely many pairs of perfect powers whose difference equals N.

Let 1 < p_1 < p_2 < p_3 < ... be the sequence of all positive perfect powers (with 1 sometimes adjoined) listed in strictly increasing order. Prove or disprove: the consecutive gaps p_{n+1} - p_n tend to infinity as n → ∞. Equivalently, show that for every positive integer N there are only finitely many pairs of perfect powers whose difference equals N.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Pillai's conjecture (1936/1945), which is equivalent to the statement that gaps between consecutive perfect powers tend to infinity, remains an open problem. Only the special case k = 1 (Catalan's conjecture) has been settled by Mihăilescu (2002). The general statement would follow from the abc conjecture but is not proved.

Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety of complex dimension $N$, and let $\Delta \subset X \times X$ denote the diagonal, which is an algebraic cycle of codimension $N$. Consider its cohomology class $\mathrm{cl}(\Delta) \in H^{2N}(X \times X, \mathbb{Q})$. By the Künneth formula
$$H^{2N}(X \times X, \mathbb{Q}) = \bigoplus_{a+b=2N} H^a(X, \mathbb{Q}) \otimes H^b(X, \mathbb{Q}),$$
the class decomposes as $\mathrm{cl}(\Delta) = \sum_{a+b=2N} \mathrm{cl}(\Delta)_{a,b}$ with $\mathrm{cl}(\Delta)_{a,b} \in H^a(X, \mathbb{Q}) \otimes H^b(X, \mathbb{Q})$. Since the Hodge decomposition is compatible with the Künneth decomposition, each component $\mathrm{cl}(\Delta)_{a,b}$ is a rational Hodge class on $X \times X$.

Question: Is each Künneth component $\mathrm{cl}(\Delta)_{a,b}$ the cohomology class of an algebraic cycle on $X \times X$ with rational coefficients?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

This is Grothendieck's Künneth-type standard conjecture (Conjecture C). It remains open in general; it is implied by the Hodge conjecture in characteristic zero. Known cases include abelian varieties (Šermenev 1974; Deninger–Murre 1991), surfaces, curves, and Hilbert schemes of points on smooth surfaces (de Cataldo–Migliorini 2002).

Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety of complex dimension $N$. Fix an ample line bundle on $X$ and let $\eta \in H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})$ be the cohomology class of a hyperplane section. For each integer $p \geq 0$, the iterated cup product with $\eta^p$ gives the hard Lefschetz isomorphism
$$\eta^p \,:\, H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C}) \longrightarrow H^{N+p}(X,\mathbb{C}).$$
By the Künneth formula, $H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C}) \otimes H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C})$ embeds in $H^{2N-2p}(X \times X, \mathbb{C})$. Let $z \in H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C}) \otimes H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C}) \subset H^{2N-2p}(X \times X, \mathbb{C})$ be the unique class such that the inverse isomorphism $(\eta^p)^{-1} \,:\, H^{N+p}(X,\mathbb{C}) \to H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C})$ is given by the correspondence
$$c \;\longmapsto\; \mathrm{pr}_{1\,!}\bigl(z \cup \mathrm{pr}_2^{*}\, c\bigr),$$
where $\mathrm{pr}_1, \mathrm{pr}_2 : X \times X \to X$ are the two projections. One checks that $z$ is a Hodge class on $X \times X$, i.e. it lies in $H^{2N-2p}(X\times X, \mathbb{Q}) \cap H^{N-p,N-p}(X\times X)$.

Question: Is the class $z$ algebraic? Equivalently, is $z$ a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of cohomology classes of algebraic subvarieties of $X \times X$ of codimension $N-p$?
representations.original:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety of complex dimension $N$. Fix an ample line bundle on $X$ and let $\eta \in H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})$ be the cohomology class of a hyperplane section. For each integer $p \geq 0$, the iterated cup product with $\eta^p$ gives the hard Lefschetz isomorphism
$$\eta^p \,:\, H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C}) \longrightarrow H^{N+p}(X,\mathbb{C}).$$
By the Künneth formula, $H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C}) \otimes H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C})$ embeds in $H^{2N-2p}(X \times X, \mathbb{C})$. Let $z \in H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C}) \otimes H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C}) \subset H^{2N-2p}(X \times X, \mathbb{C})$ be the unique class such that the inverse isomorphism $(\eta^p)^{-1} \,:\, H^{N+p}(X,\mathbb{C}) \to H^{N-p}(X,\mathbb{C})$ is given by the correspondence
$$c \;\longmapsto\; \mathrm{pr}_{1\,!}\bigl(z \cup \mathrm{pr}_2^{*}\, c\bigr),$$
where $\mathrm{pr}_1, \mathrm{pr}_2 : X \times X \to X$ are the two projections. One checks that $z$ is a Hodge class on $X \times X$, i.e. it lies in $H^{2N-2p}(X\times X, \mathbb{Q}) \cap H^{N-p,N-p}(X\times X)$.

Question: Is the class $z$ algebraic? Equivalently, is $z$ a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of cohomology classes of algebraic subvarieties of $X \times X$ of codimension $N-p$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

This is precisely Grothendieck's Lefschetz standard conjecture B (algebraicity of the inverse of the hard Lefschetz operator), which is a special case of the Hodge conjecture. It remains open in general over $\mathbb{C}$. It is known in some cases: for varieties over finite fields (Katz–Messing, via the Weil conjectures), for abelian varieties (Lieberman), for surfaces, and recently for various hyper-Kähler varieties (e.g. OG10-type, certain generalized Kummer deformation types). The general case is widely regarded as still open.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The odd covering problem (Erdős–Selfridge) asking whether a covering system exists with all moduli distinct odd integers greater than 1 remains open. Partial results restrict the structure of any hypothetical such system (e.g., the lcm of the moduli must be divisible by 9 or 15; in the square-free case it must have at least 22 prime divisors), and ongoing work (e.g., 2021 and 2025 preprints) continues to investigate the problem, but no full resolution is known.

Let $\mathbb{F}$ be the algebraic closure of a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, and let $A$ be an abelian variety over $\mathbb{F}$. Suppose $A$ admits two liftings to characteristic $0$: complex abelian varieties $A_1$ and $A_2$ defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, each equipped with an isomorphism whose reduction recovers $A$. Recall that a Hodge class on a smooth projective complex variety $X$ of dimension $n$ is a class in $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Q}) \cap H^{p,p}(X)$ for some $0 \le p \le n$. Choose Hodge classes $z_1$ on $A_1$ of degree $2p$ and $z_2$ on $A_2$ of complementary degree $2(\dim A - p)$. Fix a prime $\ell$ different from the characteristic of $\mathbb{F}$, and view $z_1$ and $z_2$ as classes in $\ell$-adic cohomology $H^{2p}_{\text{ét}}(A_1,\mathbb{Q}_\ell(p))$ and $H^{2(\dim A - p)}_{\text{ét}}(A_2,\mathbb{Q}_\ell(\dim A - p))$ via the comparison isomorphism with Betti cohomology. Using the smooth and proper reduction maps, transport these classes to $\ell$-adic cohomology classes on $A$, and define $\kappa \in \mathbb{Q}_\ell$ to be their cup-product pushed forward to $H^0$, i.e. the intersection number of the reductions of $z_1$ and $z_2$ over $\mathbb{F}$.

Question: Is $\kappa$ necessarily a rational number, independent of the choices of liftings $A_1, A_2$ and of $\ell$?

This rationality question is a well-known consequence that would follow from the Hodge conjecture (or even from the conjecture that Hodge classes on abelian varieties reduce to algebraic classes in positive characteristic). Let $q$ be a prime power and let $\mathbb{F}$ denote an algebraic closure of $\mathbb{F}_q$. Let $A$ be an abelian variety over $\mathbb{F}$ of dimension $g$, and let $\tilde{A}$ be a lift of $A$ to characteristic zero: that is, a smooth projective abelian scheme $\mathcal{A}$ over the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}$ of some number field (or over a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field contained in $\mathbb{F}$), together with an isomorphism of the special fiber with $A$, and with generic fiber $\tilde{A}$ defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ (embedded in $\mathbb{C}$). Fix a prime $\ell$ different from the residue characteristic.

For any smooth projective variety $X$ over $\mathbb{C}$, a Hodge class of codimension $p$ on $X$ is an element of $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Q}) \cap H^{p,p}(X)$. Via the comparison isomorphism between Betti and $\ell$-adic cohomology, and via the smooth proper base change isomorphism, such a class on $\tilde{A}_{\mathbb{C}}$ yields a class in $H^{2p}_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(A,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)$, which we call the reduction of the Hodge class.

Fix a Hodge class $z_1 \in H^{2p}(\tilde{A}_{\mathbb{C}},\mathbb{Q}) \cap H^{p,p}(\tilde{A}_{\mathbb{C}})$, and let $\bar{z}_1 \in H^{2p}_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(A,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ be its reduction over $\mathbb{F}$. Let $Z$ be an algebraic cycle on $A$ of codimension $g - p$, defined over $\mathbb{F}$, and let $\mathrm{cl}(Z) \in H^{2(g-p)}_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(A,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ be its cycle class. Form the intersection (cup product followed by the trace map)
$$\kappa := \langle \bar{z}_1, \mathrm{cl}(Z) \rangle \in \mathbb{Q}_\ell.$$

Question: Must $\kappa$ always lie in $\mathbb{Q}$, for every choice of $A$, lift $\tilde{A}$, Hodge class $z_1$, and algebraic cycle $Z$ on $A$?

representations.normalized:
Consider configurations of $n$ labeled points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A self-stress on such a configuration is an assignment of real weights $w_{ij}=w_{ji}$ to the pairs $\{i,j\}$ such that, for every $i$,
$$\sum_{j\neq i} w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)=0.$$
The set of all self-stresses on a fixed configuration forms a vector space, called the self-stress fiber of that configuration. Two self-stress fibers (over two configurations) are said to be sign-preservingly equivalent if there exists a linear isomorphism between them that preserves, for each edge $\{i,j\}$, the sign (positive, negative, or zero) of the corresponding stress coefficient.

The configuration space of $n$ labeled points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is stratified by the equivalence relation: two configurations lie in the same stratum if and only if their self-stress fibers are sign-preservingly equivalent, and strata are taken to be the maximal connected subsets with this property.

Problem: For $n=10$, classify all distinct types of strata of the configuration space of $10$ labeled points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ under this equivalence.

Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ labeled vertices. A tensegrity framework on a subgraph $G \subseteq K_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a placement $p=(p_1,\dots,p_n) \in (\mathbb{R}^d)^n$ of the vertices together with the assignment of real "stress" weights $w_{ij}$ to the edges $\{i,j\}\in E(G)$, satisfying the equilibrium condition
$$\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E(G)} w_{ij}\,(p_j - p_i) = 0 \qquad \text{for every vertex } i.$$
For a fixed configuration $p$, the set of all such stresses forms a real vector space $W(G,p)$, the space of self-stresses of $(G,p)$. The configuration space $(\mathbb{R}^d)^n$ is partitioned into strata according to sign-preserving equivalence of the self-stress fibers: two configurations $p$ and $p'$ lie in the same stratum for $G$ if there is a linear isomorphism $W(G,p)\to W(G,p')$ that preserves the sign pattern of every stress on every edge (i.e. the strata record which sign patterns of stresses are realizable for the given placement).

Fix $n$ (and the ambient dimension $d$). Determine all pairs of subgraphs $G_1, G_2 \subseteq K_n$ that induce the same stratification of the configuration space $(\mathbb{R}^d)^n$, i.e. that produce identical partitions into strata in the sense above. Equivalently, classify the equivalence classes of subgraphs of $K_n$ under the relation "induces the same stratification."

representations.normalized:
Setup. Work in the real projective plane. The planar Cayley algebra is the algebraic system whose objects are points and lines and whose basic operations are:
- join: given two distinct points P, Q, the line P ∨ Q passing through them;
- meet: given two distinct lines ℓ, m, their intersection point ℓ ∧ m.

A Cayley algebra system (in finitely many input points) is a finite sequence of such join/meet operations starting from a tuple of input points, producing as outputs certain derived points and lines whose construction may be conditioned on incidence equations among the constructed objects.

A tensegrity framework on a graph G with n vertices is a realization of the n vertices as points p_1, …, p_n in the plane (the edges are drawn as straight segments). The framework admits a non-trivial self-stress (equivalently, lies in the tensegrity stratum of G) if and only if the points (p_1, …, p_n) satisfy certain algebraic conditions on the configuration space (ℝℙ^2)^n. The (closure of the) locus of all such configurations is the tensegrity stratum associated to G.

A Cayley algebra system S is said to define a tensegrity stratum Σ if the set of input configurations for which S can be performed (all required meets/joins exist and all imposed incidence conditions hold) is exactly Σ.

Problem. Give necessary and sufficient conditions under which two planar Cayley algebra systems S_1 and S_2 (possibly using different intermediate constructions and incidence relations) define the same tensegrity stratum. Equivalently, classify planar Cayley algebra systems up to defining the same tensegrity stratum.

Related work (Karpenkov 2017; Karpenkov–Müller 2021) constructs Cayley/Grassmann–Cayley algebra systems describing tensegrity strata in the plane and in higher dimensions, but the classification of equivalent Cayley algebra systems (when two systems define the same stratum) does not appear to have been resolved in subsequent literature. Status: open.

Let G = (V, E) be a finite graph with n vertices and let d ≥ 3 be an integer. A configuration of G in R^d is a map p : V → R^d. A tensegrity (or self-stress) on (G, p) is an assignment of weights w : E → R, one per edge, satisfying the equilibrium condition at every vertex v ∈ V:
  Σ_{u : {u,v} ∈ E} w_{uv} (p(u) − p(v)) = 0.
The configuration space of G in R^d is the space of all maps p : V → R^d (up to a chosen equivalence, e.g. affine or Euclidean), and its tensegrity stratification is the decomposition according to the dimension (and combinatorial type) of the cone of self-stresses W(G, p). In the planar case d = 2, the strata of codimension 1 (and several higher codimension strata) admit explicit descriptions by classical projective geometric conditions on the points p(v) (expressible, for instance, through Cayley-algebra/meet–join operations, with conditions such as "six points lie on a conic" appearing for specific graphs).

Problem. Develop a systematic theory of geometric (projective/incidence) conditions that cut out the strata of the tensegrity stratification of the configuration space of an arbitrary graph G in R^d for d ≥ 3. In particular, for each combinatorial type of self-stress cone, give explicit geometric conditions on the configuration p : V → R^d that characterize membership in the corresponding stratum, generalizing the known planar descriptions to the multidimensional setting.

Searches indicate that geometric conditions defining strata of tensegrity configuration spaces are well-studied only in the planar case (via Cayley/meet-join expressions, conics, Pascal-type theorems). In dimensions d ≥ 3 the literature explicitly states that almost nothing is known, and no systematic theory of stratum-defining geometric conditions has been developed. The problem appears to remain open.

Consider a continuum robot whose body consists of n flexible rods driven at their proximal ends by prescribed axial displacements u = (u_1, …, u_n) ∈ U ⊂ ℝ^n. Under a Cosserat-rod (or equivalent constant-curvature) model, the forward kinematic map F : U → SE(3) sends each input vector u to the pose F(u) = (R(u), p(u)) of the robot's end effector, where R(u) ∈ SO(3) and p(u) ∈ ℝ^3. Because of unmodeled effects (rod elasticity, friction, manufacturing tolerances, external loads), the physically realized map F̃ differs from the nominal model F by an unknown positioning error e(u) = p̃(u) − p(u).

Design a positioning-error compensation scheme, i.e. a correction map C : U × D → U (where D denotes any available calibration or sensor data) with the following properties:

(a) For a desired end-effector position p* in the workspace, the compensated input u_c = C(F^{-1}(p*), D) satisfies
    sup_{p* ∈ W} ‖ p̃(u_c) − p* ‖ ≤ ε,
for a target accuracy ε strictly smaller than the uncompensated error sup_{p* ∈ W} ‖ p̃(F^{-1}(p*)) − p* ‖.

(b) C is computable in real time and stable with respect to perturbations of D.

Provide such a compensation method, prove convergence/error bounds, and characterize the class of error models e(u) for which the method achieves accuracy ε.

Consider families of recogniser P systems (membrane systems) used to decide languages in polynomial time. A recogniser P system has an input membrane, halts on every computation, and outputs either "accept" or "reject". A family {Π(n)}_{n∈ℕ} of such P systems is called:

- confluent if, for every input, every computation of the corresponding P system halts and all halting computations yield the same accept/reject answer;
- deterministic if, for every input, the initial configuration admits exactly one computation.

A family decides a problem in polynomial time if the number of computation steps is bounded by a polynomial in the size of the input, and the family is uniformly constructible in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine.

Send-in communication rules are rules that move an object from the region surrounding a membrane into that membrane; such rules cannot distinguish among different membranes that share the same label and the same electrical charge.

Question. Fix a "sufficiently powerful" model of P systems (for instance, P systems with active membranes restricted so that send-in rules behave as above). Decide which of the following holds:

(a) Every confluent recogniser P system family of the model that works in polynomial time can be simulated, with at most polynomial overhead, by a deterministic recogniser P system family of the same model; or

(b) There exists a variant of P systems (within the class above) in which confluent nondeterminism is strictly more powerful than determinism, i.e., some language decidable in polynomial time by a confluent family of that variant is not decidable in polynomial time by any deterministic family of the same variant.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The relationship between confluence and determinism in polynomial-time recogniser P systems is a long-standing open question in membrane computing complexity. While confluent P systems are known to be simulable by deterministic Turing machines (e.g., in exponential space), no polynomial-overhead deterministic P system simulation is known, nor has a strict separation been proved for standard models. Recent work on shallow non-confluent P systems and related variants discusses the gap but does not resolve the confluent-vs-deterministic question for the polynomial-time recogniser setting.

Consider P systems with active membranes used as recognisers of decision languages over a finite alphabet Σ. A recogniser P system halts on every input and signals acceptance or rejection by sending a distinguished object out of the skin membrane.

A semi-uniform family {Π_x}_{x∈Σ*} is one for which there exists a deterministic Turing machine M running in time polynomial in |x| that, on input x, outputs an encoding of a recogniser P system Π_x whose computations accept iff x belongs to the language.

A uniform family {Π_n, w_x} is specified by two deterministic polynomial-time Turing machines:
 • F, which on input 1^n outputs an encoding of a "skeleton" P system Π_n depending only on the length n = |x|;
 • E, which on input x outputs a multiset w_x of objects that is placed into a designated input region of Π_{|x|}.
The combined system Π_n with initial multiset w_x augmented decides membership of x in the language.

Let PMC_AM (resp. PMC*_AM) denote the class of languages decidable by polynomial-time uniform (resp. semi-uniform) families of P systems with active membranes (with the standard rule set: object evolution, communication, dissolution, and elementary and non-elementary membrane division, with electrical charges).

Question: Is PMC_AM = PMC*_AM? More generally, for "sufficiently powerful" variants of recogniser P systems, do polynomial-time uniform and polynomial-time semi-uniform families recognise exactly the same class of decision languages?

Consider the framework of recognizer P systems (membrane systems) used as decision-problem solvers in polynomial time. Two standard constructor regimes are:

(a) Semi-uniform: a polynomial-time Turing machine M takes each input instance w (encoded as a string) and outputs a P system Π_w that decides whether w is in the language L; the time and size of Π_w are polynomially bounded in |w|.

(b) Uniform: a polynomial-time Turing machine F takes only the input length n (in unary) and outputs a single P system family member Π_n together with a polynomial-time encoding of inputs of length n as multisets that are placed into a designated input membrane of Π_n; Π_n then decides membership in L for any input of length n.

In a semi-uniform construction, M may produce, across the set of inputs of a fixed length n, super-polynomially many distinct underlying membrane structures (i.e., the rooted tree of nested membranes, ignoring multiset contents and rules attached to membranes can vary unboundedly with the specific instance w of length n). A natural obstruction to converting a semi-uniform construction into a uniform one is that F, given only n, cannot in polynomial time output a single fixed "skeleton" membrane structure that encompasses all the membrane structures M would generate on the various length-n inputs.

Question: Is the ability of a polynomial-time semi-uniform constructor M to produce super-polynomially many different membrane structures on inputs of the same length ever computationally essential? Equivalently, for every language L recognized in polynomial time by a semi-uniform family of recognizer P systems (in some fixed standard variant, e.g., P systems with active membranes), does there exist a polynomial-time uniform family of recognizer P systems (of the same variant) that decides L? Or are there variants of P systems for which this conversion provably fails, so that semi-uniform polynomial-time recognition is strictly more powerful than uniform polynomial-time recognition?

Background. A P system with active membranes is a computational device consisting of a hierarchy of nested membranes; each membrane carries an electrical charge (positive, negative, or neutral) and contains a multiset of objects drawn from a finite alphabet. Computation proceeds in synchronous, maximally parallel steps governed by rules that may rewrite objects, send objects through a membrane (possibly changing its charge), dissolve a membrane, or divide a membrane into two copies. A "single-membrane" P system is one whose membrane structure consists of just one membrane (the skin); in many variants, such isolated single membranes working in polynomial time are known to characterize exactly the class P.

Question. Consider the family of P-system variants V with the following property: any single, isolated membrane of V running for a polynomially bounded number of steps recognizes only languages in P. Prove or disprove the following uniform reduction claim:

(A) For every variant V in this family, there exists a polynomial-time deterministic Turing machine simulator M such that the global behavior of any P system Π in V on any input is equivalent to the system obtained by replacing the internal evolution of each individual membrane of Π by M; that is, all computational power of V beyond P arises solely from membrane division, inter-membrane communication, and the resulting network structure of membranes.

Sub-question (counting). As a key special case, decide whether the following is possible in deterministic polynomial time per step on a single charged membrane: given a multiset over a one-letter alphabet {a} entering the membrane in parallel with multiplicity n (where n may be exponential in the input size, encoded in unary by the parallel arrival of n copies of a), produce inside the membrane a binary representation of n using only standard rules of P systems with active membranes (object rewriting, communication, and charge changes) that operate in polynomial time. Equivalently: can a single charged membrane feasibly "count" an exponential number of identical objects arriving simultaneously, converting their unary multiplicity into a binary numeral?

Recent work on space complexity in P systems with active membranes (e.g., the Journal of Membrane Computing articles from 2021–2022 on alternative/binary space measures) explicitly notes that it remains unresolved whether efficient (binary) encoding of object multiplicities strictly increases computational power over the natural unary encoding for the standard variants. Consider recognizer cell-like P systems with active membranes operating in polynomial time (confluent semantics). The structure of such a system is a rooted tree of nested membranes, each labeled and possibly polarized, containing multisets of objects that evolve in parallel by maximally parallel application of rules of the standard types: object evolution, send-in and send-out communication, dissolution, and membrane division (elementary and possibly non-elementary). A uniform family {Π_n} of such P systems decides a language L if, on input of size n, Π_n halts in polynomially many steps and outputs acceptance iff the input is in L.

For a P system Π define its division depth as the maximum, over all computations and over all membranes ever created by division rules, of the nesting depth at which a division rule is applied. For a function d: ℕ → ℕ let PMC_AM(d) denote the class of languages decided in polynomial time by uniform families of confluent recognizer P systems with active membranes whose division depth on input of size n is at most d(n).

It is known that:
 (i) PMC_AM(0) = P,
 (ii) PMC_AM(1) = P^{#P},
 (iii) PMC_AM(poly(n)) = PSPACE.

Questions:

Consider recognizer cell-like P systems with active membranes operating in polynomial time (confluent semantics). The structure of such a system is a rooted tree of nested membranes, each labeled and possibly polarized, containing multisets of objects that evolve in parallel by maximally parallel application of rules of the standard types: object evolution, send-in and send-out communication, dissolution, and membrane division (elementary and possibly non-elementary). A uniform family {Π_n} of such P systems decides a language L if, on input of size n, Π_n halts in polynomially many steps and outputs acceptance iff the input is in L.

For a P system Π define its division depth as the maximum, over all computations and over all membranes ever created by division rules, of the nesting depth at which a division rule is applied. For a function d: ℕ → ℕ let PMC_AM(d) denote the class of languages decided in polynomial time by uniform families of confluent recognizer P systems with active membranes whose division depth on input of size n is at most d(n).

It is known that:
 (i) PMC_AM(0) = P,
 (ii) PMC_AM(1) = P^{#P},
 (iii) PMC_AM(poly(n)) = PSPACE.

Questions:
(a) For every fixed constant d ≥ 1, is PMC_AM(d) ⊊ PMC_AM(d+1), i.e., does division depth induce a proper infinite hierarchy at constant depths, and what are matching upper bounds characterizing PMC_AM(d) for each constant d ≥ 2?
(b) Characterize PMC_AM(d(n)) for intermediate growth rates such as d(n) = O(log n): which standard complexity class (if any) does it equal?
