The MacMahon Omega operator $\Omega_{\geq}$ acts on Laurent series in an auxiliary variable $\lambda$ by

$$\Omega_{\geq}\!\left(\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} a_n\, \lambda^n\right) \;=\; \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n,$$

that is, it discards all terms with negative powers of $\lambda$ and then sets $\lambda = 1$. It admits a well-developed calculus of "practical" evaluation rules on rational functions in $\lambda$ (such as

$$\Omega_{\geq}\,\frac{1}{(1-\lambda x)(1-\lambda^{-1} y)} \;=\; \frac{1}{(1-x)(1-xy)},$$

and similar identities), which makes it effective in combinatorial partition analysis.

Construct an operator $\Phi$, acting on (formal Laurent or power) series with coefficients in some standard ring (e.g.\ $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$ or $\mathbb{Q}[[q_1,q_2,\ldots]]$), having the following two properties:

1. (Positivity) For every series $f = \sum_n c_n\, \mu^n$ in its domain, the output $\Phi(f)$ contains no terms with negative coefficients; equivalently, $\Phi$ removes (or annihilates) every monomial whose coefficient is negative while preserving those with nonnegative coefficients.

2. (Practical calculus) $\Phi$ obeys a system of closed-form evaluation rules on a natural class of rational generating functions, analogous in scope and usability to the known rules for $\Omega_{\geq}$, so that $\Phi$ can be effectively computed in concrete partition-theoretic settings — in particular for generating functions arising from linked partition ideals in the sense of Andrews.

Either exhibit such an operator $\Phi$ together with its rule system and demonstrate an application to a family of linked partition ideals, or prove that no such operator can exist.

Let $\mathbb{H} = \{z = x+iy : y > 0\}$ denote the upper half-plane, and for a real parameter $s > 0$ let $\partial\mu_s$ denote the measure $\frac{dx\,dy}{y^s}$ on $\mathbb{H}$. Define the weighted Bergman space
$$A_s(\mathbb{H}) := L^2(\mathbb{H}, \partial\mu_s) \cap \{\text{holomorphic functions on } \mathbb{H}\},$$
with inner product $\langle f, g\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{H}} f(z)\overline{g(z)}\,\frac{dx\,dy}{y^s}$.

Fix a subgroup $\Gamma \le \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ of finite covolume $\mathrm{Cov}(\Gamma)$ (with respect to the hyperbolic measure $\frac{dx\,dy}{y^2}$). For $\gamma = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \in \Gamma$ and a holomorphic function $f$ on $\mathbb{H}$, define the weight-$k$ slash action
$$(f|_\gamma)(z) := (cz+d)^{-k}\, f\!\left(\frac{az+b}{cz+d}\right),$$
where $k = s$ is the appropriate weight associated with the parameter $s$.

A function $f \in A_{s-2}(\mathbb{H})$ is called:
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{tracelike} if $\displaystyle\sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} |f|_\gamma(z)|^2 = C\, y^{-s}$ for some constant $C > 0$ and all $z \in \mathbb{H}$;
\item \emph{wandering} if $\langle f|_\gamma,\, f\rangle = 0$ for all $\gamma \in \Gamma \setminus \{\mathrm{Id}\}$.
\end{itemize}

Set $s_0 := \frac{4\pi}{\mathrm{Cov}(\Gamma)} + 1$. (For $\Gamma = \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, $\mathrm{Cov}(\Gamma) = \pi/3$, so $s_0 = 13$.) It is known that tracelike vectors exist if and only if $s \le s_0$, that wandering vectors exist if and only if $s \ge s_0$, and that at $s = s_0$ the two conditions are equivalent.

Problem: For $\Gamma = \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ (or more generally for an arbitrary finite-index $\Gamma \le \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$), exhibit an explicit nonzero function $f \in A_{s_0 - 2}(\mathbb{H})$ at $s = s_0$ that is simultaneously tracelike and wandering.

Background. The classical Erdős–Lehner theorem describes the limiting distribution of the number of parts in a uniformly random partition of n: if λ is chosen uniformly from the set of partitions of n and ℓ(λ) denotes its number of parts (length), then after suitable centering and scaling, (ℓ(λ) − μ_n)/σ_n converges in distribution to a Gumbel (doubly exponential) law as n → ∞, with explicit constants μ_n, σ_n of order √n log n and √n respectively.

Setup. Capparelli, Meurman, A. Primc and M. Primc (CMMP) introduced certain classes of colored integer partitions defined by difference conditions of Rogers–Ramanujan–Gordon type. For fixed parameters in their construction, let P_CMMP(n) denote the set of CMMP-partitions of n, and for λ ∈ P_CMMP(n) let ℓ(λ) be its length (total number of parts, counted with color/multiplicity as prescribed by the CMMP definition).

Problem. Choose λ uniformly at random from P_CMMP(n). Determine the asymptotic distribution of the length ℓ(λ) as n → ∞: find centering and scaling sequences a_n, b_n and a non-degenerate limit law F such that

   ℙ[(ℓ(λ) − a_n)/b_n ≤ x] → F(x) as n → ∞,

and more generally obtain Erdős–Lehner type limit theorems for natural statistics on partitions arising in generalizations of Rogers–Ramanujan-type identities, in particular for the CMMP families.

For an integer $n\ge 0$ and an integer $m$, let $M(m,n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ whose crank equals $m$, where the crank of a partition $\lambda$ is defined by
$$\operatorname{crank}(\lambda)=\begin{cases}\ell(\lambda) & \text{if }o(\lambda)=0,\\ \mu(\lambda)-o(\lambda) & \text{if }o(\lambda)>0,\end{cases}$$
with $\ell(\lambda)$ the largest part of $\lambda$, $o(\lambda)$ the number of ones in $\lambda$, and $\mu(\lambda)$ the number of parts of $\lambda$ strictly larger than $o(\lambda)$. The associated crank generating function satisfies
$$\sum_{n\ge 0}\Bigl(\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}M(m,n)z^m\Bigr)q^n \;=\; \prod_{n\ge 1}\frac{1-q^n}{(1-zq^n)(1-z^{-1}q^n)}.$$
For each $n\ge 1$ define the (normalized) crank polynomial
$$C_n(z)\;=\;\sum_{m=-(n-1)}^{n-1} M(m,n)\,z^{\,m+n-1}\;\in\;\mathbb Z[z].$$
It is known that Ramanujan's partition congruences
$$p(5n+4)\equiv 0\pmod 5,\quad p(7n+5)\equiv 0\pmod 7,\quad p(11n+6)\equiv 0\pmod{11}$$
are equivalent to the divisibility of $C_{5n+4}(z)$, $C_{7n+5}(z)$, $C_{11n+6}(z)$ by the cyclotomic polynomials $\Phi_5(z)$, $\Phi_7(z)$, $\Phi_{11}(z)$ respectively in $\mathbb Z[z]$.

Determine the complete factorization of the crank polynomials $C_n(z)$ into irreducible factors over $\mathbb Z[z]$ (or, equivalently, over $\mathbb Q[z]$), describing in particular which cyclotomic polynomials divide $C_n(z)$ and the structure of the remaining (non-cyclotomic) irreducible factors as functions of $n$.

Nandi's first partition identity (arising from level-4 standard modules of the affine Lie algebra $A_2^{(2)}$) asserts that a certain explicitly defined set of integer partitions—those satisfying Nandi's difference conditions for the first identity—has generating function equal to
$$\prod_{n\ge 0}\frac{1}{(1-q^{14n+2})(1-q^{14n+3})(1-q^{14n+4})(1-q^{14n+10})(1-q^{14n+11})(1-q^{14n+12})}.$$
On the other hand, one has the analytic identity
$$\sum_{i,j,k,\ell\ge 0}\frac{q^{4i^2+12ij+8ik+4i\ell+12j^2+16jk+8j\ell+6k^2+6k\ell+2\ell^2}}{(q^2;q^2)_i\,(q^2;q^2)_j\,(q;q)_k\,(q;q)_\ell}=\prod_{n\ge 0}\frac{1}{(1-q^{14n+2})(1-q^{14n+3})(1-q^{14n+4})(1-q^{14n+10})(1-q^{14n+11})(1-q^{14n+12})},$$
where $(a;q)_n=\prod_{r=0}^{n-1}(1-aq^r)$. Provide a combinatorial interpretation of the quadruple sum on the left-hand side as a generating function for the partitions enumerated by Nandi's first identity. Concretely: exhibit a statistic-preserving bijection (or an equivalent combinatorial construction) that, for each $(i,j,k,\ell)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^4$, identifies the summand
$$\frac{q^{4i^2+12ij+8ik+4i\ell+12j^2+16jk+8j\ell+6k^2+6k\ell+2\ell^2}}{(q^2;q^2)_i\,(q^2;q^2)_j\,(q;q)_k\,(q;q)_\ell}$$
with the generating function of a naturally defined subfamily of the partitions in Nandi's first identity, in such a way that the disjoint union of these subfamilies, indexed by $(i,j,k,\ell)$, recovers all of the partitions counted by that identity.

Background. Andrews–Gordon type identities express, for integers $k \ge 2$ and $1 \le i \le k$, the generating function
$$\sum_{n_1,\dots,n_{k-1} \ge 0} \frac{q^{N_1^2+N_2^2+\cdots+N_{k-1}^2+N_i+N_{i+1}+\cdots+N_{k-1}}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q;q)_{n_2}\cdots (q;q)_{n_{k-1}}}, \qquad N_j := n_j+n_{j+1}+\cdots+n_{k-1},$$
as an infinite product, where $(a;q)_n := \prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1-aq^j)$. The series above is "manifestly positive" in that every coefficient in its $q$-expansion is visibly a sum of non-negative terms. Kurşungöz introduced manifestly positive double/multi-sum representations for the generating functions of various partition families (including those arising in Andrews–Gordon, Bressoud, and Kanade–Russell type identities), in which each summand directly enumerates partitions of a prescribed shape satisfying explicit difference and congruence conditions. Bressoud gave a combinatorial proof of the Rogers–Ramanujan and Schur identities by constructing an explicit bijection between two families of partitions, one defined by difference conditions and one by congruence conditions, refined by appropriate statistics.

Problem. Produce a Bressoud-style combinatorial proof — that is, an explicit weight-preserving bijection (or system of bijections) between partition families with difference conditions and partition families with congruence/product-side conditions — that establishes the Kurşungöz-type manifestly positive multi-sum representations of Andrews–Gordon / Bressoud type partition generating functions. Equivalently, give a direct combinatorial interpretation of each term of the Kurşungöz manifestly positive series as enumerating a class of partitions, together with an explicit bijection to the partitions counted by the corresponding product side.

Let $F$ be a totally real number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_F$, and let $\mathcal{O}_F^+$ denote the monoid of totally positive integers in $\mathcal{O}_F$ (elements $\alpha\in\mathcal{O}_F$ whose images under every real embedding of $F$ are positive), together with $0$. A partition of $\alpha\in\mathcal{O}_F^+$ is an unordered (multi-)representation $\alpha=\beta_1+\beta_2+\cdots+\beta_k$ with each $\beta_i\in\mathcal{O}_F^+\setminus\{0\}$. An element $\beta\in\mathcal{O}_F^+\setminus\{0\}$ is called (additively) indecomposable if it cannot be written as $\beta=\gamma+\delta$ with $\gamma,\delta\in\mathcal{O}_F^+\setminus\{0\}$.

Consider the formal generating series of partitions over $F$,
$$P_F(q) \;=\; \sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal{O}_F^+\cup\{0\}} p_F(\alpha)\, q^{\alpha},$$
where $p_F(\alpha)$ is the number of partitions of $\alpha$ (with $p_F(0)=1$), and $q^\alpha$ is a formal symbol indexed by $\alpha\in\mathcal{O}_F^+$ satisfying $q^{\alpha}q^{\beta}=q^{\alpha+\beta}$.

(a) Identify an appropriate algebraic/analytic structure (e.g., a suitable ring, module, modular- or Jacobi-form-like object, multivariable $q$-series ring indexed by a cone in $\mathcal{O}_F\otimes\mathbb{R}$, etc.) in which $P_F(q)$ naturally lives and which plays the role analogous to the ring of formal power series in one variable $q$ in the classical case $F=\mathbb{Q}$ (where the Euler product $\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{-1}$ is the partition generating function).

(b) Within this structure, describe the analogue of the "building block" $1\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$: namely, characterize the set of additively indecomposable totally positive integers of $F$ and explain in what sense they serve as the generators in the partition product expansion of $P_F(q)$.

representations.normalized:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the set of all integer partitions. For $\lambda\in\mathcal{P}$, let $|\lambda|$ be its size and $\ell(\lambda)$ its length, with parts $\lambda_1\ge \lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge \lambda_{\ell(\lambda)}>0$.

For $k\ge 1$, define the shifted symmetric power-sum functions on partitions by
$$p_k(\lambda) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{\ell(\lambda)}\Big[\big(\lambda_i - i + \tfrac{1}{2}\big)^k - \big(-i+\tfrac{1}{2}\big)^k\Big],$$
and let $\Lambda^*$ be the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra generated by the $p_k$. (Elements of $\Lambda^*$ are called shifted symmetric functions.)

Given any function $f:\mathcal{P}\to\mathbb{Q}$, define its $q$-bracket by
$$\langle f\rangle_q \;=\; \frac{\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{P}} f(\lambda)\, q^{|\lambda|}}{\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{P}} q^{|\lambda|}}\;\in\;\mathbb{Q}[[q]].$$
It is known that for every $f\in\Lambda^*$, $\langle f\rangle_q$ is a quasimodular form (over $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$), and that there exists an operator $D:\Lambda^*\to\Lambda^*$ satisfying $\langle Df\rangle_q = q\dfrac{d}{dq}\langle f\rangle_q$ for all $f\in\Lambda^*$.

For a prime $p$ and a quasimodular form $g(q)=\sum_{n\ge 0} a_n q^n$ of weight $k$, the $p$-th Hecke operator is
$$T_p(g) \;=\; \sum_{n\ge 0}\big(a_{np} + p^{k-1} a_{n/p}\big)\,q^n,$$
with the convention that $a_{n/p}=0$ when $p\nmid n$.

Problem. Construct, for each prime $p$, an operator $T_p$ on $\Lambda^*$ such that
$$\langle T_p f\rangle_q \;=\; T_p\langle f\rangle_q \qquad \text{for all } f\in\Lambda^*,$$
or prove that no such family of operators exists.

The problem was posed by Jan-Willem van Ittersum as an open question in a recent collection of open problems on q-series and modular forms. Let $p/q$ be a positive rational number with $q$ odd. Define a sequence of odd positive integers $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots$ recursively as follows: having chosen $n_1, \dots, n_{k-1}$ (with the empty sum $0$ when $k=1$), let $n_k$ be the smallest odd positive integer strictly greater than $n_{k-1}$ (and at least $1$ when $k=1$) such that
$$\frac{1}{n_1} + \frac{1}{n_2} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n_k} < \frac{p}{q}.$$
If at some stage equality $\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k} = \frac{p}{q}$ can be achieved by choosing $n_k$ to be the smallest odd integer making the partial sum equal to $p/q$, the procedure terminates. Prove or disprove: for every positive rational $p/q$ with $q$ odd, this odd-denominator greedy unit-fraction procedure terminates after finitely many steps.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The odd greedy expansion termination problem is a well-known open problem in the theory of Egyptian fractions. While every rational p/q with odd q is known to admit a finite Egyptian fraction representation with odd denominators, it remains unknown whether the specific odd greedy procedure always terminates. Heuristic arguments suggest the answer is yes, but no proof is known.

Let $n \geq 2$ and let $F_n$ denote the free group of rank $n$. Consider the direct product
$$G = F_n \times F_n,$$
where the first factor is freely generated by $\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$ and the second factor is freely generated by $\{y_1,\dots,y_n\}$. Regard $G$ as a quotient of the free group $F_{2n}$ on $\{x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_n\}$ by the relations $[x_i,y_j]=1$ for all $1 \leq i,j \leq n$. Two generating tuples of length $k$ of a group are called Nielsen equivalent if one can be transformed into the other by a finite sequence of Nielsen transformations (replacing one entry by its inverse, swapping two entries, or replacing one entry by its product with another). An automorphism of $G$ is called tame if it is induced by some automorphism of the ambient free group $F_{2n}$.

Determine whether the following two statements hold:

(a) Every generating tuple of $G$ of cardinality $2n$ is Nielsen equivalent to $(x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_n)$.

(b) Every automorphism of $G$ is tame.

$$M(n) = \sup \{ |\mathrm{Orb}_\varphi(u)| : u \in F_n,\ \varphi \in \mathrm{Aut}(F_n),\ |\mathrm{Orb}_\varphi(u)| < \infty \},$$
i.e., how large can such a finite orbit be as $u$ ranges over $F_n$ and $\varphi$ ranges over $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$?

A finite orbit of size k under iteration of an automorphism φ of F_n exists if and only if Aut(F_n) contains an element of order k. The possible torsion orders in Aut(F_n) were classified by McCool and, more generally, by Khramtsov, so the answer is in principle reduced to a known result about finite subgroups of Aut(F_n). The associated quantitative question of bounding the number of automorphic images of a word of given length is conjectured to be polynomial of degree 2n−2, and this remains open in general.

Let $G$ be a finitely presented group, i.e., a group admitting a presentation $G = \langle X \mid R \rangle$ with both $X$ and $R$ finite. For a finite generating set $S$ of $G$, let $B_S(n)$ denote the number of elements of $G$ expressible as a product of at most $n$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$. The group $G$ is said to have polynomial growth if $B_S(n) \le C n^d$ for some constants $C, d > 0$ and all $n$, and exponential growth if $B_S(n) \ge a^n$ for some $a > 1$ and all sufficiently large $n$ (these notions are independent of the choice of finite generating set $S$). A free 2-generator semigroup in $G$ is a sub-semigroup generated by two elements $a, b \in G$ such that all distinct positive words in $a, b$ represent distinct elements of $G$. A subgroup $H \le G$ is nilpotent of finite index if $[G:H] < \infty$ and the lower central series of $H$ terminates at the trivial group in finitely many steps.

Answer the following two questions:

(a) Must every finitely presented group have either polynomial growth or exponential growth (equivalently: does no finitely presented group have intermediate growth)?

(b) Must every finitely presented group either contain a free 2-generator semigroup or contain a nilpotent subgroup of finite index?

The existence of a finitely presented group of intermediate growth is a well-known major open problem in geometric/combinatorial group theory. Grigorchuk's 1984 examples of groups of intermediate growth answered Milnor's question but are only finitely generated, not finitely presented. The companion dichotomy (free 2-generator semigroup vs. virtually nilpotent) is similarly unresolved for finitely presented groups; by Gromov's theorem virtually nilpotent groups are precisely those of polynomial growth, so part (b) is closely tied to part (a).

Consider a one-dimensional branching random walk defined as follows. Start with a single particle at position $x>0$. At each integer time step, every alive particle is replaced by a finite point process of children, each child being displaced from its parent by an independent copy of a fixed step distribution; particles that reach the half-line $(-\infty,0]$ are killed (absorbed). Introduce a drift parameter so that the system is supercritical for drifts strictly above a critical value $\varepsilon_c$ and subcritical at or below it; let $\varepsilon = \varepsilon_c - \delta$ measure the closeness to criticality.

For branching Brownian motion (the continuous analogue), the following fine near-critical and critical results are known: (i) the system survives with positive probability iff $\delta>0$; (ii) on the scale $L = \pi/\sqrt{\delta}$, the survival probability starting from $L+x$ converges as $\delta \downarrow 0$ to a nontrivial traveling-wave $\theta(x)\in(0,1)$ solving the Fisher–KPP equation; (iii) sharp asymptotics for the survival probability are available when $x<L$ and $L-x\to\infty$.

Problem. Establish the analogues of (i)–(iii) for the branching random walk above, with explicit scaling constants in terms of the step distribution and offspring law. A key prerequisite is to develop refined estimates, beyond the first-order exponential-decay rate given by Mogul'skii's theorem, for the probability that a one-dimensional random walk with $n$ steps remains in a prescribed interval $[a,b]$ — and more generally between two prescribed curves $f(\lfloor nt\rfloor)\le S_k\le g(\lfloor nt\rfloor)$ — including precise polynomial prefactors and dependence on the endpoints. Use these estimates to prove the corresponding precise survival and scaling theorems for the near-critical branching random walk with killing at the origin.

Several components have been addressed in the literature: survival probability of branching random walks killed below a linear boundary (Aïdékon–Jaffuel, Bérard–Gouéré, Gantert–Hu–Shi) and critical branching random walks with small drift have been studied, providing analogues of some BBM results. Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to (0,\infty)$ be a smooth, strictly decreasing function. For each $T>0$, consider the time-inhomogeneous branching Brownian motion on $\mathbb{R}$ defined as follows: starting from one particle at the origin at time $0$, each particle moves as a continuous martingale with instantaneous variance $\sigma(t/T)^2$ at time $t\in[0,T]$, and independently of its motion branches at rate $1$ into two children that continue independently with the same dynamics. Let $M_T$ denote the maximal position among all particles alive at time $T$.

It is known that there exist explicit constants $v_\sigma=\int_0^1 \sigma(s)\,ds$ and
$$w_\sigma = 2^{-1/3}\alpha_1\int_0^1 \sigma(s)^{1/3}|\sigma'(s)|^{2/3}\,ds,$$
where $-\alpha_1\approx -2.33811$ is the largest zero of the Airy function $\mathrm{Ai}$, such that with the centering
$$m_T = v_\sigma T - w_\sigma T^{1/3} - \sigma(1)\log T,$$
the family $\{M_T - m_T\}_{T\ge 0}$ is tight.

Prove that $M_T - m_T$ converges in distribution as $T\to\infty$, and identify the limiting law.

representations.normalized:
Consider a time-inhomogeneous branching Brownian motion (BBM) on the real line defined as follows. Fix a time horizon T>0 and a strictly decreasing, positive, continuously differentiable function σ:[0,1]→(0,∞). Starting from a single particle at the origin at time 0, each particle moves as a Brownian motion with time-dependent variance σ²(t/T) at time t∈[0,T], and independently undergoes dyadic branching at rate 1; upon branching, a particle is replaced by two offspring at its current location, which then evolve independently according to the same rules.

For t∈[0,T] let N(t) denote the set of particles alive at time t and let X_u(t) denote the position of particle u∈N(t). Define the maximum
   M_T := max_{u∈N(T)} X_u(T),
and the extremal point process
   E_T := Σ_{u∈N(T)} δ_{X_u(T) - m_T},
where m_T is the centering
   m_T = v_σ T − w_σ T^{1/3} − σ(1) log T,
with v_σ = ∫₀¹ σ(s) ds·√2 (the linear speed) and w_σ an explicit constant determined by σ such that M_T − m_T is tight.

Questions:
(a) Prove that E_T converges weakly, as T→∞, to a non-trivial random point process on ℝ, and describe its limit (e.g. as a decorated Poisson point process whose intensity and cluster law are determined by σ).
(b) Describe the genealogy of the extremal particles in the following sense. For each pair of particles u,v∈N(T) attaining positions near M_T, let τ_T(u,v)∈[0,T] denote the time of their most recent common ancestor. Identify a suitable rescaled statistic of (τ_T(u,v)/T) for tuples of near-maximal particles, and show that this statistic converges, as T→∞, to a limit describable in terms of Neveu's continuous-state branching process (the CSBP with branching mechanism ψ(θ)=θ log θ), equivalently to a Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent structure.

Consider a branching Brownian motion (BBM) with time-varying variance defined as follows. Fix a time horizon t > 0 and a measurable speed function σ²:[0,1] → (0,∞) (or, equivalently, an increasing covariance function A:[0,1] → [0,∞) with A(0)=0, A(1)=1). Starting from a single particle at the origin at time 0, each particle performs an independent Gaussian motion whose infinitesimal variance at time s ∈ [0,t] is σ²(s/t), and independently branches at rate 1 into two offspring that continue the same dynamics. Let M_t denote the position of the rightmost particle at time t, and let m_t denote its typical value (i.e. m_t is chosen so that M_t − m_t is tight as t → ∞).

(a) Determine the large-deviation asymptotics
    P(M_t ≥ (1+δ) m_t)  as t → ∞,
for fixed δ > 0, identifying the exponential rate (and any subexponential corrections) in terms of the speed function σ².

(b) Describe the limiting law of the genealogical and spatial structure of the BBM (for example, the empirical measure of particle trajectories, or the ancestral path of the leading particle) conditioned on the rare event {M_t ≥ (1+δ) m_t}.

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

Large deviation results and conditional descriptions for the maximum are well understood for standard (constant-variance) BBM and have been extended to several variants (BBM with selection/coalescence, periodic environments, branching random walks). For variable-speed/time-inhomogeneous BBM, recent work (e.g., Bovier–Hartung and related, including the 2024 paper "From 1 to infinity: the log-correction for the maximum of variable-speed BBM") has determined the order and log-corrections of the typical maximum, and slower deviation results exist for ordinary BBM. However, a complete large-deviation principle of the form P(M_t ≥ (1+δ)m_t) together with the conditional description of the process for general time-varying variance does not appear to have been fully resolved in the literature, so the status is taken as unknown.

representations.normalized:
Consider the following particle system on the real line, called the N-branching random walk with selection. Fix an integer N ≥ 1 and a probability distribution μ on ℝ (the displacement distribution). Start with N particles at arbitrary positions. At each discrete time step:
1. Every particle gives birth to two children at its current position (and then dies).
2. Each child performs an independent jump distributed as μ.
3. Only the N rightmost particles among the 2N children are retained; the remaining N particles are removed.

Let M_n^N denote the position of the rightmost particle at generation n. It is known that:
- If μ has some exponential moment (i.e. ∫ e^{λx} dμ(x) < ∞ for some λ > 0), then n^{-1} M_n^N converges a.s. to a deterministic speed v_N, and v_N tends to a finite limit as N → ∞ at a rate of order (log N)^{-2}.
- If μ has a regularly varying tail of index α > 0 (polynomial tail), the time-space scaling and the limiting speed exhibit qualitatively different behavior, governed by the heavy-tail index.

Question. For displacement distributions μ that are subexponential but not regularly varying — i.e., μ has no exponential moment, yet its tail decays faster than any polynomial (for example, stretched-exponential tails of the form P(X > x) ∼ exp(-x^β) with 0 < β < 1, or tails behaving like exp(-x/log x), etc.) — determine the asymptotic speed v_N = lim_{n→∞} M_n^N / n and the qualitative behavior of the N-branching random walk with selection. In particular, identify the correct scaling of v_N as N → ∞ and describe the genealogical/spatial structure of the surviving population in these intermediate tail regimes.

The intermediate regime between exponential-moment (light-tailed) displacements and regularly varying (polynomial) tails for N-branching random walks with selection of the N rightmost particles appears to remain open. Consider the N-branching random walk (N-BRW) on the real line defined as follows. Fix an integer N ≥ 1 and a displacement distribution μ on ℝ. Start with N particles at arbitrary positions in ℝ. At each discrete time step, every particle independently produces two children, and each child is displaced from its parent by an independent random variable with law μ; among the 2N children produced, only the N rightmost are retained to form the next generation.

Recall that a probability distribution μ on ℝ (supported on, or with right tail F̄(x) = μ((x,∞))) is called subexponential if F̄ is long-tailed and F̄∗F̄(x) / F̄(x) → 2 as x → ∞. Examples include all regularly varying tails as well as e.g. Weibull-type tails with stretched-exponential decay.

For displacement distributions with regularly varying right tails, it is known that the advance (front speed / position) of the cloud of N particles is driven, on the relevant scale, by single large jumps of individual particles rather than by cooperative behavior of many particles.

Question: For every subexponential displacement distribution μ, is the macroscopic advance of the N-particle cloud necessarily caused by jumps of single particles (as in the regularly varying case), or do there exist subexponential displacement distributions for which interaction between particles produces a genuinely different leading mechanism for the advance of the cloud?

representations.normalized:
Consider the N-particle branching random walk on $\mathbb{R}$ defined as follows. At each integer time, a population of exactly $N$ particles is maintained on the real line. From time $n$ to time $n+1$, each particle is replaced by two offspring; each offspring is placed at the location of its parent plus an independent jump drawn from a fixed displacement distribution $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$. Out of the $2N$ offspring, only the $N$ rightmost are kept and constitute the population at time $n+1$.

Sample $k$ particles uniformly at random from the population at a large time $T$, and trace their ancestral lineages backward in time. After a suitable time rescaling depending on $N$ and $\mu$, this yields a $k$-particle coalescent process describing the genealogy.

Recall that a displacement distribution $\mu$ is called subexponential if its tail $\overline{F}(x) = \mu((x,\infty))$ satisfies $\overline{F^{*2}}(x)/\overline{F}(x) \to 2$ as $x \to \infty$, where $F^{*2}$ is the convolution of $F$ with itself. The star-shaped coalescent is the (degenerate) coalescent process in which all blocks merge simultaneously into a single block at one random time.

Question: For every subexponential displacement distribution $\mu$, is the limiting genealogy of the N-particle branching random walk (in the limit $N \to \infty$, with appropriate time rescaling) given by the star-shaped coalescent?

Constructions of two-parameter measure-valued diffusions with the two-parameter Poisson–Dirichlet / Pitman–Yor (i.e. $\mathrm{Dirichlet}(\theta,\alpha,\nu_0)$) law as stationary distribution have been given. Petrov (2009) constructed a diffusion on the Kingman simplex with PD$(\alpha,\theta)$ stationary law; Feng–Sun and others gave Wright–Fisher type constructions of the two-parameter Poisson–Dirichlet diffusion; and Forman, Rizzolo, Shi and Winkel (Ann. Reversibility (as opposed to mere stationarity) for general parameters is established in this work.

Let $\psi:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be an increasing function, and let $G_\psi$ denote the continuous multiplicative graph whose law is characterized by $\psi$ (so that $\psi$ controls the connectivity intensity at each scale $\lambda$). It is known that the sufficient condition
$$\int_{1}^{\infty}\frac{d\lambda}{\psi(\lambda)} < \infty$$
implies that the limiting graph $G_\psi$ is almost surely compact. Determine whether this integrability condition is sharp; that is, decide whether the divergence
$$\int_{1}^{\infty}\frac{d\lambda}{\psi(\lambda)} = \infty$$
implies that $G_\psi$ is almost surely non-compact.

Let $(B^b_t)_{t\ge 0}$ and $(B^r_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be two independent standard one-dimensional Brownian motions, both started at $0$, defined on a common probability space. Let $(c_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be a measurable $\{b,r\}$-valued process, independent of $(B^b, B^r)$, that assigns to each time $t$ a "colour". Define the cumulative occupation times
$$\Lambda^b_t = \int_0^t \mathbf{1}_{\{c_s=b\}}\,ds, \qquad \Lambda^r_t = \int_0^t \mathbf{1}_{\{c_s=r\}}\,ds,$$
so that $\Lambda^b_t + \Lambda^r_t = t$ for every $t\ge 0$. Define the recombined process
$$B_t := B^b(\Lambda^b_t) + B^r(\Lambda^r_t), \qquad t\ge 0.$$
Then $(B_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is itself a standard one-dimensional Brownian motion started from $0$.

Question. Does there exist a measurable functional $F$ on the path space of one-dimensional continuous paths, taking values in pairs of continuous paths, such that
$$\bigl(B^b, B^r\bigr) = F(B) \qquad \text{almost surely}?$$
Equivalently, can the two component Brownian motions $B^b$ and $B^r$ be recovered from the single Brownian motion $B$ in a measurable way?

Let $X = (X_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be either a superprocess or a branching Markov process taking values in the space of finite (or Radon) measures on a Polish state space $E$, with a branching/spatial motion mechanism whose mean semigroup $(T_t)_{t \ge 0}$ acts on a suitable function space over $E$. Existing spatial limit theorems for $X$ — namely, strong and weak laws of large numbers describing the asymptotic spatial distribution of $X_t$ after suitable normalization, the $L\log L$ moment criteria characterising non-degenerate martingale limits of the associated mean-zero martingales, and central limit theorems describing the fluctuations of $X_t$ around its law-of-large-numbers limit — have typically been proved under the assumption that the mean semigroup $(T_t)$ admits a spectral gap and a leading eigenfunction (i.e. has discrete spectrum at the top, in particular satisfying a Perron–Frobenius / $\lambda$-positivity condition). This assumption fails for fundamental examples such as supercritical super-Brownian motion on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where the mean semigroup is the heat semigroup with continuous spectrum.

Problem: Develop spatial limit theorems — strong/weak laws of large numbers, $L\log L$ criteria for the non-degeneracy of the limiting martingales, and central limit theorems for fluctuations — for supercritical superprocesses and branching Markov processes on general state spaces, under hypotheses that do not require the mean semigroup to possess a discrete spectrum (or a spectral gap), so that the resulting framework includes super-Brownian motion on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and other models with continuous-spectrum mean semigroups.

Problem: Develop spatial limit theorems — strong/weak laws of large numbers, $L\log L$ criteria for the non-degeneracy of the limiting martingales, and central limit theorems for fluctuations — for supercritical superprocesses and branching Markov processes on general state spaces, under hypotheses that do not require the mean semigroup to possess a discrete spectrum (or a spectral gap), so that the resulting framework includes super-Brownian motion on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and other models with continuous-spectrum mean semigroups.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Several works since 2018 have established spatial limit theorems beyond the discrete-spectrum / $\lambda$-positivity setting, including strong laws of large numbers for super-Brownian and super-stable processes, $L^2$ laws of large numbers for supercritical branching Markov processes beyond $\lambda$-positivity, and skeleton-decomposition-based LLNs for supercritical superprocesses. However, a unified treatment covering LLN, $L\log L$ criteria, and CLT for general superprocesses and branching Markov processes without spectral-gap assumptions does not yet appear complete, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

representations.normalized:
Fix $\kappa\in(8/3,8)$ and let $D\subsetneq\mathbb C$ be a simply connected domain. Let $\Gamma$ be a nested conformal loop ensemble $\mathrm{CLE}_\kappa$ in $D$, i.e. the canonical conformally invariant random countable collection of non-crossing loops obtained by iterating $\mathrm{CLE}_\kappa$ inside each loop. To each loop $\ell\in\Gamma$ assign an i.i.d. real weight $\xi_\ell$ with common law $\mu$ (a probability measure on $\mathbb R$ with mean zero and finite variance), independent of $\Gamma$. For $z\in D$ and $\varepsilon>0$, let $N_\varepsilon(z)$ denote the set of loops of $\Gamma$ that surround the disk $B(z,\varepsilon)$, and define
$$h_\varepsilon(z)=\sum_{\ell\in N_\varepsilon(z)}\xi_\ell - \mathbb E\Big[\sum_{\ell\in N_\varepsilon(z)}\xi_\ell\Big].$$
The nesting field is the random distribution $h=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow 0}h_\varepsilon$ (the limit existing in an appropriate space of distributions). When $\kappa=4$ and $\mu$ is a centered law with appropriate variance, $h$ is (a multiple of) the Gaussian free field on $D$, and it is known that the loop collection $\Gamma$ together with the weights $(\xi_\ell)$ used to construct $h$ is almost surely a measurable function of $h$ alone.

Question: For which $\kappa\in(8/3,8)\setminus\{4\}$ and for which laws $\mu$ (beyond the Gaussian case at $\kappa=4$) is the pair $(\Gamma,(\xi_\ell)_{\ell\in\Gamma})$ almost surely determined by the nesting field $h$?

Let $D \subsetneq \mathbb{C}$ be a simply connected planar domain and let $\kappa \in (8/3, 8)$. The conformal loop ensemble $\mathrm{CLE}_\kappa$ on $D$ is the (unique) conformally invariant probability measure on countable collections of non-crossing simple ($\kappa \le 4$) or non-simple ($\kappa > 4$) loops in $D$ such that the loops are locally distributed like Schramm–Loewner evolution curves of parameter $\kappa$. For $z \in D$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, let $N_\varepsilon(z)$ denote the number of loops of the CLE that surround the disk of radius $\varepsilon$ centered at $z$. It is known that, after subtracting its mean, the field $N_\varepsilon(z) - \mathbb{E}[N_\varepsilon(z)]$ converges almost surely as $\varepsilon \to 0$, in a suitable space of distributions, to a conformally invariant random generalized function $h$ on $D$, called the CLE$_\kappa$ nesting field.

Describe the extremal process of the CLE$_\kappa$ nesting field $h$. More precisely, identify the scaling limit (as $\varepsilon \to 0$, with appropriate centering and normalization) of the point process formed by the locations and values of the near-maxima of the field $N_\varepsilon(\cdot) - \mathbb{E}[N_\varepsilon(\cdot)]$ on $D$, including its intensity measure and the cluster law around its atoms, and compare its structure with that of the extremal process of the two-dimensional Gaussian free field.

representations.normalized:
Let $(X_t)_{t\ge 0}$ denote a standard one-dimensional binary branching Brownian motion: a single particle starts at the origin and performs a standard Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}$; independently of everything else, at rate $1$ each particle is replaced by two offspring that thereafter evolve as independent branching Brownian motions from the location of their parent. Let
$$ M_t \; := \; \max\{ X_t^{(i)} : i \in N(t) \} $$
denote the position of the rightmost particle alive at time $t$, where $N(t)$ is the set of particles alive at time $t$. Let $\mu_t$ denote the median of $M_t$, i.e. the (unique) real number such that $\mathbb{P}(M_t \ge \mu_t) = 1/2$.

It is known (Bramson) that
$$ \mu_t \; = \; \sqrt{2}\, t \;-\; \frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}\,\log t \;+\; O(1) \qquad (t \to \infty), $$
and indeed $\mu_t = \sqrt{2}\,t - \tfrac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}\log t + c + o(1)$ for some constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$.

After rescaling so that the leading speed equals $2$ (equivalently, working with the maximum of BBM whose particles diffuse with variance parameter giving asymptotic speed $2$, so that $\mu_t = 2t - \tfrac{3}{2}\log t + O(1)$), the function $t \mapsto \mu_t$ is differentiable for $t$ sufficiently large.

Prove or disprove the following asymptotic expansion of the instantaneous front velocity:
$$ \frac{d\mu_t}{dt} \; = \; 2 \;-\; \frac{3}{2t} \;+\; o\!\left(\frac{1}{t}\right) \qquad \text{as } t \to \infty. $$

Consider one-dimensional dyadic branching Brownian motion (BBM): start with a single particle at the origin which performs a standard Brownian motion; at rate 1 it dies and is replaced by two offspring, each of which independently performs a standard Brownian motion from the location of the parent and itself branches at rate 1, and so on. For t ≥ 0 let R_t denote the position of the rightmost particle alive at time t.

Bramson's theorem and its refinements show that for the median front position m_t, defined by P(R_t ≥ m_t) = 1/2, one has the Ebert–van Saarloos expansion
    d m_t / dt = √2 − 3 / (2√2 · t) + o(1/t)   as t → ∞
(equivalently, m_t = √2 t − (3/(2√2)) log t + C + o(1) for a constant C).

Question: Let μ_t denote a "front position" for the BBM defined in one of the following alternative ways:
  (a) μ_t = E[R_t], the expected position of the rightmost particle;
  (b) μ_t = argmax_x f_t(x), the most likely position (mode) of R_t, where f_t is the density of R_t.

Prove (or disprove) that for each such alternative choice of front position μ_t one has the same asymptotic
    d μ_t / dt = √2 − 3 / (2√2 · t) + o(1/t)   as t → ∞.

   μ_t = sup{ x ∈ ℝ : h(x,t) = c }.

   μ_t = 2t - (3/2) log t + a + o(1)   as t → ∞

   ∂_t μ_t = 2 - 3/(2t) + o(1/t)   as t → ∞.

representations.normalized:
Consider one-dimensional binary branching Brownian motion: start with a single particle at the origin performing standard Brownian motion; at rate 1 each particle splits into two independent particles which independently continue the same dynamics. Let $M_t$ denote the position of the right-most particle alive at time $t$, and let $m(t)$ denote the median (or any fixed quantile) of $M_t$.

It is classical (Bramson) that
$$ m(t) = \sqrt{2}\, t - \frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}\,\log t + O(1) \qquad (t\to\infty), $$
and the refined Bramson expansion asserts the more precise form
$$ m(t) = \sqrt{2}\, t - \frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}\,\log t + c_0 + \frac{c_1}{\sqrt{t}} + \frac{c_2 \log t}{t} + o\!\left(\frac{\log t}{t}\right), $$
for explicit constants $c_0, c_1, c_2$.

Define the (instantaneous) front velocity $v(t) := m'(t)$. Formally differentiating the refined expansion suggests
$$ v(t) = \sqrt{2} - \frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}\, t} - \frac{c_1}{2\, t^{3/2}} + \frac{c_2 (1 - \log t)}{t^2} + o\!\left(\frac{\log t}{t^2}\right). $$

Provide a rigorous proof (or disproof) that this term-by-term differentiation is valid; equivalently, establish the velocity expansion above, including the $t^{-3/2}$ correction and the $t^{-2}\log t$ term, with the same constants $c_1, c_2$ appearing in the refined Bramson expansion of $m(t)$.

representations.normalized:
Consider branching Brownian motion (BBM) with decay of mass on the real line, defined as follows. At time 0 there is a single particle at the origin carrying unit mass. Particles move as independent standard Brownian motions and branch at rate 1 into two daughters that inherit the parent's position and mass. In addition, each particle's mass decays continuously at a rate proportional to the total mass currently within a fixed neighbourhood of its position (the "decay-of-mass" interaction). Let ζ(t, x) denote the local mass density at time t and position x, and for m ∈ (0,1) define the left and right front locations
   d(t, m) = inf{ x > 0 : ζ(t, x) < m },
   D(t, m) = sup{ x ∈ ℝ : ζ(t, x) > m }.
It is known that for standard BBM the rightmost particle is located near √2 · t. The "front gaps" relative to this standard BBM front are √2 t − d(t, m) and √2 t − D(t, m), and these are conjectured to be of order t^{1/3}.

Prove or disprove: for every m ∈ (0,1) there exist real exponents a and b with 0 < a < 1/3 < b < 1 such that, almost surely,
   √2 t − d(t, m) grows faster than t^{a} (i.e. t^{a} = o(√2 t − d(t,m)) as t → ∞),
   √2 t − D(t, m) = o(t^{b}) as t → ∞.

representations.normalized:
Consider branching Brownian motion with decay of mass on the real line, defined as follows. At time $0$ there is a single particle at the origin with mass $1$. Particles move independently as standard Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}$ and branch at rate $1$, each branching event replacing a particle by two daughter particles at the same location, sharing the parent's mass equally (or, in an equivalent variant, each retaining the parent's mass). In addition, the mass $M_u(t)$ of a particle $u$ alive at time $t$ decays according to
$$\frac{d}{dt} M_u(t) \;=\; -\, M_u(t) \int_{\mathbb{R}} \phi\!\big(X_u(t)-y\big)\, \rho(t,y)\, dy,$$
where $X_u(t)$ is the position of particle $u$, $\rho(t,y) = \sum_{v \text{ alive at } t} M_v(t)\, \delta_{X_v(t)}(y)$ is the empirical mass density, and $\phi$ is a fixed nonnegative, even, compactly supported smooth interaction kernel. Let
$$\mathcal{M}(t) \;=\; \max_{u \text{ alive at } t} M_u(t)$$
be the largest particle mass at time $t$.

It is known that there exist constants $C, \alpha > 0$ such that almost surely, for all sufficiently large $t$,
$$\mathcal{M}(t) \;\le\; C\, t^{-\alpha}$$
(a polynomial-type upper bound). It is conjectured that $\mathcal{M}(t)$ in fact decays substantially faster than any such polynomial rate.

Problem. Improve the upper bound on $\mathcal{M}(t)$: determine the true asymptotic rate of decay of the largest particle mass $\mathcal{M}(t)$ as $t \to \infty$, and in particular establish a bound that decays strictly faster than the existing polynomial bound (for instance, show a stretched-exponential or exponential rate of decay, if true).

Consider the following individual-based Markov model of Darwinian evolution on the trait space $X = \mathbb{R}^d$. The population at time $t$ is described by a finite point measure
$$\nu^K_t = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{N_t} \delta_{x_i(t)},$$
where $K>0$ is a scaling parameter (carrying capacity) and $x_i(t) \in X$ are the traits of the $N_t$ individuals alive at time $t$. An individual of trait $x$ undergoes the following independent events:
- it gives birth at rate $K r(x) + b(x)$, where with probability $1 - p(x)$ the newborn inherits trait $x$ and with probability $p(x)$ the newborn has trait $x + h$, where $h$ is drawn from a mutation kernel $m_K(x,\cdot)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$;
- it dies at rate $K r(x) + d(x) + \sum_{j \neq i} \frac{c(x, x_j(t))}{K}$, where $c: X \times X \to \mathbb{R}_+$ is a competition kernel.

Assume that as $K \to \infty$, suitable rescalings of $m_K$ (so that $K \int h h^T m_K(x,dh) \to \Sigma(x)$) and the standard moment/regularity conditions hold so that the sequence $(\nu^K_\cdot)$ converges in law in $D(\mathbb{R}_+, M_F(\mathbb{R}^d))$ to a continuous measure-valued superprocess $\nu = (\nu_t)_{t \ge 0}$ satisfying the associated martingale problem (a generalized super-Brownian motion with logistic-type interaction).

Question: Does the limiting measure-valued process $\nu_t$ almost surely admit a density with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $t > 0$, at least in the one-dimensional case $d = 1$ (as is the case for classical super-Brownian motion in dimension one)?

representations.normalized:
Consider an individual-based branching particle system on a Polish space $E$ depending on a scaling parameter $n\in\mathbb{N}$, defined as follows. At time $0$ there are particles in $E$, each of mass $1/n$. Each particle, independently, moves according to a (sub-)Markov process with generator $L$ on $E$, lives for an exponentially distributed time with mean $1/n$, and at the end of its life is replaced at its terminal location by a random number of offspring with offspring distribution whose generating function satisfies the standard near-critical rescaling so that, as $n\to\infty$, the empirical measure-valued processes
$$X^{(n)}_t \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i}\delta_{x_i(t)}$$
converge weakly in the Skorokhod space $D([0,\infty),\mathcal{M}_F(E))$ to a measure-valued superprocess $\nu=(\nu_t)_{t\ge 0}$ taking values in the space $\mathcal{M}_F(E)$ of finite measures on $E$, with branching mechanism $\psi$ and spatial motion generator $L$.

Assume that the limiting superprocess $\nu$ becomes extinct almost surely, i.e.
$$\mathbb{P}_\mu\bigl(\,\exists\, T<\infty:\ \nu_T = 0\,\bigr)=1\qquad\text{for every initial law }\mu\in\mathcal{M}_F(E)\setminus\{0\}.$$

Let $\tau:=\inf\{t\ge 0:\nu_t = 0\}$ denote the extinction time. A probability measure $\eta$ on $\mathcal{M}_F(E)\setminus\{0\}$ is called a quasi-stationary distribution (QSD) for $\nu$ if
$$\mathbb{P}_\eta(\nu_t\in A\mid\tau>t)=\eta(A)\qquad\text{for all }t\ge 0\text{ and all Borel sets }A\subset\mathcal{M}_F(E)\setminus\{0\}.$$

Problem: Determine existence, uniqueness, characterization, and domains of attraction of quasi-stationary distributions $\eta$ for the limiting superprocess $\nu$ in the almost-sure extinction regime. In particular, identify the Yaglom-type limits
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb{P}_\mu\bigl(\nu_t\in\,\cdot\,\bigm|\,\tau>t\bigr)$$
and describe the class of initial measures $\mu$ for which this limit exists and equals a QSD.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Quasi-stationary distributions for subcritical superprocesses have been investigated in subsequent works. In particular, for subcritical $(\xi,\psi)$-superprocesses, the existence of Yaglom limits and a characterization of all QSDs has been established under asymptotic conditions on the mean semigroup (e.g. Sun's "Quasi-stationary distributions for subcritical superprocesses"), and related results are available for continuous-state branching processes (Lambert 2007) and CSBPs with competition. The general problem in the full generality posed (arbitrary individual-based scaling limit with a.s. extinction) remains only partially resolved.

Consider the following Darwinian-evolution model with a continuous trait space $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$.

Microscopic individual-based particle system. At time $t \ge 0$ the population is described by a finite point measure
$$\nu_t^K = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{N_t} \delta_{x_i(t)} \in \mathcal{M}_F(X),$$
where $K \in \mathbb{N}$ is a scaling parameter (carrying capacity), $N_t$ is the population size, and $x_i(t) \in X$ is the trait of individual $i$. Each individual with trait $x$ undergoes, independently:
- clonal reproduction at rate $b(x)$, producing one offspring whose trait is either equal to $x$ (with probability $1-\mu(x)$) or distributed according to a mutation kernel $m(x, dy)$ (with probability $\mu(x)$);
- death at rate $d(x) + \tfrac{1}{K}\sum_{j=1}^{N_t} c(x, x_j(t))$, where $c(\cdot,\cdot) \ge 0$ is a competition kernel.

The rates $b, d, \mu, m, c$ are assumed bounded and sufficiently regular.

Macroscopic limit. Under appropriate initial conditions $\nu_0^K \to \xi_0$ in probability as $K \to \infty$, the process $(\nu_t^K)_{t\ge 0}$ converges in probability (in the Skorokhod topology on $\mathbb{D}([0,T], \mathcal{M}_F(X))$) to the unique deterministic measure-valued solution $(\xi_t)_{t\ge 0}$ of
$$\frac{d}{dt}\langle \xi_t, f\rangle = \int_X \Big( (1-\mu(x))b(x) f(x) + \mu(x) b(x)\!\!\int_X f(y)\, m(x,dy) - d(x) f(x) - f(x)\!\!\int_X c(x,y)\, \xi_t(dy)\Big) \xi_t(dx)$$
for every $f \in C_b(X)$.

Genealogies. For each individual present at time $t$ in the microscopic system, there is a well-defined ancestral lineage back to time $0$, and consequently a genealogical tree (or ultrametric measure space, in the sense of Greven–Pfaffelhuber–Winter) associated with a sample of individuals.

Problem. Provide a rigorous description of the genealogical structure both in the microscopic individual-based particle system (for fixed $K$) and in the macroscopic limit $\xi_t$. More precisely:

(a) For fixed $K$, construct, in a tractable analytic or probabilistic form (for instance as a marked tree, a lookdown construction, or a random ultrametric measure space), the law of the genealogy of a uniform sample of $n$ individuals alive at time $t$ in $\nu_t^K$.

(b) Identify the limit, as $K \to \infty$, of these sampled genealogies, and characterize it as a (possibly deterministic, possibly random) genealogical object associated with the measure-valued solution $(\xi_t)_{t\ge 0}$. In particular, determine whether and in what sense the macroscopic model admits an intrinsic genealogy lifting the dynamics on $\mathcal{M}_F(X)$.

Call a sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge 0}$ of distinct integers self-ordered if for all positive integers $m$ and $n$,
$$\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(a_n - a_k) \;\Big|\; \prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(a_m - a_k).$$
Known families of self-ordered integer sequences include:
(i) the sequence $a_n = n$ and, more generally, any affinely transformed sequence $(\alpha a_n + \beta)$ obtained from a self-ordered sequence;
(ii) for any nonconstant polynomial $f(X) \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ with $f \neq \pm X$ and any integer $b$ whose forward orbit $\{b, f(b), f(f(b)), \ldots\}$ is infinite, the orbit sequence $a_n = f^{(n)}(b)$.

Exhibit a self-ordered integer sequence that is not obtained, up to an affine transformation, from an iterative dynamical construction of the form (ii); or prove that no such sequence exists.

Fix integers $a, b$ and initial values $u_0, u_1 \in \mathbb{Z}$, and define the sequence $\{u_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ by the linear recurrence
$$u_{n+1} = a\, u_n + b\, u_{n-1}, \qquad n \geq 1.$$
Let $E = \{u_n : n \geq 0\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be the set of values of this sequence, and consider the ring of integer-valued polynomials on $E$,
$$\mathrm{Int}(E,\mathbb{Z}) = \{ f(X) \in \mathbb{Q}[X] : f(E) \subseteq \mathbb{Z} \}.$$
Fix a prime number $p$. For each integer $n \geq 0$, let $I_n \subseteq \mathbb{Q}$ be the fractional ideal of $\mathbb{Z}$ generated by $0$ together with the leading coefficients of all polynomials $f \in \mathrm{Int}(E,\mathbb{Z})$ with $\deg f \leq n$, and define the characteristic sequence
$$\varphi(n) = -v_p(I_n),$$
where $v_p$ denotes the $p$-adic valuation (so $\varphi(n)$ is the $p$-adic valuation of the corresponding denominator ideal). The sequence $\{\varphi(n)\}_{n \geq 0}$ is known to be superadditive, so by Fekete's lemma the limit
$$L(a,b,u_0,u_1,p) \;=\; \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\varphi(n)}{n}$$
exists in $[0,\infty]$.

Determine this limit explicitly as a function of $a$, $b$, $u_0$, $u_1$, and the prime $p$, for arbitrary integer parameters $a$ and $b$ (in particular for $|b| \neq 1$, where the case $b = 1$ — which covers the Fibonacci and Lucas sequences — has been treated previously).

Consider the combinatory logic built from the basic combinators $S$ and $K$, with terms formed by application. Recall the usual axioms of weak reduction:
- $Kxy \to x$,
- $Sxyz \to xz(yz)$.

Strong reduction (in the sense of Curry) is the smallest relation $\succ$ on combinatory terms that extends weak reduction, is compatible with application, and additionally validates the analogues of the $\xi$-rule and of $\eta$ in combinatory form. Equivalently, $\beta\eta$-strong reduction is the combinatory analogue of $\beta\eta$-reduction in the $\lambda$-calculus, in the sense that under the standard translations between $\lambda$-terms and combinators, $\beta\eta$-strong reduction corresponds to $\beta\eta$-reduction.

It is known that $\beta\eta$-strong reduction is confluent (Church–Rosser): whenever $M \succ^* N_1$ and $M \succ^* N_2$, there exists $P$ with $N_1 \succ^* P$ and $N_2 \succ^* P$. The only classically known proof of this fact proceeds by translating to the $\lambda$-calculus and invoking the confluence of $\lambda\beta\eta$-reduction.

Problem. Give a direct, self-contained proof of the confluence of $\beta\eta$-strong reduction for combinators, carried out entirely within combinatory logic and not relying on the confluence of $\lambda\beta\eta$-reduction in the $\lambda$-calculus.

Let types be the set of expressions built from a countable set of propositional variables using a single binary arrow constructor →. Consider the restricted combinatory logic whose basis consists of the four combinators

  B : (b → c) → (a → b) → (a → c),
  B′ : (a → b) → (b → c) → (a → c),
  I : a → a,
  W : (a → a → b) → (a → b),

with application as the only term-formation rule, and where typing follows the usual rules: each basis combinator may be assigned any substitution instance of its principal type schema, and if M has type σ → τ and N has type σ then (M N) has type τ.

A type τ is said to be inhabited in this system if there exists a closed term X built from B, B′, I, W by application such that X : τ is derivable.

Equivalently, consider the implicational fragment T→ of the propositional logic of ticket entailment, whose theorems coincide with the inhabited types of the BB′IW-system above.

Question: Is there an algorithm which, given any type τ as input, decides whether τ is inhabited in the BB′IW combinatory logic (equivalently, whether τ is a theorem of T→)?

Work in the untyped lambda calculus. A closed lambda term is called solvable if it has a head normal form (equivalently, if there exist closed terms N_1,...,N_k such that M N_1 ... N_k is beta-convertible to the identity); otherwise it is called unsolvable. A lambda theory is a congruence on lambda terms that contains beta-conversion. Let H denote the least lambda theory that equates all unsolvable closed terms. A combinator is a closed lambda term.

The range property for a lambda theory T asserts that for every combinator F, the set { [F M]_T : M is a closed lambda term }, where [ . ]_T denotes the equivalence class modulo T, is either a singleton or infinite.

Problem: Decide whether the range property holds for H. That is, prove that for every combinator F, either H ⊢ F M = F N for all closed terms M and N, or there exist infinitely many closed terms M_1, M_2, M_3, ... such that H ⊬ F M_i = F M_j for all i ≠ j; or else exhibit a combinator F for which both alternatives fail.

Work in the untyped lambda calculus / combinatory logic with the two basic combinators B and ω governed by the reduction rules

    B x y z  ⇒  x (y z),
    ω x      ⇒  x x.

A closed term built only by application from the symbols B and ω (an "applicative combination of B and ω") is a fixed-point combinator if for every term x one has

    Y x  =  x (Y x)

(equality being convertibility under the above rules, or at least β-equality in the lambda-calculus realization B = λxyz. x(yz), ω = λx. xx).

Question: Does there exist such an applicative combination of B and ω that is a fixed-point combinator? Either exhibit one explicitly, or prove that no fixed-point combinator can be obtained by applicative combination of B and ω alone.

A closed term built only by application from the symbols B and ω (an "applicative combination of B and ω") is a fixed-point combinator if for every term x one has

    Y x  =  x (Y x)

(equality being convertibility under the above rules, or at least β-equality in the lambda-calculus realization B = λxyz. x(yz), ω = λx. xx).

Question: Does there exist such an applicative combination of B and ω that is a fixed-point combinator? Either exhibit one explicitly, or prove that no fixed-point combinator can be obtained by applicative combination of B and ω alone.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem is listed in the TLCA list of open problems and we found no published solution. General surveys on fixed-point combinators (including Endrullis–Klop and related work on fpc generating schemes) do not report a resolution of the specific question of whether a fixed-point combinator can be built using only the combinators B and ω. The status therefore appears to be open.

Consider the simply typed lambda-calculus extended with positive recursive types, defined as follows. Types are built from a countable set of type variables and the arrow constructor →, together with a fixpoint constructor μp.τ where p is a type variable that occurs only positively in τ (a variable p occurs positively in p, in σ → τ if it occurs negatively in σ and positively in τ, and negatively in σ → τ if it occurs positively in σ and negatively in τ; under μp.τ the standard occurrence rules apply). The typing system extends simply typed λ-calculus with the introduction and elimination rules for μp.τ:

  Γ ⊢ M : τ[μp.τ / p]            Γ ⊢ M : μp.τ
  ───────────────────────         ─────────────────────────
  Γ ⊢ M : μp.τ                   Γ ⊢ M : τ[μp.τ / p]

(equivalently, μp.τ is identified with its unfolding τ[μp.τ / p]).

Let F_ω denote the higher-order polymorphic lambda-calculus of Girard, with type constructors of all finite kinds, universal quantification over all kinds, and the usual typing rules; a pure λ-term M is typable in F_ω if there is some assignment of F_ω-types to its free variables and a closed F_ω-type σ such that M : σ is derivable (after erasing type annotations).

Question: Does there exist a pure λ-term M that is typable in the system with positive recursive types described above, but is not typable in F_ω?

representations.normalized: Work in untyped combinatory logic over a countably infinite set of variables. A combinator is a closed term built from atomic constants and application; a proper combinator is one whose principal normal form has the shape $\lambda x_1\cdots\lambda x_n.\,M$ where $M$ is a (possibly empty) application of the variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$ (in particular, contains no constants other than these variables). A finite set $\mathcal{B}=\{C_1,\dots,C_k\}$ of proper combinators is called combinatorially complete (a basis) if for every $n\ge 0$ and every term $M$ of the untyped lambda calculus built from variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$ using application and abstraction, there exists a combinator $T$ over $\mathcal{B}$ such that $T\,x_1\cdots x_n =_\beta M$.\n\nProblem: Provide a decision procedure that, given as input a finite set $\mathcal{B}$ of proper combinators (each specified by its principal normal form), decides whether $\mathcal{B}$ is combinatorially complete. Equivalently, produce an abstraction algorithm parameterized by the finite set $\mathcal{B}$ which, applied to an arbitrary lambda term, either returns an equivalent term over $\mathcal{B}$ or reports a failure that certifies that $\mathcal{B}$ is not a basis.

The general basis decision problem for proper combinators in untyped combinatory logic, posed by Statman (1986/1993), is widely regarded as still open. Partial decidability results are known in restricted settings: Bokay (J. Functional Programming, 1998) and subsequent work give precise characterizations and decidability of the basis problem for the linear and affine lambda-calculi, and known results show that beyond order 2 various related problems become undecidable. No full algorithm for the unrestricted case is documented.

Work in the untyped lambda-calculus, whose terms are generated by the grammar M ::= x | (M M) | (λx.M) modulo α-conversion, with the one-step β-reduction relation →_β induced by the rule (λx.M) N →_β M[x := N] applied in any context, and its reflexive-transitive closure ↠_β. Fix an effective Gödel numbering of lambda-terms so that "effective" / "computable" refers to total recursive functions on the set of terms.

A one-step strategy is a computable function F from lambda-terms to lambda-terms such that for every term M, either F(M) = M (when M is in β-normal form) or M →_β F(M) (a single β-reduction step). Define:
 (a) F is one-step cofinal if for every term M and every reduction sequence M ↠_β N there exists k with N ↠_β F^k(M).
 (b) F is one-step Church-Rosser if for all terms M, N with M =_β N (β-convertible) there exist i, j with F^i(M) = F^j(N) (syntactic identity).
 (c) F is a one-step enumeration strategy if for every term M the iterates F^0(M), F^1(M), F^2(M), … enumerate (up to syntactic equality) the set { N : M ↠_β N } of all β-reducts of M.
 (d) A confluence function is a computable function G of two arguments such that whenever M ↠_β N₁ and M ↠_β N₂, the term G(N₁, N₂) satisfies N₁ ↠_β G(N₁, N₂) and N₂ ↠_β G(N₁, N₂).

For combinatory logic (with combinators S, K and the usual reduction rules) it is known that there exist effective one-step cofinal, one-step Church-Rosser, and one-step enumeration strategies, while no effective confluence function exists.

Determine which of these four results carry over to the untyped lambda-calculus: namely, decide for each of (a), (b), (c) whether an effective one-step strategy of that kind exists for β-reduction, and decide whether an effective confluence function exists for β-reduction.

(i) Combinatory logic CL (terms built from the constants S, K and application) with weak reduction →w (the contextual closure of the rules Kxy →w x and Sxyz →w xz(yz)); or

(ii) The untyped λ-calculus, with either β-reduction or βη-reduction.

A closed term M is called a uniform universal generator if there exists a non-trivial context C[∗] such that, for every closed term N of the system,
   M ↠ C[N].

Question: Does a uniform universal generator exist in CL under weak reduction? Does one exist in the λ-calculus under β-reduction? Under βη-reduction?

representations.normalized:
Background. Intersection types extend simple types by allowing finite intersections: types are generated by the grammar τ ::= a | τ → τ | τ ∧ τ, where a ranges over a fixed countable set of type atoms. A typing context Γ is a finite assignment of intersection types to term variables of the untyped λ-calculus. Standard intersection type assignment derives judgments Γ ⊢ M : τ via rules for variables, application, abstraction, intersection introduction (Γ ⊢ M : τ and Γ ⊢ M : σ imply Γ ⊢ M : τ ∧ σ), and intersection elimination (Γ ⊢ M : τ ∧ σ implies Γ ⊢ M : τ and Γ ⊢ M : σ).

Setup. Let E be a finite set of equations between intersection types, i.e., a finite set of unordered pairs {τ_i, σ_i}. Let =_E denote the smallest congruence on intersection types (with respect to all type-forming operations) that contains E. Extend the intersection type assignment system by adding the conversion rule

   Γ ⊢ M : τ     (τ =_E σ)
   ─────────────────────
        Γ ⊢ M : σ

Call the resulting system IT(E). A term M is strongly normalizing if every β-reduction sequence starting from M terminates. The system IT(E) is said to have the strong normalization property if every λ-term typable in IT(E) is strongly normalizing.

Problem. Characterize, in terms of structural properties of E, exactly those finite sets E of equations between intersection types for which the system IT(E) has the (strong) normalization property. In particular, provide necessary and sufficient conditions on E that guarantee strong normalization of all IT(E)-typable terms.

Consider the type assignment system Fω (the Curry-style higher-order polymorphic lambda calculus), whose type constructors are stratified by order: order-0 constructors are types, order-1 constructors are functions from types to types, and in general order-(n+1) constructors map lower-order constructors to types. For each n ≥ 0, let Fn denote the subsystem of Fω in which all type constructors used (in types, in quantifiers, and in type-application reductions appearing in type derivations) have order at most n; thus F0 is essentially the polymorphic lambda calculus (system F restricted to type-level variables), and the systems form an increasing hierarchy F0 ⊆ F1 ⊆ F2 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ Fω = ⋃_{n} Fn with respect to typability of pure (untyped) lambda terms.

Question: Does this typability hierarchy collapse at level F1? Equivalently, prove or disprove: every pure lambda term M that is typable in Fω is already typable in F1.

Consider the lambda calculus with the polymorphic type assignment system whose types are built from type variables by the formation rules T ::= a | T → T | ∀a. T. Assign to every type variable a a natural number called its level (or order). Define the stratified polymorphic type assignment system of order n, written ⊢_n, as the natural-deduction style assignment system whose rules are the usual ones of Curry-style System F (variable, →-introduction, →-elimination, ∀-introduction with the standard eigenvariable side condition), except that the ∀-elimination rule

   Γ ⊢ M : ∀a. A         Γ ⊢ M : A[B/a]

is restricted by requiring that the level of the quantified variable a be at most n (equivalently, only quantifiers over variables of level ≤ n may be instantiated).

It is known that:
 • ⊢_0 has exactly the typing power of the simply typed (Curry) λ-calculus,
 • ⊢_1 types exactly the λ-terms that are β-normalizable (i.e. exactly the terms whose normal forms exist).

Problem. For every integer n ≥ 2, give an exact characterization of the set of (untyped) λ-terms M that are typable in ⊢_n, that is, for which there exist a context Γ and a type A with Γ ⊢_n M : A.

Consider the simply typed lambda-calculus extended with finite products (including the unit/terminal type) and finite sums (including the empty/initial type), with terms formed using lambda-abstraction, application, pairing, projections, injections, case analysis, and the empty-case eliminator. Let =β denote the standard β-equational theory of this calculus and let =βη denote its extension by the η-rules for arrow types, product types (including surjective pairing and unit collapse), and sum types (including the η-rule for the empty type and the commuting/η-rule for sums).

A binary relation = on typed terms is called a typically-ambiguous congruence if it is a congruence with respect to all term constructors and is closed under type substitutions (i.e., if M = N then for every substitution σ of types for type variables, σM = σN). Such a relation is consistent if it does not equate all closed terms of some inhabited type (equivalently, if it is not the total relation).

Question: Is =βη the maximum consistent typically-ambiguous congruence containing =β? Equivalently, is every typically-ambiguous congruence relation that properly extends =βη necessarily inconsistent?

Consider the following setting. Fix a finite signature of type constructors, each with a fixed arity and a fixed variance (covariant or contravariant) in each argument, together with a partial order ≤₀ on the 0-ary constructors (the base types). A simple type term τ is built from a countable set of type variables and the constructors. The non-structural subtype order ≤ on (possibly infinite, regular) trees is the largest relation such that: (i) on base types it agrees with ≤₀; and (ii) for constructors of equal or different shape, ≤ is defined non-structurally, meaning, in particular, that constructors of different outermost shape can be related when the order on base types is non-trivial (so the ordering is not restricted to terms of identical structure as in structural subtyping). A simple subtyping constraint is an inequality τ ≤ τ′ between type terms with variables. Given a finite set of such constraints C = {τᵢ ≤ τ′ᵢ}_{i=1,…,n} and two further type terms τ and τ′, the entailment problem asks whether every assignment of (regular) tree types to the variables that satisfies all constraints in C also satisfies τ ≤ τ′; this is written C ⊨ τ ≤ τ′.

Question: Is this subtype entailment problem decidable for simple subtyping constraints interpreted over non-structurally ordered trees?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The decidability of entailment for non-structural subtype constraints is a long-standing open problem. Rehof and Henglein proved PSPACE-hardness and conjectured PSPACE-completeness but no complete algorithm is known. Niehren and collaborators reformulated the problem via automata theory and word equations, explaining its difficulty, and identified decidable fragments, but the general question remains open as of the most recent available literature.

Let System F denote the polymorphic λ-calculus with types generated by the grammar
  T ::= X | T → T | ∀X. T,
and terms generated by variables, application, λ-abstraction, type abstraction ΛX.t, and type application t T, equipped with the usual β-reduction rules together with the η-rule for both ordinary λ-abstractions and type abstractions (the βη polymorphic λ-calculus).

Following Mendler's 1987 formulation, a Mendler-style recursive type for a type expression F[X] (with X possibly occurring in negative positions) is a type μX.F[X] together with:
 • a constructor in_F : ∀X.(X → μX.F[X]) → F[X] → μX.F[X], or equivalently an isomorphism between μX.F[X] and F[μX.F[X]] given by introduction and elimination operators;
 • a recursor R_F : ∀C. (∀X.(X → C) → F[X] → C) → μX.F[X] → C
satisfying the expected reduction equations relating R_F applied to a constructed value to the application of its argument.

Say that Mendler-style recursive types are definable in System F (with βη) when, for every type expression F[X], one can exhibit a closed System-F type μX.F[X] and closed System-F terms implementing in_F and R_F such that the defining equations of the recursor hold modulo βη-conversion of System F.

Question: Are Mendler-style recursive types (in the 1987 sense, admitting non-positive type expressions F[X]) definable in System F with βη-conversion?

Work in the pure untyped λ-calculus. For a set O of λ-terms (the "observables"), define the contextual (observational) equivalence ∼_O on λ-terms by: M ∼_O N iff for every context C[·], C[M] ∈ O ⇔ C[N] ∈ O (where membership is taken up to β-conversion). Recall the following sets of λ-terms:

• W, the set of weak head normal forms (terms of the form λx.P or x P_1 … P_k).
• T, the set of top normal forms (terms that are either an abstraction or have a variable in head position, i.e. terms that are not head-reducible to a redex at the root—equivalently, root-stable terms).
• SA, the set of strongly active terms: a term M is strongly active if for every context C[·], C[M] has a head normal form.
• Given a set X of λ-terms, SA_X, the set of strongly active terms depending on X: terms M such that for every context C[·], whenever C[M] has a head normal form, that head normal form involves a term from X in a prescribed way (active relative to X).
• HA, the set of head active terms: terms that reduce to an unsolvable of order ∞ (mute terms / those whose Böhm tree is ⊥ and which are "head-active" in the standard sense).

Problem. For each of the five observable sets O ∈ {W, T, SA, SA_X, HA}, exhibit a notion of tree associated to each λ-term M (i.e. a tree-like normal form Tree_O(M), in the spirit of Böhm trees, Lévy–Longo trees, or Berarducci trees) such that for all λ-terms M, N:

   M ∼_O N  ⇐⇒  Tree_O(M) = Tree_O(N) (possibly up to a suitable infinitary η-expansion / equivalence relation on trees that must also be specified).

In each case, give a precise definition of the tree representation and prove that the resulting equality on trees coincides exactly with the contextual equivalence ∼_O.

Work in the untyped λ-calculus. Let Λ° denote the set of closed λ-terms, and let λβ denote the standard β-conversion theory on λ-terms. A closed term E ∈ Λ° is called easy if, for every closed term M ∈ Λ°, the equational theory λβ ∪ {M = E} is consistent (i.e., does not prove every equation between λ-terms). A closed term E ∈ Λ° is called simple easy if for every inverse limit λ-model D constructed as a filter model over a suitable intersection type system, and for every element d of D, there exists a continuous interpretation of E into D whose value equals d (equivalently, E can be forced to denote any prescribed element in such filter models). It is known that every simple easy term is easy.

Question: Does the converse hold? That is, is every easy closed λ-term necessarily simple easy?

Work in the simply typed lambda-calculus. Fix a (possibly infinite) set A of atomic type variables (atoms). Simple types over A are generated by the grammar τ ::= a | τ → τ where a ranges over A. Terms are the usual simply typed lambda terms, considered modulo βη-equivalence.

The higher-order matching problem is the following decision problem: given a closed simply typed equation t = u, where t is a term of the simply typed lambda calculus containing free variables (the "unknowns") of arbitrary types built from atoms in A, and u is a closed normal-form term, decide whether there exists a substitution σ assigning closed lambda terms to the unknowns of t such that σ(t) =_{βη} u.

A type ρ is a retract of a type τ, written ρ ◁ τ, if there exist closed simply typed lambda terms C : ρ → τ and D : τ → ρ such that D ∘ C =_{βη} λx.x. The retraction problem is: given ρ and τ built from atoms in A, decide whether ρ ◁ τ holds.

Question: Is the higher-order matching problem decidable when types may be built from an arbitrary (more than one) number of atomic type variables? In particular, is the retraction problem ρ ◁ τ decidable in the many-atoms setting?

Stirling's 2009 proof establishes decidability of higher-order matching only for types built from a single atom; the game-theoretic argument relies on this restriction. The generalization to many atoms, including the corresponding retraction problem ρ ◁ τ, does not appear to have been resolved in the subsequent literature. Partial results exist (e.g., proof systems for affine βη-retractions and tableau-based decision procedures for restricted retraction problems), but no full decidability proof or undecidability result for the many-atoms higher-order matching problem appears in the located sources.

representations.normalized:
Background. A CPO (complete partial order) is a partially ordered set in which every directed subset has a least upper bound. A function between CPOs is Scott continuous if it is monotone and preserves least upper bounds of directed subsets. A reflexive CPO is a CPO D together with a continuous retraction (application, abstraction) between D and the CPO [D → D] of Scott continuous self-maps of D; every reflexive CPO induces a model of the untyped λ-calculus, whose equational theory is the set of equations M = N between closed λ-terms that hold in the model. The model is called extensional when the retraction is an isomorphism. A reflexive CPO model is called continuously complete if, in addition to directed suprema, it has suprema of all chains indexed by ordinals (i.e. all ordinal-indexed monotone chains have least upper bounds preserved by the application/abstraction maps). Filter models are the standard class of λ-models constructed from intersection type systems; they form a subclass of (continuously complete) CPO models.

Let λβ denote the least equational λ-theory (β-conversion) and λβη the least extensional λ-theory (βη-conversion).

Question. Does there exist a continuously complete CPO model of the untyped λ-calculus whose equational theory is exactly λβ? Does there exist a continuously complete CPO model (necessarily extensional) whose equational theory is exactly λβη? Equivalently, is λβ (respectively λβη) precisely the set of equations valid in all (extensional) continuously complete CPO models of the λ-calculus; or is there a filter model whose theory is exactly λβ or exactly λβη?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of whether there is a continuous (CPO) model of the untyped λ-calculus with theory exactly λβ or exactly λβη is widely cited as a longstanding open problem. Strong partial negative results are known: extensional reflexive Scott domains are not complete for λβη, and effective CPO models cannot have theory λβ or λβη (their order theories are not r.e.). Moving to ω₁-continuous models, a reflexive domain whose theory is exactly λβη has been constructed, but the question for the standard continuously complete CPO/filter-model setting (and for λβ) remains open as of currently available literature.

The Expansion Postponement conjecture, due to Pollack (1992), remains open in general. Partial results exist: it has been established for all normalising PTSs (Poll 1998) and for further classes via an induction principle and via cut elimination in sequent calculi for PTSs.
