Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be a symmetric positive definite matrix with distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots > \lambda_n > 0$ and let $1 \le p < n$. Consider the following continuous-time matrix differential equations on $\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}$, which arise as gradient/non-gradient learning rules for extracting principal and minor components of $A$:

(i) Oja's principal subspace flow
$$\dot X = (I_n - XX^{\top})\,A\,X.$$

(ii) Oja's minor subspace flow
$$\dot X = -(I_n - XX^{\top})\,A\,X.$$

(iii) Xu's (LMSER) flow
$$\dot X = A X - X X^{\top} A X - X (X^{\top} A X - X^{\top} X\, X^{\top} A X).$$

(iv) Brockett's double-bracket flow on the orthogonal group: with $N = \operatorname{diag}(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n)$, $\mu_1>\cdots>\mu_n$, and $H(t) = \Theta(t) A \Theta(t)^{\top}$ for $\Theta \in O(n)$,
$$\dot H = [H,[H,N]].$$

Address the following questions for each of the flows (i)–(iv):

(a) Determine the complete set of equilibria and classify them by linearization (hyperbolic/non-hyperbolic, stable/unstable, saddle).

(b) Prove or disprove that every bounded trajectory converges to a single equilibrium point (as opposed to converging only to a connected set of equilibria), and characterize the set of initial conditions from which the trajectory is bounded.

(c) Identify the stable manifolds and basins of attraction of the asymptotically stable equilibria; in particular, for the principal subspace flow (i), describe explicitly the open dense set of initial conditions $X(0)$ for which $X(t)$ converges to a matrix whose columns span the dominant $p$-dimensional invariant subspace of $A$.

(d) For the minor subspace flow (ii) — known to be unstable in the unbounded ambient state space — determine whether there exists an invariant submanifold (e.g.\ the Stiefel manifold $\operatorname{St}(p,n) = \{X : X^{\top}X = I_p\}$) on which the flow is well-posed and globally convergent to a matrix spanning the minor $p$-dimensional invariant subspace, and analyze stability on and transverse to this submanifold.

(e) Establish convergence rates (exponential vs.\ polynomial) near each asymptotically stable equilibrium, and compare the global dynamical behavior (e.g.\ Morse–Lyapunov structure, gradient structure with respect to natural Riemannian metrics) of the four flows.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem (Problem 3.9 in the 2004 Princeton compilation of unsolved problems in systems and control) was posed by Helmke, Yoshizawa, Evans, Manton, and Mareels. Subsequent literature (Yan–Helmke–Moore, Manton, Chen–Amari, Peng–Yi, and others) has obtained partial results: gradient/Riemannian structure of Brockett's, Oja's principal, and Xu's flows is known, with global convergence to single equilibria established for the principal-subspace versions on suitable domains. Minor-component flows are known to be generically unstable in the unconstrained formulation, with stable variants requiring projection onto the Stiefel manifold. A fully unified, complete global dynamical classification of all four flows (including basins of attraction and minor-component cases) does not appear to have been published, so the problem is still considered (at least partially) open.

Consider a family of linear time-invariant systems on $\mathbb{R}^n$ indexed by a finite set $\mathcal{M}=\{1,\dots,m\}$:
$$\dot x(t) = A_{\sigma(t)} x(t) + B_{\sigma(t)} u(t), \qquad y(t) = C_{\sigma(t)} x(t) + D_{\sigma(t)} u(t),$$
where, for each $i\in\mathcal{M}$, $A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, $B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}$, $C_i\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}$, $D_i\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times p}$ are given matrices. The switching signal $\sigma:[0,\infty)\to\mathcal{M}$ is an arbitrary measurable, piecewise constant function with finitely many discontinuities on each bounded interval. Assume that the switched system is uniformly exponentially stable, meaning there exist constants $c,\lambda>0$ such that for every switching signal $\sigma$, the state transition matrix $\Phi_\sigma(t,s)$ of $\dot x = A_{\sigma(t)} x$ satisfies $\|\Phi_\sigma(t,s)\|\le c e^{-\lambda(t-s)}$ for all $t\ge s\ge 0$.

Define the $\mathcal{L}_2$-induced gain of the switched system as
$$\gamma := \sup_{\sigma}\;\sup_{0\ne u\in L_2([0,\infty);\mathbb{R}^p)}\; \frac{\|y\|_{L_2}}{\|u\|_{L_2}},$$
where $y$ is the output produced by initial condition $x(0)=0$, input $u$, and switching signal $\sigma$.

Problem: Provide a constructive, computable characterization of $\gamma$. In particular:
(a) Develop an effective procedure (e.g., a finite-dimensional convex program, a Riccati-type condition, or a converging sequence of upper and lower bounds with explicit error estimates) that computes $\gamma$ to arbitrary accuracy for any given data $\{(A_i,B_i,C_i,D_i)\}_{i\in\mathcal{M}}$.
(b) Determine the computational complexity (in particular, the decidability) of testing whether $\gamma\le \gamma_0$ for a given rational threshold $\gamma_0>0$.
(c) Characterize the "worst-case" switching signal $\sigma^\ast$ (when it exists) that attains, or approaches, the supremum, and describe its structural properties.

Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth vector field, and consider the dynamical system $\dot{x}(t) = f(x(t))$ on the state space $\mathbb{R}^n$ (or an open subset thereof). A partition $\mathcal{P} = \{P_i\}_{i \in I}$ of the state space is a collection of pairwise disjoint connected regions whose union is the whole state space. Given such a partition, the associated quantized system is the discrete-event system whose state at any time $t$ is the index $q(t) = i$ such that $x(t) \in P_i$, and whose transitions are the events $i \to j$ that occur whenever a trajectory of $\dot{x} = f(x)$ leaves $P_i$ and enters $P_j$ through their common boundary. The quantized system is called deterministic if, for every region $P_i$ and every boundary face of $P_i$, all trajectories of $f$ that cross that face do so into the same neighbouring region $P_j$ (equivalently, the symbolic sequence of visited regions is uniquely determined by the initial region rather than by the precise initial state inside it).

Problem: For an arbitrary given vector field $f$, find (i.e. construct, or characterize the existence of) a partition $\mathcal{P}$ of the state space such that the associated quantized system is deterministic in the sense above.

Consider a stochastic N-machine flowshop in which machines are arranged in tandem and process a single product type. Let α(t) be a finite-state, continuous-time Markov chain on a state space M = {α^1, …, α^p} ⊂ R^N representing the random capacities (maximum production rates) of the N machines, with given generator Q. Let x(t) = (x_1(t), …, x_N(t)) ∈ R^N denote the state of the system, where x_i(t) is the buffer content (work-in-process for i = 1, …, N−1) and x_N(t) is the surplus/backlog of finished goods relative to a constant demand rate z > 0. The state dynamics are
   ẋ_1(t) = u_1(t) − u_2(t),
   ẋ_i(t) = u_i(t) − u_{i+1}(t),  i = 2, …, N−1,
   ẋ_N(t) = u_N(t) − z,
with initial conditions x(0) = x and α(0) = α, where the control u(t) = (u_1(t), …, u_N(t)) ∈ R^N_+ is required to satisfy the capacity constraints 0 ≤ u_i(t) ≤ α_i(t) and the non-negativity-of-work-in-process constraints x_i(t) ≥ 0 for i = 1, …, N−1, for all t ≥ 0. A control u(·) is called admissible if it is {F_t}-progressively measurable (where F_t = σ(α(s) : s ≤ t)) and satisfies these constraints almost surely.

Given a discount rate ρ > 0 and a running cost G : R^N × R^N_+ → R_+ that is jointly convex and satisfies polynomial growth (typical choice: G(x,u) = c^+·x^+ + c^−·x^− with componentwise penalties for inventory and backlog), define the expected discounted cost

   J(x, α, u(·)) = E ∫_0^∞ e^{−ρt} G(x(t), u(t)) dt.

Problem. Find an admissible feedback control u*(·) that minimizes J(x, α, u(·)) over all admissible controls, and give an explicit characterization (e.g., via the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation and threshold/turnpike structure) of the optimal feedback policy and of the value function V(x, α) = inf_{u(·)} J(x, α, u(·)) for general N ≥ 2.

The problem of optimal feedback production control for the stochastic N-machine flowshop with Markov-modulated capacities and discounted cost is studied in a series of works by Presman, Sethi, H. Zhang and Q. Zhang. Existence/uniqueness of viscosity solutions of the HJB equation and asymptotic (hierarchical) optimality results are known, but an explicit closed-form characterization of the optimal feedback policy and value function for general N ≥ 2 remains open; only partial structural results (e.g., for N = 2 or in long-run-average asymptotic limits) are available.

Problem 1 (Decentralized control with communication between controllers). Let a plant be modeled by a control system

  x(t+1) = f(x(t), u_1(t), …, u_r(t), w(t)),    y_i(t) = h_i(x(t), v_i(t)),  i = 1, …, r,

where x(t) ∈ X is the state, u_i(t) ∈ U_i is the control input of controller i, w(t) is a process disturbance, y_i(t) ∈ Y_i is the partial observation available to controller i, and v_i(t) is a measurement noise. A fixed performance criterion J (e.g. a cost functional, a specification language, or a closed-loop property) is given.

For every ordered pair (i, j) with i ≠ j, controller i is allowed to send to controller j, at each time t, a message m_{ij}(t) ∈ M_{ij} from a finite (or otherwise constrained) alphabet, where m_{ij}(t) is a causal function of the past observations of controller i and of the past messages controller i has received. Each controller i then produces u_i(t) as a causal function of its own past observations y_i and of the past messages {m_{ki}}_{k ≠ i} it has received.

Synthesize the r local control laws together with the family of communication protocols {m_{ij}}_{i ≠ j} so that the performance criterion J is optimized (or, when J is a specification, so that the specification is satisfied). In particular, characterize when such a tuple (controllers + communication protocols) exists, give constructive procedures producing it, and quantify the trade-off between the cardinality / rate of the communication alphabets and the achievable performance.

Problem 2 (Decentralized control of a discrete-event system with communication between supervisors). Let G = (Q, Σ, δ, q_0) be a discrete-event system (generator), with event set Σ partitioned into controllable events Σ_c and uncontrollable events Σ_uc, generating the language L(G) ⊆ Σ*. Let K ⊆ L(G) be a given specification (legal) language. For each i = 1, …, r, supervisor S_i has an observation mask P_i : Σ* → Σ_{o,i}* (natural projection onto its observable events Σ_{o,i} ⊆ Σ) and is allowed to control only the events in Σ_{c,i} ⊆ Σ_c.

For every ordered pair (i, j) with i ≠ j, supervisor i may send to supervisor j a message in an alphabet Δ_{ij}, where each sent message is a causal function of the local observation history of i and of the messages already received by i. Each supervisor S_j chooses its control pattern (enable/disable decision over Σ_{c,j}) as a causal function of P_j applied to the executed string and of the received messages.

Synthesize the r local supervisors together with all inter-supervisor communication maps so that the closed-loop language equals K (or is as close to K as possible under a given partial order on sublanguages of L(G)). Determine existence conditions, provide a synthesis algorithm, and characterize minimal communication (smallest alphabets / fewest transmissions) required to achieve the specification.

Consider nonlinear evolution equations on an infinite-dimensional state space, for example boundary-controlled nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations of the form
  u_t(x,t) = u_{xx}(x,t) + f(x, u(x,t), u_x(x,t)), x ∈ (0,1), t > 0,
  u(0,t) = 0,
  u(1,t) = U(t),
with state u(·,t) in a suitable Banach (or Hilbert) function space, where f is a smooth nonlinearity that may render the uncontrolled equilibrium u ≡ 0 unstable, and where U(t) is the scalar boundary control input.

The classical (finite-dimensional) backstepping method designs a stabilizing state-feedback for strict-feedback nonlinear ODE systems by recursively constructing a coordinate transformation z = T(x) and a feedback law that maps the closed-loop system to a target system whose origin is globally asymptotically stable. For linear PDEs, an analogous infinite-dimensional backstepping method has been developed using a Volterra integral transformation
  w(x,t) = u(x,t) − ∫_0^x k(x,y) u(y,t) dy,
together with a boundary feedback U(t) = ∫_0^1 k(1,y) u(y,t) dy, which converts the open-loop unstable PDE into an exponentially stable target PDE; the kernel k is determined by a well-posed hyperbolic PDE.

Problem. Develop a systematic infinite-dimensional backstepping methodology for general nonlinear partial differential equations. Specifically:
(a) Construct an invertible (possibly nonlinear, e.g. spatial Volterra-series) state transformation and a boundary (or distributed) feedback law that maps a broad class of nonlinear parabolic (or hyperbolic) PDEs with boundary actuation into a chosen exponentially stable target nonlinear PDE.
(b) Establish well-posedness of the resulting kernel equations (the recursive sequence of PDEs determining the multilinear kernels of the Volterra transformation), prove convergence of the Volterra series in an appropriate function-space norm, and identify the largest class of nonlinearities f for which such a design succeeds.
(c) Prove global (or semiglobal) asymptotic stability, with quantitative decay rates, of the closed-loop system in the chosen norm.

Significant progress has been made since 2004 on infinite-dimensional backstepping for nonlinear PDEs. Vazquez and Krstic developed a Volterra-series backstepping design for 1-D parabolic PDEs with Volterra-type nonlinearities, and subsequent work has extended the method to various classes of nonlinear hyperbolic and parabolic PDEs, with recent neural-operator approximations of the gain kernels. However, a fully general nonlinear infinite-dimensional backstepping framework (handling arbitrary smooth nonlinearities with global stability guarantees) remains open, and current surveys continue to list it as an area of active research.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\Gamma = \partial\Omega$, filled with an isotropic elastic medium of density $\rho > 0$ and Lamé parameters $\lambda, \mu$ satisfying $\mu > 0$ and $3\lambda + 2\mu > 0$ (all smooth functions of $x \in \overline{\Omega}$). For a vector-valued boundary control $f : \Gamma \times [0,T] \to \mathbb{R}^3$, consider the dynamical Lamé system
$$
\rho\, u_{tt} - \mu\,\Delta u - (\lambda+\mu)\nabla(\operatorname{div} u) - (\nabla \lambda)\,\operatorname{div} u - 2(\nabla \mu \cdot \nabla)\,u - (\nabla \mu)\times \operatorname{curl} u = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega \times (0,T),
$$
$$
u\big|_{t=0} = 0,\qquad u_t\big|_{t=0} = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega,
$$
$$
u\big|_{\Gamma\times[0,T]} = f.
$$
For $T > 0$ and controls $f \in L^2(\Gamma\times[0,T];\mathbb{R}^3)$ supported in $[0,T]$, define the reachable set at time $T$ as the pair-valued set
$$
\mathcal{U}^T := \big\{\, \{u^f(\cdot,T),\, u^f_t(\cdot,T)\} \;:\; f \in L^2(\Gamma\times[0,T];\mathbb{R}^3)\,\big\} \subset L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)\times H^{-1}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3),
$$
together with its component projections $\mathcal{U}^T_0$ (first slot) and $\mathcal{U}^T_1$ (second slot).

Let $c_p = \sqrt{(\lambda+2\mu)/\rho}$ and $c_s = \sqrt{\mu/\rho}$ denote the local speeds of the compressional (fast, $p$-) and shear (slow, $s$-) waves, and for $\tau > 0$ let $\Omega^\tau_p$ and $\Omega^\tau_s$ denote the subdomains of $\Omega$ filled, respectively, by $p$- and $s$-waves issuing from $\Gamma$ within time $\tau$ (defined via the eikonal distances associated with $c_p$ and $c_s$).

Describe the structure of the reachable set $\mathcal{U}^T$ for arbitrary $T > 0$. In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Determine the closure of $\mathcal{U}^T$ (and of its projections $\mathcal{U}^T_0$, $\mathcal{U}^T_1$) inside $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)\times H^{-1}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)$ as an explicit subspace defined by geometric/analytic conditions related to $\Omega^T_p$ and $\Omega^T_s$.
\item Decide whether $\mathcal{U}^T$ has finite or infinite codimension in the natural energy space, and identify a complete set of obstructions to approximate controllability of the full state $\{u(\cdot,T),u_t(\cdot,T)\}$.
\item Characterise those times $T$ and configurations $(\Omega,\lambda,\mu,\rho)$ for which the second component $\mathcal{U}^T_1$ fails to be dense even in $H^{-1}(\Omega^T_s;\mathbb{R}^3)$.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\Gamma = \partial\Omega$, filled with an isotropic elastic medium of density $\rho > 0$ and Lamé parameters $\lambda, \mu$ satisfying $\mu > 0$ and $3\lambda + 2\mu > 0$ (all smooth functions of $x \in \overline{\Omega}$). For a vector-valued boundary control $f : \Gamma \times [0,T] \to \mathbb{R}^3$, consider the dynamical Lamé system
$$
\rho\, u_{tt} - \mu\,\Delta u - (\lambda+\mu)\nabla(\operatorname{div} u) - (\nabla \lambda)\,\operatorname{div} u - 2(\nabla \mu \cdot \nabla)\,u - (\nabla \mu)\times \operatorname{curl} u = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega \times (0,T),
$$
$$
u\big|_{t=0} = 0,\qquad u_t\big|_{t=0} = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega,
$$
$$
u\big|_{\Gamma\times[0,T]} = f.
$$
For $T > 0$ and controls $f \in L^2(\Gamma\times[0,T];\mathbb{R}^3)$ supported in $[0,T]$, define the reachable set at time $T$ as the pair-valued set
$$
\mathcal{U}^T := \big\{\, \{u^f(\cdot,T),\, u^f_t(\cdot,T)\} \;:\; f \in L^2(\Gamma\times[0,T];\mathbb{R}^3)\,\big\} \subset L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)\times H^{-1}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3),
$$
together with its component projections $\mathcal{U}^T_0$ (first slot) and $\mathcal{U}^T_1$ (second slot).

Let $c_p = \sqrt{(\lambda+2\mu)/\rho}$ and $c_s = \sqrt{\mu/\rho}$ denote the local speeds of the compressional (fast, $p$-) and shear (slow, $s$-) waves, and for $\tau > 0$ let $\Omega^\tau_p$ and $\Omega^\tau_s$ denote the subdomains of $\Omega$ filled, respectively, by $p$- and $s$-waves issuing from $\Gamma$ within time $\tau$ (defined via the eikonal distances associated with $c_p$ and $c_s$).

Describe the structure of the reachable set $\mathcal{U}^T$ for arbitrary $T > 0$. In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Determine the closure of $\mathcal{U}^T$ (and of its projections $\mathcal{U}^T_0$, $\mathcal{U}^T_1$) inside $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)\times H^{-1}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)$ as an explicit subspace defined by geometric/analytic conditions related to $\Omega^T_p$ and $\Omega^T_s$.
\item Decide whether $\mathcal{U}^T$ has finite or infinite codimension in the natural energy space, and identify a complete set of obstructions to approximate controllability of the full state $\{u(\cdot,T),u_t(\cdot,T)\}$.
\item Characterise those times $T$ and configurations $(\Omega,\lambda,\mu,\rho)$ for which the second component $\mathcal{U}^T_1$ fails to be dense even in $H^{-1}(\Omega^T_s;\mathbb{R}^3)$.
\end{enumerate}

The problem on the structure of reachable sets for the dynamical Lamé system with boundary control was posed by Belishev (Problem 5.2 in the 2004 collection). Partial results are known: continuity of the input-to-state map in $L^2$, approximate controllability of the first component over the subdomain filled by shear waves, and recovery of the response operator $R_\infty$ from $R_{2T_0}$ for sufficiently large $T_0$ (Belishev–Lasiecka 2002). A 2013 paper "Reachable sets of a Lamé type dynamical system" extends some results, but a full description of $\mathcal{U}^T$ for arbitrary $T>0$ does not appear to have been achieved; the problem appears still open.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be an unbounded open set with smooth boundary, let $\omega \subset \Omega$ be a non-empty open subset (the control region), and let $T>0$. Consider the controlled heat equation
\[
\begin{cases} \partial_t u - \Delta u = h\,\chi_\omega & \text{in } (0,T)\times\Omega,\\ u = 0 & \text{on } (0,T)\times\partial\Omega,\\ u(0,\cdot) = u_0 & \text{in }\Omega,\end{cases}
\]
where $u_0 \in L^2(\Omega)$ and $h \in L^2((0,T)\times\omega)$ is the control. The system is said to be null-controllable at time $T$ if for every $u_0 \in L^2(\Omega)$ there exists a control $h$ such that the corresponding solution satisfies $u(T,\cdot) \equiv 0$ in $\Omega$.

Characterize the pairs $(\Omega,\omega)$ with $\Omega$ unbounded for which null-controllability holds at every (equivalently, some) time $T>0$. In particular:

(a) When $\Omega = (0,\infty)$ and the control acts at the boundary point $x=0$ (boundary control), determine for which initial data $u_0 \in L^2(0,\infty)$ null-controllability can be achieved in finite time, and describe the obstruction (it is known that no nontrivial compactly supported smooth datum can be driven to zero in finite time).

(b) When $\omega \subset \Omega$ has finite Lebesgue measure but $\Omega\setminus\omega$ is unbounded, decide whether the system is null-controllable; if not, identify the largest class of initial data that can be driven to zero in time $T$.

(c) Provide a geometric/spectral characterization of those unbounded geometries $(\Omega,\omega)$ ensuring null-controllability, analogous to the Lebeau--Robbiano result for bounded domains.

The problem is a long-standing open problem proposed by Micu and Zuazua. Substantial partial progress exists: negative results show lack of null-controllability when the uncontrolled region is unbounded (e.g. heat equation on the half-line via boundary control, or bounded control region in an unbounded domain), while positive results are known when the uncontrolled region $\Omega\setminus\omega$ is bounded (Cabanillas–De Menezes–Zuazua, and later works using Carleman estimates). A complete geometric characterization for unbounded domains remains unresolved.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega=\overline{\Gamma_0}\cup\overline{\Gamma_1}$, where $\Gamma_0$ and $\Gamma_1$ are disjoint relatively open subsets and $\Gamma_1\neq\emptyset$. Consider the wave system with Neumann boundary control $u$ on $\Gamma_1$ and collocated velocity observation $y$ on $\Gamma_1$:
\[
\begin{cases}
w_{tt}(x,t)=\Delta w(x,t), & x\in\Omega,\;t\ge 0,\\[2pt]
w(x,t)=0, & x\in\Gamma_0,\;t\ge 0,\\[2pt]
\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial\nu}(x,t)=u(x,t), & x\in\Gamma_1,\;t\ge 0,\\[2pt]
y(x,t)=w_t(x,t), & x\in\Gamma_1,\;t\ge 0,
\end{cases}
\]
with state space $X=H^1_{\Gamma_0}(\Omega)\times L^2(\Omega)$ (where $H^1_{\Gamma_0}(\Omega)=\{f\in H^1(\Omega):f|_{\Gamma_0}=0\}$), input space $U=L^2(\Gamma_1)$ and output space $Y=L^2(\Gamma_1)$. It is known that this system is a well-posed and conservative linear system in the sense of Weiss; in particular, for every $\tau\ge 0$, the input–state–output map $\Sigma_\tau:X\times L^2([0,\tau];U)\to X\times L^2([0,\tau];Y)$ is unitary.

A well-posed linear system $\Sigma$ with transfer function $\mathbf{G}(s)$ is called regular if the strong limit
\[
D:=\lim_{\lambda\to+\infty,\;\lambda\in\mathbb{R}}\mathbf{G}(\lambda)v
\]
exists in $Y$ for every $v\in U$; the bounded operator $D:U\to Y$ is then called the feedthrough operator of $\Sigma$.

Question: Is the conservative wave system above a regular linear system in the sense of Weiss? Equivalently, does the strong limit $\lim_{\lambda\to+\infty}\mathbf{G}(\lambda)v$ exist in $L^2(\Gamma_1)$ for every $v\in L^2(\Gamma_1)$?

The regularity of the wave equation with boundary control and collocated observation has been established in several geometric/boundary-condition settings after the problem was posed in 2004: e.g., B.-Z. Guo and X. Zhang proved regularity for the wave equation with partial Dirichlet boundary control and observation (SIAM J. Control Optim., 2005), and analogous regularity results were obtained for related second-order systems (Euler–Bernoulli plate with Neumann control and collocated observation, linear elasticity with boundary control/observation). The fully general open problem—regularity of the conservative wave system with mixed Dirichlet/Neumann boundary conditions on arbitrary smooth bounded domains—appears to be resolved in important specific cases but not stated as completely settled in full generality.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, let $\omega \subset \Omega$ be a nonempty open subset, and let $T>0$. Consider the semi-linear wave equation with internal control
$$
\begin{cases}
y_{tt}-\Delta y + f(y) = h\,\mathbf{1}_{\omega} & \text{in } \Omega\times(0,T),\\
y=0 & \text{on } \partial\Omega\times(0,T),\\
y(\cdot,0)=y^0,\ y_t(\cdot,0)=y^1 & \text{in } \Omega,
\end{cases}\qquad (1)
$$
where $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $h\in L^2(\omega\times(0,T))$ is the control. The natural energy space is $H_0^1(\Omega)\times L^2(\Omega)$.

Assume:

(H1) (Subquadratic-logarithmic growth on the nonlinearity.) The function $f$ is locally Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$ and satisfies
$$
\limsup_{|s|\to\infty}\frac{|f(s)|}{|s|\,\log^2(1+|s|)} = 0.
$$

(H2) (Geometric Control Condition.) The pair $(\omega,T)$ satisfies the Geometric Control Condition: every generalized bicharacteristic ray of the wave operator $\partial_t^2-\Delta$ in $\Omega\times(0,T)$, reflected at the boundary according to the laws of geometric optics, meets the control region $\omega$ in time strictly less than $T$.

The system (1) is said to be exactly controllable in time $T$ with controls in $L^2(\omega\times(0,T))$ if for every $(y^0,y^1),(z^0,z^1)\in H_0^1(\Omega)\times L^2(\Omega)$ there exists $h\in L^2(\omega\times(0,T))$ such that the corresponding solution of (1) satisfies $y(\cdot,T)=z^0$ and $y_t(\cdot,T)=z^1$.

Question: Do (H1) and (H2) together imply the exact controllability of (1)?

Zuazua's 1993 result establishes exact controllability for the semi-linear wave equation in one space dimension under such a growth condition, and analogous results in higher dimensions are known under stronger assumptions (e.g., globally Lipschitz or asymptotically linear nonlinearity, or stronger growth conditions). The general question, whether the (almost-optimal) growth condition combined with the Geometric Control Condition implies global exact controllability in arbitrary space dimension, does not appear to have been resolved; recent works on 1D constructive approaches and on subcritical equations continue to treat partial cases, indicating the problem remains open.

Consider the following two control problems.

(A) Electromagnetic "masking" problem. Let Ω ⊂ R^3 be a bounded smooth obstacle with electromagnetic boundary impedance χ, and let D ⊂ Ω be a strictly interior subdomain with electromagnetic boundary impedance χ₀. Let (E_i, B_i) denote an incoming electromagnetic field (a solution of the free-space Maxwell equations in R^3 × R) impinging on the configuration. The total field outside Ω is written as (E_i + E_s, B_i + B_s), where (E_s, B_s) is the scattered field generated by Ω carrying impedance χ and by a controllable surface current ψ(x,t) supported on ∂Ω (or on a control surface inside Ω \ D).

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on (Ω, D, χ, χ₀) under which there exists a vector control function ψ such that, for the prescribed incoming field (E_i, B_i), the scattered field satisfies
   E_s(x,t) = 0 and B_s(x,t) = 0  for all x ∈ R^3 \ Ω and all t ∈ R,
i.e., an external observer cannot distinguish the controlled obstacle from free space ("masking"). When such ψ exists, characterize it constructively and study its uniqueness, stability with respect to (E_i, B_i), and the bandwidth of incoming fields for which masking is achievable.

(B) Drag optimization / locomotion problem. Let Ω_t ⊂ R^3, t ∈ R, be a time-dependent rigid obstacle moving in an incompressible Newtonian fluid of constant viscosity η > 0, filling the exterior R^3 \ Ω_t. The fluid velocity u and pressure p satisfy the Navier–Stokes equations
   ∂_t u + (u·∇)u − η Δu + ∇p = f,  div u = 0,  in R^3 \ Ω_t,
with no-slip boundary conditions on ∂Ω_t determined by the rigid motion of Ω_t, with prescribed initial data and external force f, and decaying at infinity. The shape Ω_t = R(t) Ω₀ + c(t) is determined by a "maneuver", i.e. a smooth curve t ↦ (R(t), c(t)) ∈ SO(3) × R^3 (or, more generally, by a controllable family of shape changes).

Given the rest initial state (linear velocity, angular velocity) = (0,0) of the body and a desired final state (w^+, ω^+) ∈ R^3 × R^3, find a maneuver t ↦ (R(t), c(t)) on a finite time interval [0,T] that drives the body from (0,0) to (w^+, ω^+) while minimizing the time-integrated hydrodynamic drag exerted by the fluid on the body. Establish existence, regularity, and characterization (e.g. via a Pontryagin-type maximum principle) of optimal maneuvers, and identify qualitative properties such as symmetry, scaling with viscosity η, and the dependence on the target state (w^+, ω^+).

Given the rest initial state (linear velocity, angular velocity) = (0,0) of the body and a desired final state (w^+, ω^+) ∈ R^3 × R^3, find a maneuver t ↦ (R(t), c(t)) on a finite time interval [0,T] that drives the body from (0,0) to (w^+, ω^+) while minimizing the time-integrated hydrodynamic drag exerted by the fluid on the body. Establish existence, regularity, and characterization (e.g. via a Pontryagin-type maximum principle) of optimal maneuvers, and identify qualitative properties such as symmetry, scaling with viscosity η, and the dependence on the target state (w^+, ω^+).

Notation. For a real symmetric matrix $P$, write $P\succ 0$ ($P\prec 0$) to mean $P$ is positive (negative) definite. For a real matrix $C\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, define the polyhedral cone
$$\mathcal{C}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : Cx\ge 0\},$$
where the inequality is taken componentwise. Given a square matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and the cone $\mathcal{C}$, we say that a symmetric matrix $P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is a copositive Lyapunov function for the pair $(A,\mathcal{C})$ if
$$x^{\top}Px>0\quad\text{for all }0\ne x\in\mathcal{C},\qquad x^{\top}(A^{\top}P+PA)x<0\quad\text{for all }0\ne x\in\mathcal{C}.$$

Problem 1. Given $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $C\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ defining $\mathcal{C}=\{x:Cx\ge 0\}$, determine necessary and sufficient conditions (verifiable in terms of $A$ and $C$) for the existence of a symmetric matrix $P$ such that
$$x^{\top}Px>0\text{ for all }0\ne x\in\mathcal{C},\qquad x^{\top}(A^{\top}P+PA)x<0\text{ for all }0\ne x\in\mathcal{C}.$$

Problem 2. Given two square matrices $A_1,A_2\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and two matrices $C_1,C_2$ defining the cones $\mathcal{C}_i=\{x:C_i x\ge 0\}$ ($i=1,2$), assume each $\mathcal{C}_i$ is invariant under the flow of $\dot x=A_i x$. Determine sufficient conditions for the existence of a single symmetric matrix $P$ that is simultaneously a copositive Lyapunov function for both $(A_1,\mathcal{C}_1)$ and $(A_2,\mathcal{C}_2)$, i.e.\
$$x^{\top}Px>0\ \forall\,0\ne x\in\mathcal{C}_i,\quad x^{\top}(A_i^{\top}P+PA_i)x<0\ \forall\,0\ne x\in\mathcal{C}_i,\ \ i=1,2.$$

Let $\mathcal{H} = \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}_+)$ with the standard basis $\{e_n\}_{n\ge 0}$, and let $\{P_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be the nest of orthogonal projections onto $\mathrm{span}\{e_0,\dots,e_{n-1}\}$ (with $P_0=0$). Define the nest algebra of causal bounded operators
$$\mathcal{T} = \{A\in B(\mathcal{H}) : (I-P_n)A P_n = 0 \text{ for all } n\ge 0\},$$
i.e.\ the algebra of lower-triangular bounded linear operators with respect to $\{e_n\}$. An element of $\mathcal{T}$ is called a (bounded, causal, linear) time-varying stable operator.

A linear time-varying plant is described by a (possibly unbounded) causal linear operator $P$ between dense subspaces of $\mathcal{H}$ admitting a right coprime factorization $P = NM^{-1}$ with $N,M\in\mathcal{T}$ and the existence of $X,Y\in\mathcal{T}$ such that $XM+YN = I$. A controller $C = UV^{-1}$ (with $U,V\in\mathcal{T}$ coprime over $\mathcal{T}$) stabilizes $P$ if the closed-loop transfer operator from external signals to internal signals lies in $\mathcal{T}$, equivalently if $MV+NU$ is invertible in $\mathcal{T}$. The plant $P$ is called stabilizable if some such $C$ exists, and strongly stabilizable if it can be stabilized by a $C$ which itself belongs to $\mathcal{T}$ (i.e.\ a stable controller).

Problem. Give a necessary and sufficient condition, intrinsic to the coprime factorization data $(N,M)$ of $P$ over the nest algebra $\mathcal{T}$, for $P$ to be strongly stabilizable. Equivalently, characterize those stabilizable linear time-varying systems on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}_+)$ that admit a stable causal linear time-varying stabilizing controller, in analogy with the parity interlacing property that characterizes strong stabilizability of finite-dimensional linear time-invariant plants.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The problem appears to remain open in full generality. Partial progress has been made: Feintuch showed that the nest algebra of causal stable time-varying operators has infinite stable rank, implying that there exist stabilizable linear time-varying systems that are not strongly stabilizable; sufficient conditions have been obtained for the slowly time-varying case and for asymptotically time-invariant systems. No complete intrinsic characterization analogous to the LTI parity interlacing property is known.

Let K denote either the real field R or the complex field C. For a matrix A ∈ K^{n×n}, let γ(A) := max{Re λ : λ is an eigenvalue of A} denote its spectral abscissa. Fix a real number β with γ(A) < β < 0. Given constants M ≥ 1 and β < 0, the matrix A is said to be (M, β)-stable if the matrix exponential satisfies

   ‖e^{tA}‖ ≤ M · e^{β t}    for all t ≥ 0,

where ‖·‖ denotes the spectral (operator 2-) norm. A pair (A, B) ∈ K^{n×n} × K^{n×m} is called (M, β)-stabilizable if there exists a feedback matrix F ∈ K^{m×n} such that A + B F is (M, β)-stable.

Address each of the following three problems.

(1) Given A ∈ K^{n×n} and β ∈ (γ(A), 0), determine in closed (analytic) form the quantity

   M_β(A) := inf{ M ≥ 1 : A is (M, β)-stable }.

(2) Given fixed constants M ≥ 1 and β < 0, give an analytic characterization of the set of all (M, β)-stabilizable pairs (A, B) ∈ K^{n×n} × K^{n×m}.

(3) Given matrices A ∈ K^{n×n}, D ∈ K^{n×ℓ} and E ∈ K^{q×n}, determine analytically the (M, β)-stability radius

   r_{M,β}(A; D, E) := inf{ ‖Δ‖ : Δ ∈ K^{ℓ×q} and A + D Δ E is not (M, β)-stable }.

The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2004 collection of unsolved problems in systems and control theory concerning transient behavior of linear systems. Subsequent literature (e.g., work by Hinrichsen, Plischke, and Wirth on transient bounds and M-matrices) has developed bounds and numerical methods but no fully analytic closed-form solutions to all three sub-problems are known. The problem appears to remain open.

Consider a finite family $\{f_1, \dots, f_m\}$ of smooth vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $f_i(0)=0$ for each $i$, and assume that each individual system $\dot x = f_i(x)$ is globally asymptotically stable. For a piecewise constant switching signal $\sigma:[0,\infty)\to\{1,\dots,m\}$, consider the switched nonlinear system
$$\dot x(t) = f_{\sigma(t)}(x(t)).$$
The switched system is said to be globally uniformly asymptotically stable (GUAS) if it is globally asymptotically stable at the origin uniformly over all switching signals $\sigma$.

Let $\mathcal{L} = \{f_1,\dots,f_m\}_{LA}$ denote the Lie algebra of vector fields generated by $f_1,\dots,f_m$ under the Lie bracket $[f,g](x) = \frac{\partial g}{\partial x}f(x) - \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}g(x)$.

In the linear case $f_i(x) = A_i x$, it is known that if the matrix Lie algebra generated by $\{A_1,\dots,A_m\}$ is solvable (or, more generally, decomposes as the sum of a solvable ideal and a subalgebra of compact type), then the switched linear system admits a common quadratic Lyapunov function and is GUES under arbitrary switching.

Problem: Find verifiable conditions on the Lie algebra $\mathcal{L}$ generated by the nonlinear vector fields $f_1,\dots,f_m$ (e.g., nilpotency, solvability, or finite-dimensionality together with appropriate structural properties) that guarantee global uniform asymptotic stability of the switched nonlinear system $\dot x = f_{\sigma(t)}(x)$ under arbitrary switching. In particular, determine whether solvability of $\mathcal{L}$ (in the sense of nonlinear vector fields) implies GUAS, and identify the broadest Lie-algebraic structural condition on $\mathcal{L}$ that ensures stability under arbitrary switching for any choice of GAS vector fields $f_1,\dots,f_m$ generating a Lie algebra with that structure.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The problem remains open in general. Partial results exist: Margaliot and Liberzon (2006) proved that switched nonlinear systems generated by a pair of GAS vector fields whose iterated Lie brackets of order three vanish are GUAS, generalizing the commuting and nilpotent linear cases. The full nonlinear analogue of the linear solvable / "solvable + compact" theorem (Agrachev–Liberzon, Liberzon–Hespanha–Morse) has not been established.

Consider a commensurate fractional-order linear time-invariant system described by the pseudo-state-space equation
    D^α x(t) = A x(t),    x(t) ∈ ℝ^n,
where D^α denotes the Caputo (or Riemann–Liouville) fractional derivative of commensurate order α ∈ (0, 2), and A is a real n×n matrix whose entries are uncertain and lie in prescribed intervals:
    A ∈ A_I := { A ∈ ℝ^{n×n} : a_{ij}^- ≤ a_{ij} ≤ a_{ij}^+, 1 ≤ i,j ≤ n }.
Recall that the nominal system with a fixed matrix A is stable in the sense of Matignon if and only if every eigenvalue λ of A satisfies |arg(λ)| > απ/2. The interval system is said to be robustly stable if this spectral condition holds for every A ∈ A_I.

Problem. Provide a computationally tractable, necessary and sufficient robust stability test for the interval fractional-order system above: that is, give a finite, checkable criterion (for example via a finite collection of vertex/edge polynomials or matrices, or via linear matrix inequalities) on the data (a_{ij}^-, a_{ij}^+, α) that holds if and only if every eigenvalue of every A ∈ A_I lies in the open sector { z ∈ ℂ : |arg(z)| > απ/2 }, covering both the regime 0 < α < 1 and the regime 1 ≤ α < 2.

Substantial progress has been made since the problem was posed. For commensurate fractional order 1 ≤ α < 2, necessary and sufficient robust stability conditions for interval fractional-order LTI systems have been developed (e.g., Lyapunov-inequality / LMI based "conservatism-free" tests). Consider a single-input single-output time-delay system of the form

    dx/dt = A x(t) + A_d x(t - τ) + b φ(σ(t)),    σ(t) = c^T x(t),

where x(t) ∈ ℝ^n, τ ≥ 0 is a constant delay, A, A_d ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, b, c ∈ ℝ^n, and φ : ℝ → ℝ is a continuous scalar nonlinearity satisfying the sector condition

    k_1 σ^2 ≤ σ φ(σ) ≤ k_2 σ^2    for all σ ∈ ℝ,        (*)

with 0 ≤ k_1 < k_2. Replace φ(σ) by the linear gain k σ to obtain the linearized family

    dx/dt = A x(t) + A_d x(t - τ) + b k c^T x(t),    k ∈ [k_1, k_2].

Suppose that exponential stability of the zero solution of the linearized family has been established by either a delay-independent criterion (valid for all τ ≥ 0) or a delay-dependent criterion (valid for τ in a given interval), uniformly in k ∈ [k_1, k_2].

Question. Does such exponential stability of the linearized family imply (global, asymptotic, or exponential) stability of the zero solution of the original nonlinear time-delay system for every nonlinearity φ satisfying the sector condition (*)? Equivalently, formulate and resolve the Aizerman-type problem in both the delay-independent and the delay-dependent settings: identify classes of (A, A_d, b, c, τ, k_1, k_2) for which the implication holds, and exhibit counterexamples where it fails.

The delay-independent and delay-dependent Aizerman problem for time-delay systems with sector nonlinearity is listed as an open problem in the 2004 collection of unsolved problems in systems and control. Subsequent work has produced sufficient absolute-stability criteria (LMI- and frequency-domain-based, delay-dependent and delay-independent), but no general resolution of the Aizerman-type implication for time-delay systems has been established; the classical (delay-free) Aizerman conjecture itself is known to be false in general, while partial positive results exist for restricted system classes.

Consider the discrete-time scalar control system

   y(t+1) = a · φ(y(t)) + u(t) + w(t+1),   t = 0, 1, 2, …,

where y(t) ∈ ℝ is the measured output, u(t) ∈ ℝ is the control input, w(t) ∈ ℝ is an unknown deterministic disturbance satisfying |w(t)| ≤ Δ for some known constant Δ > 0, and a ∈ ℝ is an unknown scalar parameter belonging to a known compact interval A = [a_min, a_max].  The function φ : ℝ → ℝ is known, continuous, and Lipschitz (so that for some L > 0 one has |φ(x) − φ(x′)| ≤ L|x − x′| for all x, x′ ∈ ℝ), with φ(0) = 0.

An admissible adaptive feedback controller is a sequence of causal maps producing
   u(t) = U_t( y(0), y(1), …, y(t) ),
together with an arbitrary on-line parameter-estimation rule â(t) = E_t( y(0), …, y(t) ).

The closed-loop system is called globally stable if, for every initial condition y(0) ∈ ℝ, every parameter a ∈ A, and every disturbance sequence with |w(t)| ≤ Δ, the resulting output sequence {y(t)} and control sequence {u(t)} are uniformly bounded.

Problem.  Determine whether there exists an admissible adaptive feedback controller (with an associated estimator â(t) of the unknown parameter a) that guarantees global stability of the closed-loop system in the above sense for every nonlinearity φ in the class described, every Δ > 0, and every compact parameter interval A.  Equivalently: give either an explicit construction of such an adaptive controller together with a proof of global boundedness of {y(t), u(t)}, or prove that no such adaptive feedback controller exists by exhibiting a Lipschitz φ, a parameter interval A, and a disturbance bound Δ for which every causal adaptive feedback law produces unbounded trajectories for some admissible (a, {w(t)}, y(0)).

Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$ and let $\Omega_\nu \subset \mathbb{C}$ be an open region of the complex plane whose boundary is described by a real bivariate polynomial $f$ of total degree $\nu \ge 1$ in $(\lambda,\lambda^*)$ (equivalently, in $(x,y)$ with $\lambda = x+iy$), so that
$$
\Omega_\nu = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : f(\lambda,\lambda^*) < 0\}, \qquad \partial\Omega_\nu = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : f(\lambda,\lambda^*) = 0\}.
$$
Write $f(\lambda,\lambda^*) = \sum_{k,\ell \ge 0,\; k+\ell \le \nu} c_{k\ell}\,\lambda^{k}(\lambda^*)^{\ell}$ with $c_{k\ell} = c_{\ell k}^*$ so that $f$ is real-valued. The region $\Omega_\nu$ is called $\Omega$-transformable if there exists a rational (Möbius-type) transformation $\varphi:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ mapping $\Omega_\nu$ onto the open left half-plane $\{\mathrm{Re}\,z < 0\}$.

For a matrix $A$, denote by $\sigma(A)$ its spectrum. Say that $A$ is $\Omega_\nu$-stable if $\sigma(A) \subset \Omega_\nu$.

Generalized Lyapunov problem. Find a generalized Lyapunov-type matrix inequality/equation
$$
\mathcal{L}_f(A,P) \;\prec\; 0 \qquad (P = P^* \succ 0)
$$
where $\mathcal{L}_f(A,P)$ is a Hermitian matrix expression constructed explicitly from the coefficients $\{c_{k\ell}\}$ of $f$ and from positive (or negative) powers of $A$ and $A^*$, such that the following equivalence holds for every $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ and every $\Omega$-transformable region $\Omega_\nu$ of arbitrary boundary degree $\nu$:
$$
\sigma(A) \subset \Omega_\nu \;\iff\; \exists\, P = P^* \succ 0 \text{ such that } \mathcal{L}_f(A,P) \prec 0.
$$
Equivalently, give a constructive procedure that, from the polynomial $f$ defining an arbitrary $\Omega$-transformable region, produces such a necessary-and-sufficient Lyapunov-type characterization of $\Omega_\nu$-stability of $A$, unifying and generalizing the classical Lyapunov ($\nu=1$, left half-plane) and Stein ($\nu=2$, unit disk) theorems to all $\nu \ge 1$.

representations.normalized:
Consider a finite-dimensional nonlinear control system with disturbances and a measured output of the form
  \[\dot x = f(x,u,w), \qquad y = h(x,u,w),\]
where $x(t)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ is the state, $u(t)\in\mathbb{R}^p$ is the control input, $w(t)\in\mathbb{R}^q$ is an exogenous disturbance, and $y(t)\in\mathbb{R}^r$ is the measured output. Assume $f$ and $h$ are locally Lipschitz, and inputs $u,w$ are taken in the class of locally essentially bounded measurable functions.

For any two solutions $x_1(\cdot),x_2(\cdot)$ of the system corresponding to input pairs $(u_1,w_1)$ and $(u_2,w_2)$ respectively, with outputs $y_i=h(x_i,u_i,w_i)$, define the system to have the \emph{Incremental Input/Measurement-to-Error Stability (IMES)} property if there exist functions $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$ and $\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for all $t\ge 0$,
  \[|x_1(t)-x_2(t)|\le \beta\bigl(|x_1(0)-x_2(0)|,\,t\bigr) + \gamma_1\!\left(\|u_1-u_2\|_{[0,t]}\right) + \gamma_2\!\left(\|y_1-y_2\|_{[0,t]}\right),\]
whenever both trajectories are defined on $[0,t]$ (where $\|\cdot\|_{[0,t]}$ denotes the essential supremum on $[0,t]$).

\textbf{Problem.} Find a Lyapunov-function characterization of the IMES property; that is, exhibit a class of (preferably smooth) scalar functions $V:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ together with infinitesimal dissipation inequalities involving $f$ and $h$ such that the system enjoys the IMES property if and only if such a $V$ exists. In particular, determine whether a \emph{smooth} (i.e., $C^\infty$) Lyapunov characterization of IMES is possible.

representations.normalized:
Consider a one-dimensional tank of length $L>0$ containing an incompressible inviscid fluid, modeled by the Saint-Venant (shallow water) equations in a non-inertial frame attached to the tank. Let $H(t,x)$ denote the height of the fluid and $v(t,x)$ its horizontal velocity, satisfying
$$H_t + (Hv)_x = 0, \qquad v_t + \left(gH + \tfrac{1}{2}v^2\right)_x = -u(t), \qquad x\in[0,L],\ t\ge 0,$$
with boundary conditions $v(t,0)=v(t,L)=0$, where $g>0$ is the gravitational constant and the scalar control $u(t)$ is the horizontal acceleration of the tank. Let $D(t) = \int_0^t\int_0^s u(\sigma)\,d\sigma\,ds$ and $V(t)=\int_0^t u(s)\,ds$ denote the position and velocity of the tank. The full state of the system is $(H,v,D,V)$, and the equilibria are $(H,v,D,V)=(H_0,0,D_0,0)$ for constants $H_0>0$, $D_0\in\mathbb{R}$.

It is known that this nonlinear control system is locally controllable around any such equilibrium provided the control time $T$ is sufficiently large. Determine the infimum of all times $T>0$ for which local controllability around an equilibrium $(H_0,0,D_0,0)$ holds: that is, find the minimal $T$ such that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ with the property that, for any two states $(H^i,v^i,D^i,0)$ ($i=0,1$) within $\delta$ of the equilibrium (in a suitable Sobolev norm), there exists an admissible control $u$ steering the system from $(H^0,v^0,D^0,0)$ at time $0$ to $(H^1,v^1,D^1,0)$ at time $T$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Coron (2002) established local controllability for sufficiently large time. Subsequent work, including Bournissou–Koenig–Trélat (2022) on lack of local controllability when the time is not large enough, shows that the minimal time is at least $2L/\sqrt{gH_0}$, and that for times between $L/\sqrt{gH_0}$ and $2L/\sqrt{gH_0}$ one cannot return an equilibrium to itself. The exact minimal time for local controllability of the nonlinear water-tank system remains not fully characterized.

[{"title": "Lack of local controllability for a water-tank system when the time is not large enough", "url": "https://hal.science/hal-03588552/", "snippet": "Shows that for T less than 2T* local controllability around equilibrium fails for the nonlinear water-tank system.", "claim": "Necessary time is at least 2T*; problem of exact minimal time still being investigated."}, {"title": "Local controllability of a 1-D tank containing a fluid modeled by the shallow water equations (Coron)", "url": "https://www.esaim-cocv.org/articles/cocv/pdf/2002/02/coron.pdf", "snippet": "Proves local controllability around equilibria for sufficiently large time.", "claim": "Positive controllability result for large time, leaving the minimal time open."}, {"title": "Stabilization of the Linearized Water Tank System (Coron–Hayat)", "url": "https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00205-022-01778-0", "snippet": "Recent work on the linearized water tank with quantitative time estimates.", "claim": "Active research on time-optimal controllability of the water-tank model."}]

representations.normalized:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be Hilbert spaces, and let $A: \mathcal{D}(A) \subset X \to X$ be the generator of a strongly continuous semigroup $(T_t)_{t \geq 0}$ on $X$. Let $C: \mathcal{D}(A) \to Y$ be an admissible observation operator for $(T_t)$, meaning that there exists $\tau > 0$ and $K_\tau > 0$ such that
$$\int_0^\tau \|C T_t x\|_Y^2\, dt \leq K_\tau \|x\|_X^2 \qquad \text{for all } x \in \mathcal{D}(A).$$
The pair $(A, C)$ is said to be exactly observable (in some time $\tau > 0$) if there exists $k_\tau > 0$ such that
$$\int_0^\tau \|C T_t x\|_Y^2\, dt \geq k_\tau \|x\|_X^2 \qquad \text{for all } x \in \mathcal{D}(A).$$
Consider the following infinite-dimensional Hautus-type condition (condition (E)): there exist constants $m, M > 0$ such that
$$\|(sI - A)x\|_X^2 + |\operatorname{Re}(s)|\, \|Cx\|_Y^2 \geq m\, |\operatorname{Re}(s)|^2\, \|x\|_X^2$$
for all $x \in \mathcal{D}(A)$ and all $s \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s) < 0$ (equivalently, an analogous resolvent inequality on the left half-plane).

Prove or disprove: condition (E) is equivalent to exact observability of $(A, C)$ for every $C_0$-semigroup generator $A$ on a Hilbert space and every admissible observation operator $C$. Equivalently, formulate and establish a Hautus-type frequency-domain test that characterizes exact observability for general infinite-dimensional linear systems.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The Russell–Weiss conjecture (an infinite-dimensional Hautus test characterizing exact observability) has been verified in several special cases — notably for bounded generators, exponentially stable $C_0$-groups, and diagonal systems with one-dimensional output operators — but a full equivalence between the Hautus-type resolvent condition and exact observability for general $C_0$-semigroups on Hilbert spaces remains open.

[{"title": "On the Hautus Test for Exponentially Stable C0-Groups", "url": "https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/080724733", "snippet": "Russell and Weiss showed that a Hautus-type condition is necessary for exact observability and, under the additional assumption that A is bounded, also sufficient; the general case remains open.", "claim": "The full generalization of the Hautus test to exact observability of infinite-dimensional linear systems is still open; only partial results are available."}, {"title": "Exact observability of diagonal systems with a one-dimensional output operator", "url": "https://research.utwente.nl/en/publications/exact-observability-of-diagonal-systems-with-a-one-dimensional-ou/", "snippet": "Equivalent conditions for exact observability of diagonal systems with a one-dimensional output operator are given; one of these conditions is the conjecture of Russell and Weiss (1994).", "claim": "The Russell–Weiss Hautus conjecture has been verified in the special case of diagonal systems with one-dimensional output."}, {"title": "On exact observability for compactly perturbed infinite dimensional systems", "url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2512.25041", "snippet": "Resolvent (Hautus-type) conditions for admissibility and observability of infinite-dimensional linear evolution equations continue to be investigated.", "claim": "Research on infinite-dimensional Hautus tests remains active, indicating the general problem is not fully resolved."}]

Consider a smooth control system
  Σ_u :  ẋ = f(x,u),   y = h(x),
where x evolves in some manifold X (or open subset of R^N), u is a measurable input taking values in a set U ⊂ R^m, and the output map h takes values in R. Fix a regularity class C^r with r ∈ {∞, ω} (where C^ω denotes real-analytic).

A C^r-observer for Σ_u is, informally, a C^r dynamical system driven by (u, y) whose state asymptotically reproduces x. The system Σ_u is said to be observable for an input u if any two distinct initial states produce distinct output trajectories under u.

(a) Suppose Σ_u admits a C^r-observer. Must there exist an integer n ≥ 1 and a C^r function φ : R^n × U^{(n-1)} → R such that, along every trajectory of Σ_u,
   y^{(n)} = φ(y, y', y'', …, y^{(n-1)}, u, u', …, u^{(n-1)}) ?
(Equivalently, must the nth derivative of the output be a C^r function of the output, its n−1 previous derivatives, and the input together with its derivatives?)

(b) Let S^∞ (resp. S^ω) denote the space of C^∞ (resp. C^ω) systems Σ_u, equipped with a natural topology (e.g. Whitney C^∞ topology, resp. the appropriate topology on real-analytic systems). Does the subset of those Σ ∈ S^∞ (resp. Σ ∈ S^ω) which are observable for every C^∞ input contain an open subset — or, better, an open and dense subset — of S^∞ (resp. S^ω)?

(c) In both the C^∞ and C^ω cases, does observability of Σ for every C^∞ input imply observability of Σ for every input in a broader class (for example every measurable, or every L^∞, or every continuous input)?

Determine the answers to (a), (b), and (c).

status_assertions.value: open_status:unknown

The questions sit in the Gauthier–Kupka framework of observability and observers for nonlinear systems. While their theory (canonical forms, high-gain observers, genericity in the single-output uniformly observable case) is well developed and partial genericity/canonical-form results exist, no source found explicitly settles these three combined questions (existence of φ from existence of a C^r-observer; openness/density of systems observable for every C^∞ input; and implication between C^∞-input observability and observability for broader input classes) in the multi-input setting posed. Current status could not be conclusively verified.

Consider the Korteweg–de Vries equation on the bounded interval (0, L) with boundary control acting through the right Neumann condition:
    y_t + y_x + y_{xxx} + y y_x = 0,  (t, x) ∈ (0, T) × (0, L),
    y(t, 0) = 0,  y(t, L) = 0,  y_x(t, L) = u(t),  t ∈ (0, T),
    y(0, x) = y_0(x),  x ∈ (0, L),
where y_0 ∈ L^2(0, L) is a given initial datum and u ∈ L^2(0, T) is the scalar control input. For T > 0, define the reachable set from y_0 at time T by
    R(y_0, T) = { y(T, ·) : u ∈ L^2(0, T) },
i.e., the set of all states attainable at time T starting from y_0 with some admissible boundary control.

Question: Is it true that, for every y_0 ∈ L^2(0, L), one has 0 ∈ R(y_0, T) whenever T is large enough? In other words, is the system globally null-controllable in sufficiently large time by means of the single right Neumann boundary control u(t) = y_x(t, L)?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Substantial progress has been made. Rosier established local exact controllability around 0 for non-critical lengths; Cerpa, Crépeau, Coron, Chapouly, and Laurent–Rosier–Zhang later proved local-to-global and large-time results, including global exponential stabilization to 0 and large-time local exact controllability for critical lengths. However, the question of global null-controllability in large time using only the single right Neumann boundary control u(t) = y_x(t,L) for arbitrary L^2 initial data does not appear to have been fully settled in the literature; recent surveys and works (e.g., Cerpa 2014; Laurent–Rosier–Zhang) treat it as partially resolved.

[{"title": "Control and stabilization of the Korteweg-de Vries equation: recent progresses", "url": "https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11424-009-9194-2", "snippet": "Survey describing controllability and stabilization results for KdV on bounded intervals, including Rosier's results, critical lengths, and subsequent large-time controllability work.", "claim": "Significant partial progress has been made on the large-time controllability of KdV with boundary control."}, {"title": "Control of a Korteweg–de Vries equation: a tutorial (Cerpa)", "url": "https://www.mat.uc.cl/~eduardo.cerpa/archivos/cerpa-mcrf-14.pdf", "snippet": "Tutorial discussing local and global controllability and stabilization results for the boundary-controlled KdV equation, including large-time exact controllability for critical lengths.", "claim": "Large-time controllability results are known in many configurations, but the global question with a single right Neumann control remains delicate."}, {"title": "Another look at the control properties of the Korteweg–de Vries equation", "url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2409.15571", "snippet": "Recent work revisiting control properties of KdV, showing continuing research activity on reachable sets and large-time controllability.", "claim": "The problem of characterizing reachable sets for KdV with boundary control remains an active research area."}]

Let $H^\infty$ denote the Hardy space of functions that are analytic and bounded in the open right half plane $\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re}(s)>0\}$, equipped with the norm
$$\|F\|_\infty \;=\; \sup_{\operatorname{Re}(s)>0} |F(s)| \;=\; \operatorname{ess\,sup}_{\omega\in\mathbb{R}} |F(i\omega)|.$$
A scalar stable rational transfer function is a rational function $G(s)=p(s)/q(s)$ whose poles all lie in the open left half plane; its McMillan degree is the degree of $q$ when $p/q$ is in lowest terms. Let $\mathcal{R}_n$ denote the set of stable real-rational transfer functions of McMillan degree at most $n$.

Given $G\in H^\infty$ (for instance, a stable rational transfer function of McMillan degree $N>n$, or a stable irrational transfer function) and a positive integer $n$, consider the optimal $H^\infty$ approximation problem
$$\gamma_n(G) \;=\; \inf_{\widehat{G}\in\mathcal{R}_n}\,\|G-\widehat{G}\|_\infty.$$

Solve the following:

(a) Establish existence and uniqueness (or non-uniqueness) of a minimizer $\widehat{G}^\star\in\mathcal{R}_n$ achieving the infimum $\gamma_n(G)$.

(b) Provide a constructive characterization of all such optimal approximants $\widehat{G}^\star$ — for example through an analogue of the Adamyan–Arov–Krein / Hankel-norm theory but for the $H^\infty$ norm rather than the Hankel (semi)norm — together with a tractable (ideally polynomial-time) algorithm that computes $\widehat{G}^\star$ to prescribed accuracy.

(c) Derive sharp two-sided bounds for $\gamma_n(G)$ in terms of intrinsic invariants of $G$ (e.g. the Hankel singular values $\sigma_1(G)\ge\sigma_2(G)\ge\cdots$ of the associated Hankel operator), in particular sharpening the classical inequalities $\sigma_{n+1}(G)\le\gamma_n(G)\le 2(\sigma_{n+1}(G)+\sigma_{n+2}(G)+\cdots)$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem appears as Problem 8.1 (Antoulas–Astolfi) in the 2004 Princeton volume of unsolved problems in systems and control. Optimal $H^\infty$ rational approximation of fixed McMillan degree is widely cited as still open: no convex characterization is known (the degree constraint is a nonconvex rank constraint), and only suboptimal or quasi-convex methods (Hankel-norm/AAK approximation, balanced truncation, interpolatory $H^\infty$ model reduction, AAA, bisection methods) are available. Recent works (e.g., interpolatory $H^\infty$ model reduction, 2011; AAA, 2016) provide partial/heuristic progress but do not give a complete characterization or polynomial-time algorithm.

Consider the standard H∞ control problem. Let P be a finite-dimensional, linear, time-invariant generalized plant given in state-space form by
  ẋ = A x + B₁ w + B₂ u,
  z = C₁ x + D₁₁ w + D₁₂ u,
  y = C₂ x + D₂₁ w + D₂₂ u,
with x ∈ ℝⁿ the state, w ∈ ℝᵐ¹ the exogenous disturbance, u ∈ ℝᵐ² the control input, z ∈ ℝᵖ¹ the performance output, and y ∈ ℝᵖ² the measured output. For any internally stabilizing, proper, real-rational controller K mapping y to u, let T_{zw}(P,K) denote the closed-loop transfer matrix from w to z, and let ‖T_{zw}(P,K)‖_∞ denote its H∞ norm (the essential supremum over ω ∈ ℝ of the largest singular value of T_{zw}(P,K)(jω)). Define the optimal H∞ performance
  γ_opt(P) := inf { ‖T_{zw}(P,K)‖_∞ : K internally stabilizes P }.

Consider the standard H∞ control problem. Let P be a finite-dimensional, linear, time-invariant generalized plant given in state-space form by
  ẋ = A x + B₁ w + B₂ u,
  z = C₁ x + D₁₁ w + D₁₂ u,

  γ_opt(P) := inf { ‖T_{zw}(P,K)‖_∞ : K internally stabilizes P }.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The general problem of non-iterative computation of the H∞ optimum remains open, but partial results exist. A non-iterative procedure has been proposed for computing the infimum in the singular H∞ optimization problem by solving two Riccati and two Lyapunov equations, and closed-form H∞ optimal controllers without iteration are known for special cases such as the one-block Nehari problem and certain infinite-dimensional systems with bounded input/output operators. In the general (regular, multivariable) H∞ setting, γ-iteration is still the standard approach.

representations.normalized:
Consider a single-input single-output linear time-invariant (LTI) feedback configuration in which a real-rational, strictly proper plant P_0(s) (possibly unstable) is connected in a standard unity-feedback loop with a real-rational LTI controller C(s), and an input/output delay e^{-sT} (T ≥ 0) is inserted in the loop. Say that the closed-loop system is internally stable if all four transfer functions from the two exogenous inputs to the plant input and output are stable. For a fixed pair (P_0, C) such that the loop is internally stable at T = 0, define the delay margin

   DM(P_0, C) := sup{ T ≥ 0 : the closed-loop system with delay τ is internally stable for every τ ∈ [0, T) }.

Define the achievable delay margin of the plant by

   DM_sup(P_0) := sup{ DM(P_0, C) : C is a real-rational LTI controller that internally stabilizes P_0 at delay 0 }.

Address the following.

(1) Does there exist an unstable real-rational strictly proper LTI plant P_0 for which DM_sup(P_0) is finite?

(2) If so, give an algorithm that, on input P_0(s) and a tolerance ε > 0, computes a number that approximates DM_sup(P_0) to within ε.

(3) If so, give an algorithm that, on input P_0(s) and a value T with 0 < T < DM_sup(P_0), constructs a real-rational LTI controller C(s) such that DM(P_0, C) ≥ T.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Subsequent work has resolved Problem 1 affirmatively: a strictly proper real-rational plant has a finite uniform upper bound on the achievable delay margin under LTI control if and only if it has at least one closed right half-plane pole not at the origin. Explicit (sometimes tight) upper bounds and frequency-domain/bilinear-transform numerical procedures for estimating DM_sup have been developed (e.g., Middleton–Miller 2007 and follow-up work for unstable complex poles, 2018). However, an exact computationally feasible algorithm to compute DM_sup to arbitrary accuracy for general unstable plants and a corresponding controller synthesis procedure for any T < DM_sup remain not fully resolved.

Consider a single-input single-output discrete-time linear time-invariant plant with a stabilizing digital controller realized in state-space form

  x_c(k+1) = A_c x_c(k) + B_c y(k),    u(k) = C_c x_c(k) + D_c y(k),

where W = (A_c, B_c, C_c, D_c) ∈ R^{(n+1)×(n+m+l)} denotes the collection of controller coefficients and the resulting closed-loop system matrix A_cl(W) ∈ R^{N×N} is Schur stable (all eigenvalues strictly inside the open unit disk).

When the controller is implemented in floating-point arithmetic with B mantissa bits and E exponent bits, each nominal coefficient w_{ij} of W is replaced by a perturbed value

  w_{ij}(1 + δ_{ij}),    |δ_{ij}| ≤ 2^{-(B+1)},

provided no exponent overflow/underflow occurs (so the relative error model holds elementwise and independently). Let Δ denote the matrix of relative perturbations (δ_{ij}). Define the floating-point closed-loop stability robustness measure

  μ_FLP(W) := sup { ε > 0 : A_cl(W ⊙ (1 + Δ)) is Schur stable for every Δ with ||Δ||_∞ ≤ ε },

where W ⊙ (1 + Δ) denotes the elementwise multiplicative perturbation. Two controller realizations W_1 and W_2 are called equivalent if they produce the same input–output map; the set of all realizations equivalent to a given stabilizing controller is parameterized by nonsingular similarity transformations T ∈ R^{n×n} acting as

  (A_c, B_c, C_c, D_c) ↦ (T^{-1} A_c T, T^{-1} B_c, C_c T, D_c).

Open problem. Develop a tractable characterization and an explicit algorithm for computing, among all realizations equivalent to a given infinite-precision stabilizing controller, one that maximizes the floating-point stability robustness measure μ_FLP, i.e. solve

  sup_{T ∈ GL_n(R)} μ_FLP( (T^{-1} A_c T, T^{-1} B_c, C_c T, D_c) ),

and determine whether the supremum is attained, how it depends on the mantissa length B, and how it compares with the corresponding fixed-point robustness measure obtained by replacing multiplicative perturbations δ_{ij} w_{ij} with additive perturbations of uniform magnitude.

The problem is posed as an open problem in the 2004 collection of unsolved problems in systems and control theory. Subsequent work by the same authors and collaborators (e.g. on optimal floating-point realizations and stability-radius approximations) proposes approximate measures and numerical optimization heuristics, but no closed-form solution or tractable exact characterization of the optimal similarity transformation has been established. Let A ∈ R^{n×n} be a Hurwitz-stable real matrix (every eigenvalue has strictly negative real part), and let v, w ∈ R^n. Because A is stable, there exist unique positive semidefinite matrices P, Q ∈ R^{n×n} satisfying the Lyapunov equations

    A P + P A^T + v v^T = 0,
    A Q + Q A^T + w w^T = 0.

For a vector x ∈ R^n define the (extended) controllability subspace generated by A and x as

    K(A, x) = span{ x, A x, A^2 x, A^3 x, … } ⊆ R^n,

and let k_v = dim K(A, v), k_w = dim K(A, w). For two subspaces U, V of R^n of dimensions p and q respectively, the principal angles 0 ≤ θ_1 ≤ θ_2 ≤ … ≤ θ_min(p,q) ≤ π/2 between U and V are defined recursively by

    cos θ_i = max{ ⟨u, v⟩ : u ∈ U, v ∈ V, ‖u‖ = ‖v‖ = 1, u ⊥ u_1,…,u_{i−1}, v ⊥ v_1,…,v_{i−1} },

with maximizers u_i, v_i.

Conjecture. The nonzero eigenvalues of the product P Q (which are all real and nonnegative) coincide, counted with multiplicity, with the numbers cos^2 θ_i, where θ_1, …, θ_{min(k_v, k_w)} are the principal angles between the subspaces K(A, v) and K(A, w). Equivalently, the characteristic polynomial of PQ restricted to its range factors as ∏_i (λ − cos^2 θ_i).

Prove this conjecture or provide a counterexample.

Consider the third–order nonlinear adaptive system

    ẍ(t) + θ(t)² x(t) = 2 ζ θ(t) e(t),
    θ̇(t) = − γ θ(t) x(t) e(t),
    e(t) = u(t) − ẋ(t),

with constants ζ > 0 and γ > 0, with state (x(t), ẋ(t), θ(t)) ∈ ℝ × ℝ × ℝ_{>0}, and with input signal

    u(t) = A sin(ω₀ t + φ),    A > 0, ω₀ > 0, φ ∈ ℝ.

Equivalently, set x₁ = x, x₂ = ẋ, x₃ = θ, and write

    ẋ₁ = x₂,
    ẋ₂ = − x₃² x₁ + 2 ζ x₃ (u − x₂),
    ẋ₃ = − γ x₃ x₁ (u − x₂).

The system is designed so that, for a purely sinusoidal input u(t) = A sin(ω₀ t + φ), there exists a one–parameter family of periodic orbits on which θ(t) ≡ ω₀ and x(t) reproduces u(t).

Question. Prove or disprove the following global stability statement: for every choice of constants ζ > 0, γ > 0, every A > 0, every ω₀ > 0, every φ ∈ ℝ, and every initial condition (x₁(0), x₂(0), x₃(0)) with x₃(0) > 0, the solution of the system above is defined for all t ≥ 0, all signals remain bounded, and the frequency estimate satisfies

    lim_{t → ∞} x₃(t) = ω₀.

In particular, characterize the basin of attraction of the family of synchronized periodic orbits and determine whether convergence of the frequency estimate to the true frequency ω₀ is global (independent of initial conditions and of the design parameters ζ, γ).

The Karimi-Ghartemani–Ziarani adaptive notch filter has been analyzed using averaging and Lyapunov methods, with local/semi-global stability results and the existence of a one-dimensional adaptive integral manifold established. Current status of a fully global stability proof could not be definitively verified from the available search results.

Let n and m be positive integers, and let A_0, A_1, ..., A_m ∈ C^{n×n}. Consider the matrix-valued multivariate polynomial

   P(z_1, ..., z_m) = A_0 + z_1 A_1 + z_2 A_2 + ... + z_m A_m,

and the following property:

(1) det P(z_1, ..., z_m) ≠ 0 for all (z_1, ..., z_m) in the closed unit polydisc {(z_1,...,z_m) ∈ C^m : |z_i| ≤ 1, i = 1,...,m}.

For each positive integer k, let LMI(k) denote the following hierarchy of linear matrix inequality relaxations: there exist Hermitian positive definite matrices P_1, ..., P_m of size kn × kn (with appropriate block structure depending on k) such that a prescribed Lyapunov-type LMI built from the coefficient matrices A_0, ..., A_m and from P_1, ..., P_m is feasible. (Here the LMIs are constructed by successive lifting/relaxation of order k, in such a way that feasibility of LMI(k) is a sufficient condition for property (1), and feasibility of LMI(k) implies feasibility of LMI(k+1).)

Open Problem 1. Construct an integer-valued function

   k*: (C^{n×n})^{m+1} → Z_{≥ 1},   (A_0, A_1, ..., A_m) ↦ k*(A_0, A_1, ..., A_m),

which can be evaluated in time polynomial in n and m, with the following property: for every (A_0, ..., A_m) ∈ (C^{n×n})^{m+1}, property (1) holds if and only if LMI(k) is feasible for k = k*(A_0, A_1, ..., A_m).

A finite set of square matrices $\Sigma=\{A_1,\dots,A_m\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is said to be:
- (stable) if every infinite product $A_{i_k}A_{i_{k-1}}\cdots A_{i_1}$ with indices $i_j\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ converges to the zero matrix as $k\to\infty$; equivalently, the joint spectral radius $\rho(\Sigma):=\lim_{k\to\infty}\max_{i_1,\dots,i_k}\|A_{i_k}\cdots A_{i_1}\|^{1/k}$ satisfies $\rho(\Sigma)<1$;
- (periodically stable) if every finite product of the form $A_{i_k}A_{i_{k-1}}\cdots A_{i_1}$ (corresponding to periodic switching sequences) has spectral radius strictly less than $1$; equivalently, the generalized spectral radius $\bar\rho(\Sigma):=\limsup_{k\to\infty}\max_{i_1,\dots,i_k}\rho(A_{i_k}\cdots A_{i_1})^{1/k}$ satisfies $\bar\rho(\Sigma)<1$.

Problem 1. Give necessary and sufficient conditions, checkable by an algorithm, under which a pair of matrices $\{A_1,A_2\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is stable.

Problem 2. Give necessary and sufficient conditions under which a given finite set $\{A_1,\dots,A_m\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is periodically stable, and determine whether this property is algorithmically decidable.

Let $\mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $M_{2\times 2}(\mathbb{N})$ denote the multiplicative monoid of $2\times 2$ matrices with entries in $\mathbb{N}$. Given a finite alphabet $\Sigma = \{a_0,\dots,a_{k-1}\}$, let $\Sigma^+$ denote the free semigroup of nonempty words over $\Sigma$. A homomorphism $\varphi:\Sigma^+ \to M_{2\times 2}(\mathbb{N})$ is called an embedding if it is injective; equivalently, the finite set $X = \{A_0,\dots,A_{k-1}\}\subset M_{2\times 2}(\mathbb{N})$ defined by $A_i = \varphi(a_i)$ is a free generating set of the subsemigroup $X^+$ it generates (no nontrivial relations hold among the $A_i$ under matrix multiplication).

Resolve the following decidability questions:

(1) Is there an algorithm that, given a finite set $X = \{A_0,\dots,A_{k-1}\}\subset M_{2\times 2}(\mathbb{N})$, decides whether $X$ freely generates the semigroup $X^+$ (equivalently, whether the associated morphism $\varphi:\Sigma^+\to M_{2\times 2}(\mathbb{N})$ is an embedding)?

(2) Is there an algorithm that, given two matrices $A, B \in M_{2\times 2}(\mathbb{N})$, decides whether the multiplicative semigroup $\langle A, B\rangle^+$ generated by $\{A,B\}$ is free (i.e.\ whether $\{A,B\}$ is a free generating set)?

The decidability of freeness for multiplicative semigroups of 2×2 matrices over the nonnegative integers remains an open problem. Freeness is known to be undecidable in dimension 3 and above (even for upper-triangular integer matrices), while the 2×2 case over ℕ resists the standard reduction techniques. Recent work (e.g., Ko–Potapov 2017) has partially addressed related freeness problems in SL(2,ℤ), but the general ℕ-valued 2×2 case is still unresolved.

Let $U$ and $V$ be finite-dimensional real vector spaces and let $B : U \times U \to V$ be a symmetric $\mathbb{R}$-bilinear map. Define the associated vector-valued quadratic form $Q_B : U \to V$ by $Q_B(u) = B(u,u)$. For $\lambda \in V^{*}$, let $\lambda Q_B : U \to \mathbb{R}$ denote the scalar quadratic form $u \mapsto \lambda(Q_B(u))$. Say that $B$ is:

- definite if there exists $\lambda \in V^{*}$ such that $\lambda Q_B$ is positive-definite;
- indefinite if for every $\lambda \in V^{*}$ not annihilating $\mathrm{image}(Q_B)$, the scalar form $\lambda Q_B$ is neither positive-semidefinite nor negative-semidefinite.

Assume that $B$ is presented by its components in chosen bases of $U$ and $V$ (a list of symmetric matrices). Resolve the following three computational questions:

(a) Surjectivity. Provide necessary and sufficient conditions, checkable by an algorithm running in time polynomial in the size of the input data $(\dim U,\dim V, B)$, for deciding whether $Q_B : U \to V$ is surjective.

(b) Preimage. Assuming $Q_B$ is surjective, give a polynomial-time algorithm that, on input $v \in V$, returns some $u \in U$ with $Q_B(u) = v$.

(c) Indefiniteness. Provide necessary and sufficient conditions, checkable in polynomial time in the size of $(\dim U,\dim V, B)$, for deciding whether $B$ is indefinite in the sense above.

Recall that a Lie algebra $L$ is nilpotent if its descending central series, defined by $L^{(1)} = L$ and $L^{(k+1)} = [L, L^{(k)}]$, satisfies $L^{(r)} = \{0\}$ for some finite $r$; it is solvable if the derived series, defined by $L_{(1)} = L$ and $L_{(k+1)} = [L_{(k)}, L_{(k)}]$, satisfies $L_{(r)} = \{0\}$ for some finite $r$; and it is finite dimensional if it is finite dimensional as a real vector space.

(a) nilpotent,
(b) solvable,
(c) finite dimensional.

Problem 2. Provide an algorithm which, given the basis $F$, constructs such a basis $G$ when one exists.

Let $G$ be a signal flow graph with nodes $\{1, \dots, n\}$, where each directed edge from node $i$ to node $j$ is labeled by a rational transfer function $T_{ji}(s) = N_{ji}(s)/D_{ji}(s)$, with $N_{ji}$ and $D_{ji}$ coprime polynomials in the indeterminate $s$ (with the convention $N_{ji} = 0$, $D_{ji} = 1$ if no edge from $i$ to $j$ exists). The closed-loop behavior of such an interconnection is determined by the topology of $G$ together with the polynomials $\{N_{ji}, D_{ji}\}_{i,j=1,\dots,n}$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithmic procedure that, given as input any such signal flow graph $G$, returns a polynomial $P_G(s)$ — to be called the "characteristic polynomial" of $G$ — satisfying all of the following properties?

(i) $P_G$ is built as a polynomial expression (using only sums and products) in the polynomials $\{N_{ji}, D_{ji} : i, j = 1, \dots, n\}$, where the form of this expression depends only on the topology of $G$ and not on the particular choice of the polynomials $N_{ji}, D_{ji}$.

(ii) The roots of $P_G$ coincide (with appropriate multiplicities) with the closed-loop poles of the interconnected system represented by $G$, for every admissible assignment of the rational labels $N_{ji}/D_{ji}$.

(iii) When $G$ is a single feedback loop with forward transfer function $N/D$, $P_G$ reduces to the usual closed-loop characteristic polynomial $N + D$ (so that the construction generalizes the classical notion).

Provide such an algorithm, or prove that no such algorithm exists.

Setup. Let $\mathbf{\Delta} \subset \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be a prescribed block-diagonal uncertainty structure, and for a matrix $M \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ let
$$\mu_{\mathbf{\Delta}}(M) \;=\; \frac{1}{\min\{\bar\sigma(\Delta) : \Delta \in \mathbf{\Delta},\ \det(I-M\Delta)=0\}},$$
with $\mu_{\mathbf{\Delta}}(M)=0$ if no such $\Delta$ exists, where $\bar\sigma(\cdot)$ denotes the largest singular value. Fix a probability distribution on the unit ball $\{\Delta \in \mathbf{\Delta} : \bar\sigma(\Delta)\le 1\}$ (e.g.\ the uniform distribution on the corresponding product of balls). For a parameter $g>0$ and integer $S\ge 1$, draw i.i.d.\ samples $\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_S$ from this distribution and form the empirical lower bound
$$\hat\mu_S(M) \;=\; \max_{1\le i\le S}\, g\bigl(\Delta_i, M\bigr),$$
where $g(\Delta,M)$ is a fixed real-valued certificate function satisfying $g(\Delta,M)\le \mu_{\mathbf{\Delta}}(M)$ for every admissible $\Delta$ (so that $\hat\mu_S(M)$ is always a valid lower bound on $\mu_{\mathbf{\Delta}}(M)$).

Problem. Given the integer $n$, the certificate function $g$, and a confidence/accuracy parameter $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, determine the smallest function $S(n,g,\epsilon)$ such that for every $M\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$, drawing $S\ge S(n,g,\epsilon)$ independent samples is sufficient to guarantee
$$\Pr\bigl[\hat\mu_S(M) \;\ge\; \mu_{\mathbf{\Delta}}(M) - \epsilon\bigr] \;\ge\; 1-\epsilon.$$
That is, find the tightest possible sample-complexity lower bound $S(n,g,\epsilon)$ uniform over all $M$.
